project.name: ev204 | WKO-Austria
project.descriptionHtml:
The Innovation Map is an Open Innovation Project, created through collaborative cooperation among national and international experts, universities, and institutions. Our planet is constantly in motion, offering endless streams of opportunities and sources of inspiration. In rhythm with this movement, the Innovation Map continually evolves. We rely on vibrant participation and ongoing development through Open Innovation. Together, we not only actively shape the future but also adapt to it and create new perspectives. With it, we aim to provide a global and dynamic overview of innovations and technologies - staying at the cutting edge. This allows companies to enhance their competitiveness and develop future-proof strategies.

Visit us on www.innovationmap.at

For the past decades, we have noticed that the introduction of technology has accelerated shifts expected to happen later on. Technologies such as the steam engine or the printing press —recognized in economic terms as general-purpose-technologies (GPTs)—, enabled progressive changes that boosted productivity and transformed the relationship society has with, for instance, distances and time, knowledge, and trade. Currently, with digital tools igniting economic, political, social, and environmental developments, an essential part of the equation while introducing technologies is to make sure these are widely adopted.

To drive adoption, investments are required to make emerging technologies part of our daily lives. Let's take Gutenberg's printing press as an example. Its introduction to the publishing industry took a while before being actually adopted, requiring refurbishing and changes before its wide distribution, such as formulating a unique ink recipe, able to affix metal instead of wood. Accordingly, this was only possible because Johanne Fust decided to fund Gutenberg's project in 1450, partnering to produce books, pamphlets, and calendars. Accordingly, the fruitful outcomes of such investment are still witnessed more than 500 years after its invention.

On the same note, investing in emerging technologies, now in the 21st-century, moves in the same direction as Fust's visionary enterprise. Major technology developments involving Artificial Intelligence are driving revolutions in labor, education, environmental, governmental, health, and multiple other industries. In order to explore a complex and dynamic world, followed by the introduction and adoption of technologies, Envisioning developed an analytical tool that determines the impact emerging technologies may produce by the year 2035.

We forecasted 105 underpinning technologies and assessed their maturity level according to NASA’s Technology Readiness Level (TRL) on a scale from 1 (basic principles being tested) to 9 (technology is already being incorporated into our lives). These technologies were categorized according to the UN's Sustainability Development Goals, as an effort to straighten the relationship between technological developments and sustainable practices. Envisioning's interactive visualization allows navigation between technologies, each with a summary and description disclosing their current state of development.

All these technologies were clustered into five different trends; Data Era, Human Expansion, Generate & Drive, AgriTech & Food, and Smart Living. These trends altogether cover WKO's goals of driving innovations to their partners. You are now invited to navigate these technologies and explore the interactive visualization tool that helps trace a path towards a world of 2035.
project.summary: Welcome to 2035. The following interactive visualization tool displays 108 emerging technologies expected to impact main industries by 2035. These technologies were clustered into five different trends, disclosing the main interactions between society, companies, and these technological tools.  You are now invited to navigate our interactive visualization tool and discover an intricate world of tomorrow.

collections.name: Data Era
collections.descriptionHTML: Technologies listed in Data Era are those expected to play a substantial role in virtually any industry. By 2035, data will be interfering in many aspects, from public administration, economics, and law-making, to environmental and personal care factors. Data Era is a cross-cutting trend, intertwined with the other four trends due to its potential of embodying comprehensive tools capable of influencing every inch of this entire world.

collections.name: Human Expansion
collections.descriptionHTML: Technologies listed in Human Expansion combine the potential of synthetic biology with visions of advancing solutions intended to enhance natural organisms. By 2035, the very concept of humanity will shift, leading the global society to explore the edges of life, including aging, novel notions of living beings, and materials that gain autonomy from human manipulation. Human Expansion invites you to travel through future signs of progress in bio and nanotechnology, material science, and robotics.

collections.name: Generate & Drive
collections.descriptionHTML: Technologies listed in Generate & Drive propel innovations in the energy industry, displaying the potential future of power systems. By 2035, with the aim of lowering the human footprint on the environment, novel solutions will drive humanity to discover alternative energy sources that may exceed the boundaries of our own planet, such as harvesting energy directly from the sun. Generate & Drive is the path towards sustainability as an effort to avoid an energetic crisis.

collections.name: Agritech & Food
collections.descriptionHTML: Technologies listed in Agritech & Food drive shifts in food production systems, from tools helping farmers and producers accompany technological innovations to intricate designs that track and monitor crops and the environment as a whole. By 2035, the level of understanding and comprehensiveness of the environment will reach a degree where all scattered units will be interconnected, creating a deeper bond of how humans relate to the food we consume. Agritech & Food presents key emerging technologies that altogether display multiple scenarios of safer, more effective, and environmentally-friendly farming practices.

collections.name: Smart Living
collections.descriptionHTML: Technologies listed in Smart Living reveal how cities are expected to look in the future. These technologies hold the promise to improve urban dynamics and provide to stakeholders, public administrations, and decision-makers the necessary insights to lead the next city-based innovations. By 2035, automation will no longer be a myth but incorporated into daily lives seamlessly through automated vehicles, programmable law-making, and drones circulating above the city. Smart Living is an effort to engage players in decision-making to collect and gather insights that improve the lives of those living in urban settings.

description.shortText: An ethical framework on how human attitudes towards artificial intelligence and robotic beings should be guided from a moral point of view as a means to achieve a balance between both sides.
description.longText:
An ethical framework on how human attitudes towards artificial intelligence and robotic beings should be guided from a moral point of view as a means to achieve a balance. This ethical framework would determine the programming limits of AI, what should be allowed, and what uses should be universally forbidden. As it seems artificial intelligent beings are expected to unfold autonomously, ethical values such as responsibility, transparency, accountability, and incorruptibility should be depicted as an algorithm and programmed into their system to work accordingly. As soon as artificial beings acquire a certain level of autonomy, this set of ethical configurations would help machines understand how human society works and possibly integrate them as an extension of the humankind. 

However, to build this ethical and moral code, humans first need to establish a single set of ethical regulations for themselves before anticipating one fit for robots. Human ethics are heterogeneous, highly dependent on cultural and social attributes, besides other layers, including emotions, languages, and political beliefs. Machines work, by definition, through criteria and logical rules, yet, worldwide ethical behavior is blurry, sometimes full of exceptions that transcend the very same limit of human existence. Humans need to reinvent their upright basis and then ascertain a new language and formula to fit these artificial beings inside the human world. 

Many ethical debates are likely to pop up as soon as machines acquire their own consciousness or when robots become sentient. Questions should be employed such as until what extent humans should treat artificially intelligent agents merely as tools, or if machines would be able or not to gain the sufficient power to some day confront humankind. In front of this quandary, it is possible that an ideal ethical measurement would only come after years of human-machine interactions.

As humans interact with machines, the resulting metrics would give insights to sharpen the way this introduction should be made. For instance, from a young age, children could learn how to behave and treat robots while in school. Adults and late adopters, on the other hand, could be taught how to act and behave with specific training courses and educational material. By analyzing these outputs, it is expected that humans would be able to develop affinities and create a more symbiotic acquaintance for both humans and robots. However, another matter to keep in mind would be the possible future creation of a hierarchy system between artificial and organic beings.

# Future Perspectives

With the increasing trend of humanizing artificial intelligence by enhancing conversational skills or by embodying it in humanoid robots, it is both the uncanny valley concept and the ethics of human-machine interaction that arise as areas of concern for further evaluation. Science fiction has been exploring these relationships for more than a hundred years, considering that robots have been mostly used as metaphors for the externalization of problems faced among individuals of the humankind. 

On the other hand, when actually dealing with machines that still reproduce many human aspects, it is the conflict between similarities and differences that require a more complex approach for the future of robotics and artificial intelligence. In the coming decades, people may have relationships with more sophisticated robots, which could lead to new forms of emotions that could complement and enhance human relationships. However, it is imperative to anticipate and discourage scenarios in which relationships could become socially destructive. The key question is not whether humans could prevent this from happening or not, but rather, what sort of human-robot relationships should be tolerated and encouraged.

*Photo / Illustration: © kentoh / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Modified plant species, with more reflective leaves, used to increase the albedo-effect to cool down temperatures in certain areas.
description.longText:
Enhancing localized albedo (surface reflectivity) is a technique used in regional climate change adaptation in urban and agricultural settings. By increasing surface reflectivity of crops, solar radiation absorption is reduced, which in turn partially neutralizes the local warming effects of increased atmospheric greenhouse gas concentrations while also conserving water resources and improving public health. 

Biologists and engineers have considered a variety of techniques to implement an albedo enhancing strategy in farms. These approaches range from the simple selection of specific strains of crops to manipulating crops with traditional breeding techniques or genetically modifying certain species to provide for a better albedo-effect. Approaches include adjusting leaves waxiness, leaf canopy structure, or genetically changing plants’ hairs, cuticles, or glaucousness. 

These techniques could reduce heat in the plants and soil, leading to less evaporative losses and water stress. Studies estimate that crop albedo could be increased by as much as a third without reducing plant productivity. Also, by lowering temperatures in the farms, previously lost hours of labor due to dangerously high temperatures could be reduced.

# Future Perspectives
More reflective crops could control the climate in a particular region, helping counteract the adverse effects of warmer temperatures. One could imagine the emergence of auxiliary plantations, farms with the sole purpose of fighting climate change, and enhancing the productivity of other conventional crops.

While this could be a way of reducing global warming or modifying regional climate, little is known today about the effects of increased reflectivity on the ecosystem. A plant's nutritional capabilities, photosynthesis, soil quality, and animal life could be indirectly affected, creating new kinds of problems.

*Photo/Illustration: pavlobaliukh / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A set of algorithms that analyzes data gathered from personal devices to deeply understand the behavior patterns of an individual. It examines the political standing of the individual and automatically selects the candidate who will best serve their needs.
description.longText:
Deep learning algorithms which compare an individual's behavior patterns to the available political voting choices and select the candidate who will best serve their personal needs. Complex data cross-checking algorithms gather data from personal devices to access all available information about someone, from biometric analytics to online and offline behavior, to gain insights about the desires of each individual and provide comprehensive, tailored guidance on voting. 

Providing political and overall guidance based on society's routine choices raises ethical and moral questions that need to be addressed before this technology is deployed, such as either prohibiting this technological solution even to exist or merely imposing some functioning limitations. Otherwise, personal decisions are at peril, and the free will of an individual could be questioned. 

Yet as science progresses, scientific theories suggest that emotions are nothing more than biochemical data-processing algorithms. It means that all human experiences are the result of electrical brain activity, and the whole concept of free will loses relevance. If such theories become the norm, it might be easier to hand authority over to data processors, as they would be able to understand what is genuinely best for each person. 

# Future Perspectives

Such an immense amount of sensitive data raises fundamental questions about who ultimately has access to it. As Extended Reality evolves, for instance, lives, preferences, and relationships become even more digitized, and therefore, measurable and potentially more surveilled. With wearable and mobile devices alongside the presence of AI home assistants, machines might know us better than ever before through multiple sensors. Strong regulations and privacy measures must be implemented at every developmental stage of data gathering and processing systems to avoid possible biases within the cross-checking algorithmic process of automatic voting.

In a world where fake news is omnipresent, politicians may be confronted with situations in which they will have to convince the algorithms that their campaigns are genuine. Such a degree of automation could help increase democracy levels and assist people in pressuring candidates to maintain democratic practices while handling more accurate and specific information.

*Photo / Illustration: © MicroOne / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A method that utilizes enzymes to break down sugar molecules and use them as a means to produce hydrogen fuel for vehicles. It is virtually as energy-efficient as traditional methods of extracting fuel from organic materials, and transforms vast amounts of agricultural waste products into energy.
description.longText:
A cost-effective method of producing hydrogen from biomass to generate fuel. The process utilizes enzymes to break down complex sugar molecules, primarily glucose and xylose, and turn them into hydrogen. It is virtually as energy-efficient as the traditional methods of extracting fuel from organic materials, and could transform vast amounts of agricultural waste products into fuel.

In order to safely and adequately store hydrogen fuel, the process could be carried out through electrolysis, where particles of oxygen and hydrogen are separated, and the latter can be blended with natural gas in an existing grid or stored separately in hydrogen fuel vessels. As wastewater treatment facilities look into generating energy as a value-added co-product, particularly where Microbial Electrolysis Cell technology is utilized, on-site hydrogen storage could become an essential and relevant consideration.

The defense and industrial sectors would benefit most from this application, as quick, low-noise vehicles that do not emit exhaust fumes offer a potential substitute for current operational vehicles. Urban mobility could also benefit from this technology. By only generating small amounts of heat and water, hydrogen fuel vehicles could cut down on pollution emissions, becoming an alternative to diesel-electric systems. Economically, this could end up being a more expensive option — especially for trains, which would require significant railway track modifications. However, with the falling costs of hydrogen fuel and batteries, the prices could potentially compete with diesel-electric vehicles.

# Future Perspectives

Hydrogen technologies still face significant uphill challenges in order to meet expectations regarding viability. Yet, current research suggests that these methods and techniques can provide answers to the decarbonization of global energy systems, thus incentivizing the proper deployment of this technology. Interest in this method is rising, following the conditional promise that hydrogen is well-established in particular niches, such as forklifts. This functionality provides a ray of hope that forthcoming solutions could replicate these systems, become mainstream, and also be applied to other industries.

*Photo/Illustration: By DedMityay / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Three-dimensional objects, virtually projected in ways their design is shaped and felt by human touch. By creating an intuitive way of editing objects digitally, designers, architects, and engineers could use this technology for rapid prototyping and validation.
description.longText:
A tactile feedback system, powered by ultrasonic radiation pressure that enables humans to touch 3D digital images. Holograms release the visual inputs, and the physical experience is programmed through software using haptics. The user can sense the hologram because the air disturbances caused by ultrasound vibration provide sensory stimuli to human skin nerves.  

The visual projection occurs when a display produces 3D images by illuminating a tiny floating plastic bead, levitated by ultrasound in free space. The bead is moved at considerable speed, suspended in the air, creating 3D shapes that can be physically sensed. The disturbances caused by ultrasound waves are produced by an array of speakers positioned around the tiny bead, which allows tactile experiences.

# Future Perspectives 

Also known as acoustic trap displays, these holograms may play a critical role in all industries by creating malleable digital models' representations. Digital files could be sent online and then projected into holograms to be simulated and change shape by human touch. By creating an intuitive way of editing objects digitally, designers, architects, and engineers could use this technology for rapid prototyping and validation through a simulation model that could be tactile sensitive, working along with remote teams on product development.

By providing a shared experience of an object, this technology could avoid unnecessary travel and shipping. The user could download and experience the fabric's texture before buying a piece of clothing or trying an object in their home. 

Ultimately, instead of merely enhancing reality, this technology could enable the creation of entire virtual environments. Virtually created museums, classrooms, or bars could entertain and educate people, filled with distinct or even impossible inputs, such as extinct animals, foreign plants, or entire cities, enabling a more dynamic or alternative view of educational content. People could live inside their favorite shows or academic settings, and amusement parks with all inputs necessary to provide a fully immersive space. 

*photo/illustration: © jamesteohart / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Decentralized and encrypted protocols designed to improve the efficiency and security of digital health data, enabling data interoperability across different data points and enhancing the overall exchange of information and knowledge in a secure and tamper-proof manner.
description.longText:
A decentralized and encrypted method of distributing, sharing, and storing digital healthcare files. Cryptocurrencies and smart contracts, present in the blockchain, facilitate financial transactions and provide a solution to secure data in an encrypted ledger. 

Instead of a centrally located database to manage all medical information, in the healthcare blockchain system, medical records are shared among a decentralized network of verified nodes. Users, including doctors, nurses, and patients, can access files and add new data autonomously. 

Doctors and medical providers benefit from this technological solution by having more access to crucial medical data, besides sharing their findings across all users. By using industry standards related to APIs, this protocol improves data interoperability across different data points, such as continents and nations, thus enhancing the exchange of information and knowledge. 

# Future Perspectives

Medical datasets are a valuable asset, generally managed by private companies and institutions. By decentralizing and distributing knowledge across several nodes in the chain, healthcare data can become more accessible for all those implicated, such as patients and doctors located in areas that lack access to quality information. 

AI systems assisting the healthcare sector are gaining traction, meaning that the exchange of sensitive data increases exponentially. In order to preserve the integrity of the data exchanged, blockchain applications could ensure a reliable development of AI software, as well as improve the exchange of patient information more safely.

*Photo/Illustration: denisismagilov / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A manipulation mechanism of gene expressions in plants to improve crop yields and stress tolerance without making changes to the DNA sequence of a plant.
description.longText:
The study and application of how and when genes are expressed in crops, under the influence of mostly external factors. Different from animals, plants are stationary and, consequently, more vulnerable to environmental stresses such as high temperature, drought, pathogens, parasites, and poor soil conditions. In general, those stressors tend to suppress the development and growth of plants, damaging their DNA.

By considering genetic variations as well as epigenetic phenomena that influence the gene expression of plants, studying the process of how genes respond to the environment is becoming an important subject in the scientific community. Therefore, without making any changes to the DNA sequence of the plant, but still understanding how genes are expressed, crop epigenetics is an innovative field that promises to improve crop yields and stress tolerance.

Over the last few years, studies have contributed to a better understanding of the underlying epigenetic mechanisms for important heritable crop traits in tomatoes, such as ripening and stress response. Also, epigenetic mechanisms have been associated with transgressive segregation in hybrids generated from crosses between cultivated tomatoes and their close wild relatives. More recently, scientists have been working on the development of DNA damage response systems to ensure optimal growth and survival of plants despite the condition to which they are exposed, such as poor environmental circumstances.

By using techniques such as co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry, researchers discovered an epigenetic regulation mechanism involved in DNA damage repair in plants, which lies in a histone demethylase enzyme called lysine-specific demethylase 1-like 1 (LDL1) combined with a conserved protein called RAD54. The approach silences specific genes to remove the cell’s “epigenetic memory,” thus creating an intermediate parcel of pluripotent callus cells. Then, different genes are stimulated in the cells supporting the callus transmutation into an infant tissue made up of totally different cell types. 

This regenerative process leads to shooting induction, which ultimately leads to the formation of stems and leaves. Moreover, an essential finding on this epigenetic mechanism is that these new stems and leaves do not require seeds to grow. These approaches help shed light on the possibility of increasing the productivity of staple grains and vegetable crops in a more environmentally friendly way.

# Future Perspectives

In the future, epigenetic technology could be applied to function as biomarkers concerning exposure to specific stressors or toxic outcomes in crop variations. It could be used to monitor biotechnological systems and provide early warnings regarding the potential risk to ecosystems. Epigenetic mechanisms may generate explanations for unresolved observations in the domain of ecotoxicology, thus creating a more sustainable and natural device to monitor agriculture and thereby improve food security.  

It is expected that this field will become more widely regulated but also undergo an expansion to take it beyond agricultural efficiency. Commercial applications could become a resource in helping forests recover as well as other vegetation damaged due to pollution, exploitation, or natural disasters.

By using techniques such as co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry, researchers discovered an epigenetic regulation mechanism involved in DNA damage repair in plants, which lies in a histone demethylase enzyme called lysine-specific demethylase 1-like 1 (LDL1) combined with a conserved protein called RAD54. The approach silences specific genes to remove the cell’s “epigenetic memory,” thus creating an intermediate parcel of pluripotent callus cells. Then, different genes are stimulated in the cells supporting the callus transmutation into an infant tissue made up of totally different cell types.

This regenerative process leads to shooting induction, which ultimately leads to the formation of stems and leaves. Moreover, an essential finding on this epigenetic mechanism is that these new stems and leaves do not require seeds to grow. These approaches help shed light on the possibility of increasing the productivity of staple grains and vegetable crops in a more environmentally friendly way.

Future Perspectives

In the future, epigenetic technology could be applied to function as biomarkers concerning exposure to specific stressors or toxic outcomes in crop variations. It could be used to monitor biotechnological systems and provide early warnings regarding the potential risk to ecosystems. Epigenetic mechanisms may generate explanations for unresolved observations in the domain of ecotoxicology, thus creating a more sustainable and natural device to monitor agriculture and thereby improve food security.

It is expected that this field will become more widely regulated but also undergo an expansion to take it beyond agricultural efficiency. Commercial applications could become a resource in helping forests recover as well as other vegetation damaged due to pollution, exploitation, or natural disasters.

description.shortText: By using quantum dynamics and ultra-cold atoms as an alternative to GPS updates, this method can suggest the best course of action in order to reduce travel times and provide a more accurate estimated time of arrival without the need for satellites.
description.longText:
An instrument which measures relative position using the technique of atom interferometry. A quantum compass is an alternative to, or potentially considered as the further evolution of, the current GPS. Most current navigation systems depend on a Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), such as the Global Positioning System, a satellite-based navigation which triangulates signals sent and received from satellites orbiting the Earth. Advancements in quantum dynamics theory, especially in atomic physics, enabled the development of high-precision atomic accelerometers and gyroscopes, providing the basis for developing a faster and more precise navigation system. This software would use predictive analytics and machine learning algorithms to optimize routes and reduce operational expenses.

Quantum compasses could be integrated into a system that would analyze the position, heading, destination, and speed of a device to provide the operator with the suggested best course of action, and in turn, help reduce travel times and more accurately predict the time of arrival. This technology could also be used for vessels and ships to recommend a more suitable course or provide pinpoint accuracy for aircraft, drones, or even the geographic location of troops. As technological developments in miniaturization continue to show promising results, this technology could be increasingly useful inside smartphones and other portable devices.

# Future Perspectives

Traditional GPS can be susceptible to signal jamming or blockages; furthermore, it is estimated that just one day of complete satellite blockage would cost the UK alone more than £1 billion. These risks show the increasing importance of developing alternative navigation systems. 

With the expectation that autonomous vehicles gain popularity in the coming years, these systems would also become a standard feature in the delivery sector, enabling delivery companies to provide more precise information to customers. An integrated, complex decision-making and monitoring system will play an essential role in helping cities adapt to these self-driving vehicles by improving traffic management and energy-use efficiency.

description.shortText: Blockchain-based tracking mechanism to monitor the origin source of physical assets and certificate economic, business, trading, and manufacturing practices across the global supply chain.
description.longText:
A blockchain method designed to monitor, register, and guarantee the precedence of various goods throughout the supply chain, restoring economic trust cycles and promoting new sources of value for companies that seek to be recognized as sustainable and ethical brands. The direct monitoring or backward tracking of physical assets occurs at multiple points of the supply chain using sensors and IoT devices installed at every checkpoint. 

The constant tracking of assets can help ensure product provenance in a wide range of commodities such as diamonds, leather, pharmaceutical, helping prevent counterfeits and environmentally damaging products. The main benefit of relying on this technology is to improve the credibility of the origin certificates. For that, each asset is inscribed with an immutable serial number, linking to tamper-proof transaction history. 

# Future Perspectives

With this technology, retailers may have a real option to segment the market between responsible and non-responsible suppliers and certify as many goods as possible. Yet, blockchain may raise the cost of market segmentation, and retailers may decide to modify their certification strategy to a cheaper alternative source, which has higher rates of having non-responsible and sustainable practices.  In order to maintain a fine balance, more specific policies at the international level are required.

description.shortText: An automated production unit connected to a network for cultivating, manipulating and regenerating stem cells.
description.longText:
Automated stem cell laboratories which provide the next level of production automation, allowing the control and automation of very complex and sensitive cell manipulation processes, such as those in related to biotechnological stem cell experiments and the production of other biomaterials to cultivate biological tissues, in order to increase efficiency and reduce the costs associated with the reproduction of such experiments. Devices in such an automated laboratory are connected to a network where each one constantly acquires and analyzes real-time data in order to react with a pre-determined adaptive robotic response that is suitable for the changing environment.

The ongoing processes could be also controlled manually by the users, even though each data output from the experiments is automatically gathered and uploaded to the cloud. The outputs of the experiments serve as an input for the bioengineering industry for various processes, including cloning or even the production of laboratory-grown beef. Moreover, automated factories can be applied to produce complex ingredients, such as bovine serum albumin by integrating cGMP principles in these factories, allowing full traceability, process stability, and sustainability. 

As the cultivation of embryonic cells in an automated laboratory environment allow for larger production scales through the automation of the processes, and the expansion of the process could include the production of biological tissues made out of those cells, these factories can contribute to the manufacturing of complex cell-based products, including organs, in-vitro meat, or self-grown textiles. Moreover, they can serve as an important technology for cellular therapies in regenerative medicine due to the self-renewal abilities of the used stem cells.

# Future Perspectives

This technology applied to scaleable cultured meat development has the potential to disrupt the meat industry, one of the biggest contributors to humanity’s environmental footprint. Furthermore, it can contribute to the wide-spread application of advanced stem cell therapies capable of regenerating human tissues damaged by injuries, diseases, or aging. This will not only allow for enhanced skin rejuvenation but also the rejuvenation of internal organs, having a holistic impact on the human body, facilitating the shift to transform current treatment approaches towards regenerative medicine and beauty.

description.shortText: A silicon-based solution that can retain approximately 1MW of thermal energy per cubic meter, which can be stored and then harvested by tapping into the bright light it emits.
description.longText:
As a means to store energy, this thermal storage solution works by heating the silicon contained inside tanks, with the aid of renewable energy or a surplus of electricity from the grid. The material can retain approximately 1 MW of energy per cubic meter, which can be stored until needed and then harvested by tapping into the bright light it emits. 

The system is built with two heavily-insulated tanks. One tank stores the liquid silicon at a relatively "cool" temperature of 1,900° C. To heat it up, the silicon is pumped out of that tank through tubes exposed to heating elements that are powered by external energy sources (ideally from renewable resources). The warmer silicon then passes into the second tank, which stores it at a much hotter temperature of about 2,400° C.

When harvesting that energy, the system taps into the light — at those temperatures, molten silicon shines exceptionally brightly. The white-hot liquid is pumped through tubes that emit the brightness of the material, which is then captured by specialized solar cells known as multijunction photovoltaics and converted to electricity. The silicon, now cooling down again, is pumped back into the first tank to start the cycle over. 

# Future Perspectives
Silicon, the earth's second most abundant material, can be cheaply mined and manipulated. However, this solution is still not suitable for mobile use, and its price is outside of range for a domestic installation, mainstream adoption is unlikely to happen, thus making it more adequate for large-scale power-plants. Due to its complexity, currently, such a system could be accessible only to centralized players, possibly concentrating even more power in the energy industry.

description.shortText: A contactless human-computer interface that captures and interprets human gestures as commands in real-time through wearables, cameras, sensors, ultrasound signals, or near-infrared imagery.
description.longText:
Coupled with XR devices, this technological solution provides immersive, seamless, and natural digital content interaction to users. It is commonly employed to read hand and head gestures but could one day evolve to detect other body parts. This technology will be a crucial component to merge digital layers of information on the physical environment, enabling interaction with the digital and physical world intuitively.   

There are several ways to enable gesture tracking. The most popular utilizes hand or finger wearables with movement sensors or external trackers that detect hand and finger motions as an input. With the development and ubiquity of machine vision in smartphone cameras, it could also reach standard cameras equipped with AI and vision-based algorithms that sense and classify dynamic hand gestures in real-time. Technologies such as near-infrared imagery and ultrasound detection systems could help improve accuracy if mounted on smart devices. It would help detect the motion sent through the air from the speakers already integrated into a smartphone or tablet, for instance. 

In addition to giving commands to a computer, gesture tracking could authenticate individuals or validate transactions. In VR environments, it could translate gestures into a user's avatars and improve immersion and productivity with a new kind of interface. Currently, gesture tracking is being implemented in the automobile industry, as smart cars can read gestures to control music, decline calls, and other commands.  

# Future Perspectives

In a post-pandemic world, this technology could become the new norm as a means to interact with devices around us without touching surfaces. It could even make pointers and keyboards obsolete if paired with voice and facial recognition systems. As more advanced AI algorithms help machines understand complex human gestures, it could raise privacy concerns. Body language could quickly tell a trained computer how an individual feels and automatically store this information without the user's authorization.

description.shortText: Software powered by machine learning that combines technical knowledge with judiciary systems to detect, identify, and predict illicit activities and audit public accounts and assets, including cryptocurrencies.
description.longText:
Automated compliance software combines technical knowledge with judiciary systems to detect and prevent criminal activity through the social management of public administration. Embedded with machine learning, it would help identify illicit activity and audit public accounts and assets, including cryptocurrencies.

By combing through millions of transactions within public and private data, algorithms could identify expenditures or illegal operations, bringing sweeping changes to the financial and regulatory landscapes. The immense amount of data processing and pattern recognition achievable through machine learning has the potential to red flag corruption schemes and hold governments accountable like never before. Besides, this automated panorama could mean the improvement of many aspects of government-related functions such as legal research, outcome prediction, contract review, and fraud detection. 

Government agencies, institutions, and companies could make these audits public, aiding anyone who may want to investigate or help create more regulatory processes. In this sense, social media plays a key role in keeping citizens abreast of posts that expose dishonesty. Therefore, the population would be able to mobilize and lodge complaints en masse, and maybe even put pressure on public agencies to obligate the use of automated compliance methods across all systems.

# Future Perspectives

Although the topic of sustainability is gaining increasing political, social, and economic significance, current business practices are adapting slowly, partly due to the ever-growing number of regulations, norms, and certifications. Automated solutions could help with enforcement but also allow organizations to self-monitor more effectively. The limited spread of software and standardized exchange formats for environmental data constitute a significant obstacle to this process. Determining how best to codify environmental regulations is an area of active research that could be expanded upon using blockchain technology with the help of smart contracts.

The automation of compliance could change the whole regulatory landscape, making it almost impossible to fake expenditures. As audits become public, compliance also transforms into a social phenomenon and ceases to be an "agency-exclusive" issue. Anyone would be able to create a bot to audit the government or companies; the source code would be open for public use and more accessible to the general population, which in turn could endanger privacy and the right to secrecy of citizens. At the same time, transparency and data sharing would serve society as a whole. Also, the pressure could force public services to go digital, making the government rush to turn all their information into a machine-readable format. In a smart future, with the appliance of deep-learning techniques, such as artificial neural networks, systems might be able to predict intention and read politicians' behavior, thus avoiding political crimes committed against the population.

description.shortText: A leather-like material made of controlled fungus colonies. The fungi release a polymer-like structure similar to leather, with durable and water-repellent properties.
description.longText:
Fungi-based materials are organic, self-grown, water repellent, and antibacterial. The fungi grow by feeding on decomposing plants and vegetables, meaning they could be fed by agricultural waste or urban organic composts. 

The fungi growth is exponential. It can take two months for a newly started colony to reach the size of a cow-like piece of leather and some weeks to get the size of a small object. After reaching the desired size, the fungi is harvested, and the material is heated to eliminate all remaining fungal organisms and halt the growth. The result is a dry, flexible material, available to be shaped into manifold desired forms.

By manipulating room temperature, lighting, and atmospheric gases, it is possible to control the growth of the material to achieve a specific texture and density. Fungi-based material is carbon-negative, fully biodegradable, and the leftovers are beneficial to the earth, which can be used for composting, thus closing the loop.

# Future Perspectives

Fungi-grown materials point to an environmentally friendly approach to producing objects in general. While there are notorious problems in developing such products on a large scale, their development into the mainstream market could point to a radical change in the supply and production chains.

It could also, because of the nature of the material, give rise to challenges for developing cleaning systems. Both the chemicals and the machines used to clean could radically change or even become obsolete since this material is still unknown on how to clean; researchers believe it would not be needed. 

Another crucial point is to consider how expensive it will be. For this to impact the market equally, its price must be accessible and able to reach the overall market. Accordingly, trademarks interested in using this material must consider the value it will have to the final consumer and how the supply chain market will be affected when deployed.

description.shortText: A digital storage that enables users to access their own memory accurately, akin to a "live cloud," with memories registered through their eyes and then recalled and streamed in video format.
description.longText:
Digital storage for memories, captured by a nano camera that features zoom functionality, image-quality enhancement and video playback, is coupled with the eyeball, allowing users to continually record everything that their eyes could see. Even when the user is not actively focusing on something, the system would subsequently send the recorded material to a cloud storage service. 

The cloud storage could be accessible to the image owner as well as anyone with permission. With the help of machine vision and image recognition, the memory could be instantly identified and tagged while being stored. Specific events could be searched for using simple keywords and grouped according to the theme. Advances in natural language processing would be essential to allow fast searching throughout memories. 

By using such technology, humans would have another layer of information that tracks their activities continuously.  With images recorded and stored, it could be used as irrefutable proof in court, thus helping to solve cases objectively. In day-to-day routines, it could help discover allergic reactions or infection causes.  Editing, gathering, and streaming users' memories outside the brain could suggest a future where the very concept of identity would be enhanced. 

# Future Perspectives

With the help of energy-efficient, highly optimized storage methods, like DNA digital-data storage, it could be possible to create an archive of all of humankind's memories. Having access to all the generated memories of an individual, might give users the ability to understand both their minds and themselves better, being especially useful in therapy when dealing with traumatic situations or a distorted self-image. 

This device could also be particularly helpful as a way to alleviate symptoms in cases of dementia and Alzheimer's disease, making memories instantly accessible when the patient is unable to recall them otherwise. Furthermore, an all-time easily accessible lifelog could eventually end up taking the place of natural human memory. Users could grow accustomed to searching for digital entries on a specific subject, before even trying to remember it, and the very process of recalling would be transformed. But, some may say that there are probably biological advantages in forgetting; what would interpersonal relationships look like in a world where nothing is ever forgotten?

description.shortText: A software mounted on a wearable EEG programmed to generate audiovisual lifelogging entries, commonly presented in the form of XR glasses.
description.longText:
The digitalization and archive of a person's own experience, also known as lifelogging, is becoming ever more popular. As XR glasses grow in acceptance, so are some attempts to create a constant recording device that would store every detail of a person’s life in the form of audiovisual content. 

Even though it sounds exciting and appealing, this technology has some limitations. First, the creation of videos requires a considerable amount of energy, and it loses significant quality when stored in small formats. Some argue that most of our lived moments are somewhat irrelevant and not worthy of revisiting, which is one of the reasons this software is expected to fall into discredit soon enough. 

Yet, to make the lifelog process more efficient and meaningful, an EEG brainwave modulator could be connected to XR glasses. In this device, the camera would be triggered according to the user's change of emotional state, thus ensuring that only significant moments are recorded; the EEG would be trained to recognize the user’s emotional patterns. After the calibration and setup, it would be possible to trigger audio or video recording every time the user feels any emotion, such as fear, frustration, satisfaction, pleasure, and happiness. After the memory is recorded, it is labeled and tagged, according to emotional states, GPS location, date and time metadata, and then stashed in cloud storage. 

# Future Perspectives

As XR devices are getting ever more popular, emotional measurements will likely become embedded in their architecture. Once the energy consumption and storage challenges are solved, we can imagine a world in which all and every experience lived by a person is recorded and labeled according to a multitude of sensors, including, but not restricted to, emotion measurements. In this scenario, lying and deceiving would be impossible, as once not only a person's every lived moment could be verifiable, but also their feelings.

Correlating memories with emotional states could be a useful practice to recognize positive and negative patterns in a person's life. For instance, if most of the memories containing a specific friend are tagged with an unpleasant emotion, it might be a good idea to rethink this relationship altogether.

*Photo / Illustration: ©  Christos Georghiou / adobe.stock.com*
description.longTextHtml:
The digitalization and archive of a person's own experience, also known as lifelogging, is becoming ever more popular. As XR glasses grow in acceptance, so are some attempts to create a constant recording device that would store every detail of a person’s life in the form of audiovisual content.

Even though it sounds exciting and appealing, this technology has some limitations. First, the creation of videos requires a considerable amount of energy, and it loses significant quality when stored in small formats. Some argue that most of our lived moments are somewhat irrelevant and not worthy of revisiting, which is one of the reasons this software is expected to fall into discredit soon enough.

Yet, to make the lifelog process more efficient and meaningful, an EEG brainwave modulator could be connected to XR glasses. In this device, the camera would be triggered according to the user's change of emotional state, thus ensuring that only significant moments are recorded; the EEG would be trained to recognize the user’s emotional patterns. After the calibration and setup, it would be possible to trigger audio or video recording every time the user feels any emotion, such as fear, frustration, satisfaction, pleasure, and happiness. After the memory is recorded, it is labeled and tagged, according to emotional states, GPS location, date and time metadata, and then stashed in cloud storage.

Future Perspectives

As XR devices are getting ever more popular, emotional measurements will likely become embedded in their architecture. Once the energy consumption and storage challenges are solved, we can imagine a world in which all and every experience lived by a person is recorded and labeled according to a multitude of sensors, including, but not restricted to, emotion measurements. In this scenario, lying and deceiving would be impossible, as once not only a person's every lived moment could be verifiable, but also their feelings.

Correlating memories with emotional states could be a useful practice to recognize positive and negative patterns in a person's life. For instance, if most of the memories containing a specific friend are tagged with an unpleasant emotion, it might be a good idea to rethink this relationship altogether.

description.shortText: Chamas are informal community-based micro-finance groups designed to extend the financial assistance to economically vulnerable social groups. As it is based on the blockchain, this service provides accountability, security, and reduces fraud.
description.longText:
Unlike banks, Chamas are informal social savings groups that allow members to contribute a certain amount of money monthly, take loans at low-interest rates, earn dividends, and make investments. Initially used by women, Chamas started to grow in success and popularity, and men began to participate as well. These community-based micro-finance groups represent a powerful working example of decentralized mutual aid, and their promotion could lead to significant improvements in extending financial assistance to economically vulnerable social groups, by improving household business outcomes.

Given the informality, the main challenge lies in a flawed paper-based record-keeping system, where records are susceptible to possible loss, misplacement, and duplication. Advances in financial and communication technologies, digital IDs, mobile money, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and blockchain technology, are creating enough infrastructure to promote these informal savings groups while extending access to more substantial portions of the population, ensuring accountability, enhancing security and reducing fraud.

Built on these technologies, new types of open-sourced apps designed around current structures of Chamas could allow users to apply for and receive micro-loans within seconds, when and where needed. Furthermore, a sophisticated community-based identity system could remove the need for a centralized credit bureau and could be based on the real-world social network of users, including friends, family, neighbors, and business partners. By digitizing bookkeeping on the blockchain and implementing endorsements, guarantees, and arbitration through social networks, transparency increases, and members could view the treasurer’s account, including monetary transactions and the amount of money spent.

# Future Perspectives
Blockchain-based Chamas promise to increase transparency and provide faster micro-financing for people who desperately need the money. Chamas have the potential to proliferate and scale to unprecedented levels by leveraging technology that allows them to do what they do best. Since they do not depend on government assistance, these technologies are especially relevant in regions of social instability, poverty, and political conflicts.

description.shortText: By tracking consumption patterns through embedded sensors or blockchain nodes, connected appliances use algorithms to monitor and calculate operational needs.
description.longText:
A cloud-based system connects the supply chain and delivers end-to-end supply chain visibility and streamlined business operations, taking over responsibility for many logistical and transaction-based tasks. It manages internal and external assets and processes — such as container inventory, documents, data tracking and storage, and yard capacity — using an immutable, secure, and transparent shared network. For instance, a machine could schedule a maintenance check when it detects a certain probability of (ab)normal wear and tear. The tracked information could include any relevant data regarding logistics matters or even the temperature or composition of goods. Furthermore, each participant could view the progress of goods through the supply chain, quickly discovering the location of products in transit. 

By connecting the asset itself to the blockchain through the Internet of Things, it could provide any given machine or product the ability to automatically feed the network with status updates while comparing it with collected data on consumption habits. From voice assistants to energy meters and self-driving cars, it would store tracked data from any transaction between people and companies, making the data trackable and immutable. However, sensitive and personal information is eternally stored using cloud-based services, which creates a precedent for user (non-)ownership, thus restricting the popularity and full adoption.

To ensure safety while carrying out transactions, the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires companies to delete client data once it has served its purpose. This recently implemented law clashes with blockchain consistency, in which the data cannot be changed or removed once stored. To solve this paradox, protocols that operate on top of the blockchain are being created, giving people back total control over their data, while maintaining blockchain consistency. This mutable blockchain allows users to delete their data from the chain while storing it privately. The nodes on the blockchain keep their hash number and thus continue to be viable for future use, to resolve disputes (as long as the user continues to maintain their data connected to the node hash number). 

# Future Perspectives

With improved control, this technological solution could enhance food and drink authenticity and traceability. With advancements in big data and the Internet-of-Things, it could represent an opportunity to develop blockchain solutions for agri-food systems.

Additionally, trade is typically detrimental to sustainability, increasingly taking more than it gives from natural resources. The impact is most prominent in port terminals, more than any other business environment. Ports need to deal with water and air pollution, solid-waste management, contamination issues, and maintain active fuel spillage contingency plans. By strengthening the connection between real and virtual assets, improving audits, and enforcing sustainability goals, this cloud-based logistics system could prove to be quite useful in situations that require precise and connected services.

*Photo/Illustration: scharfsinn86 / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Robots powered by machine learning and machine vision, designed to monitor and assist the elderly and people with disabilities in performing daily tasks.
description.longText:
Robots, powered by machine learning and machine vision, designed to monitor and assist the elderly and people with disabilities while undertaking daily tasks. The robots are pre-programmed with a set of algorithms that learn and adapt their actions according to the specific needs of each patient, providing tailored services that are developed by understanding gestures, verbal, and non-verbal cues.

The deployment of machine learning technology enables the robot to estimate human poses and expressions. By learning behavior patterns, robots improve activity suggestions based on each individual. Services include providing all-inclusive care from bed to wheelchair by doing the heavy lifting, assisting with bathroom needs, preparing and serving meals, and dispensing medication. Apart from these applications, these robots can help suppress emotional needs by providing companionship, assisting therapists in further treatments such as depression, phobia, and post-traumatic disorders. 

# Future Perspectives

The deployment of automated robots in the healthcare sector is increasing exponentially. Currently, robots still perform limited tasks and are not able to conduct high demanding activities that require more attention and meticulous care. 

Yet, as AI-based systems are gaining traction and evolving at unprecedented speeds, the likelihood of substituting medical staff with robot caregivers raises proportionally. By automating the healthcare sector, it can either allocate the current personnel to more specialized tasks, such as research and monitoring, but also provoke massive lay-offs and employment crises. To avoid such a scenario, governments and institutions should create policies and training practices in advance. 

*Photo/Illustration: M.Dörr & M.Frommherz / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: An automated flying aid unit mounted with a defibrillator and other life-saving devices, designed to reduce the amount of waiting time for victims and increase their chance of survival.
description.longText:
A drone used to carry medical equipment to speed up the time of rescue and treatment, while also saving resources and fuel with transportation. A GPS guides the drone to the coordinates where a device is providing the current emergency location, thus supplying the necessary support in just a few minutes.

There are many possible uses for an ambulance-like drone. For instance, a drone could be mounted with an automated defibrillator. Upon arrival, emergency personnel can use a video feed to assist the victim and instruct people nearby on how to use the defibrillator properly. It can also be used to deliver organs in an efficient, time-saving manner. This drone has mounted sensors that maintain and monitor the organ, sending information to land in real-time. Its use could go beyond dropping off emergency kits and medicines, undertaking search and rescue missions, or working in zones of natural disasters. It could also be used to collect blood samples, as well as carry units to places where blood loss has occurred. 

This automated flying aid unit helps save lives by expanding existing emergency infrastructure through a network of fast and compact systems capable of providing emergency supplies and establishing a line of communication. An LTE advanced cellphone network infrastructure and cloud-based software may enable the necessary connectivity for controlling data and video, making it possible for the interaction between parties much easier than it currently is.

# Future Perspectives

Possibly, these ambulance drones could extinguish the need for on-land ambulances, thus giving a novel insight into how emergency support would be provided in the future. Medical installations, such as hospitals, would reduce in size once patients could have their medical assistance at the last mile, not only receiving aid when an emergency occurs. Professionals like nurses and doctors could assist patients remotely and also advise, thus avoiding possible emergencies when risk occasions are likely to happen, like in areas under threat.

*Photo/Illustration: Es sarawuth / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Computer-controlled environments that grow food autonomously without human assistance.
description.longText:
A computer-controlled environment able to perform a variety of farming functions, including seeding, watering, fertilizing, and removing weeds. To increase the level of accuracy, and depending on the plants cultivated, the user can download via an open-source platform the specific amount of water to irrigate the soil, the quantity of light dosed, or any other variable that addresses the needs of a particular species. 

The type of cultivation enabled by this system depends on the tools embedded in the miniaturized farming controlled environment.  It can range from dry agriculture to hydroponics, which is the most popular technique applied to current examples. From seeding to harvesting, the user will only be responsible for supplying the nutrients needed to grow vegetables, fruits, and herbs, such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, all already generally incorporated in the soil. With the help of machine vision, it could monitor whether plants are being excessively watered or if any fungi or bacteria have contaminated the production. It would alert the user, then require specific substances, such as fertilizers, for saving the plants.

By automating and thereby simplifying the cultivation of crops on a lower scale to meet local demand, regions that lack access to fresh produce, for instance, could be empowered to achieve food sovereignty. Also, it holds the promise to improve the diet habits of the overall population by bridging the access to healthy produce, and thus better nutrition.  

# Future Perspectives

If this automated farming method becomes popular enough to reach houses and areas of the most need —not just individuals that can afford to pay for it— it may eventually be a great ally in fighting hunger worldwide. Also, together with big data, interconnected gardens and urban agriculture could maintain a cyclic interrelation between food production and its broader environmental, economic, and social influences.

description.shortText: By layering dynamic digital inputs on contact lenses, this device enables more natural AR and VR experiences.
description.longText:
Contact lenses that can interact with augmented, mixed, and virtual reality more naturally compared to headset devices. It consists of microelectronics located in the middle of the lenses, displaying information directly on the retina, allowing users to see data even with their eyes closed.

The lenses are embedded with a proprietary wireless protocol that connects them to a portable device, such as smartphones. The smartphone, for example, would enable access to the internet in real-time and outsources computational power. Tiny built-in batteries could last for a whole day and could be recharged at night wirelessly while the lenses rest inside the cleaning case. With an integrated camera powered with facial recognition and behavioral monitoring methods to identify a target individual, this technology could provide personal identity, social media accounts, and real-time emotional data. Built-in sensors could monitor the user's glucose levels, sending real-time data to the lenses' app.

Some of the most prominent applications include gaming, medical, aerospace/defense, manufacturing, vehicle management, and navigation systems. Mixed reality contact lenses are expected to improve navigation systems and display data to help users choose the most efficient routes and means of transportation. Also, these contact lens can show real-time changes in moisture and pressure by changing colors, operating as a health sensor with cosmetic features. Lastly,  it could help the visually impaired navigate daily tasks by projecting specific colors and lights directly to the iris. The lenses would send alert messages to the wearer whenever there is a street sign or near potential danger.

# Future Perspectives

The scientific community is still in the early stages of understanding the human brain. Yet, the possibilities that accompany the developments in AR and VR are endless, including advancing in comprehending human cognition. If combined with technologies that can read brainwaves, this technology could help detect human feelings and emotions. By analyzing the signals coming out of someone's brain, whether this individual is under stress or stimulated by external inputs, the lenses could display all the data from this analysis.

In the future, these lenses could be powered with kinetic energy produced by eye movement, such as blinking. Instead of contact lenses, this device could be directly implanted in the eyeballs themselves, and the information received and collected could be delivered directly through brain implants.

description.shortText: A geothermal power-recycling plant that extracts CO2 from atmospheric air and transforms the resulting material into a byproduct. Able to generate byproducts, such as concrete, the raw materials produced can be sent to the market, thus establishing a circular carbon economy.
description.longText:
A power-recycling plant that uses geothermal energy to run a mechanism that absorbs CO2 from the atmosphere through a direct-air capture engineering system. This carbon capture technology can extract CO2 already in the atmosphere and collect the harmful gas on a large scale, converting CO2 into byproducts.

By filtering the air that passes over a special liquid, the power plant sticks CO2 into a mixture. The mixture is recycled by releasing the CO2 while using heat. The resulting material is turned into solid carbonate minerals through a high-pressure process that blends carbon dioxide, water, and basalt altogether. Able to generate byproducts, such as concrete, the raw materials produced can be sent to the market. 

# Future Perspectives

The hazards produced by CO2 exposure when transformed into byproducts need to be studied accurately before being marketed. Because it does not necessarily fight fossil fuels, this recycling system may encompass a better temporary alternative than a long-term solution. While countries across the globe prepare to shift to clean energy sources, authorities could create policies that require existing fossil fuel plants to acquire CO2 capturing credits, making it mandatory for the repurposing of the air pollutant gas.

description.shortText: An inexpensive and easy method to trigger mutations in DNA molecules, generating a high density of novel nucleotide diversity in the genomes of plants and animals. Chemical mutagenesis is a research area that has been investigated for functional genomic studies as well as plant breeding.
description.longText:
A method to induce genetic changes in DNA structure, affecting one or more genes, as a result of the interaction of certain environmental chemical compounds. It is an inexpensive and easy way to generate a high density of novel nucleotide diversity in the genomes of plants and animals, and as such is a research area that has been investigated for functional genomic studies as well as plant breeding. One of the most common chemicals used for mutagenesis in plants is ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS), which has already shown the ability to induce primarily single base point mutations.

Still, the high accumulation of environmental compounds have been showing genotoxic properties in short-term assays, which leads to a gap in time for obtaining information to determine if these events are responsible in tests for long-term animal mutagenicity and carcinogenicity. As such, scientists are performing comparative mutagenesis experiments with E. coli cells in vitro with and without mammalian liver preparations and in animal-medicated assays, so they can gather more accurate information on the order of the mutagenetic potency and how genotoxic factors can impact bacterial or mammalian cells.

Viruses and designer zinc-finger nucleases are another approach in mutagenetic research when trying to produce genetically modified ferrets, pigs, mice and zebrafish. With these tools, it becomes possible to target genes and combine them with somatic cell nuclear transfer and germ cell transplantation in order to generate gene-targeted animal models. In spite of being an advanced technique, it does not require the generation of embryonic stem cell-derived chimeras, thus making the production of non-mouse animal models faster for biomedical researchers.

# Future Perspectives

It is possible to imagine this technology as being a "helpful assistant" to new approaches to lab experimentation and biomedical research by providing ways to analyze mutagenesis without the need for the animal itself, but in-vitro simulations that could go beyond mice, while remaining applicable to plants and possibly humans as well.  More and more the mutagenicity testing of cosmetics involving minimal animal usage has shows efficiency in application without compromising the regulatory process.

description.shortText: Pods that travel inside near-vacuum-sealed pipes using linear induction propulsion systems. It works as an inter-city alternative transportation system for mass transit that could reach cruising speeds of 966 km/h.
description.longText:
A reduced-pressure sealed tube system with a near-zero friction environment for magnetic-levitating pods. These small pods would cruise at 966 km/h, propelled by a linear induction propulsion system allowing passengers to travel long distances in a short amount of time. As its regenerative braking system recovers much of the energy used during deceleration, it would generate more electricity than it consumes, providing the transportation industry and the world with a fresh perspective on clean energy production.

Reduced travel times might fundamentally alter how cities and suburbs are planned and have a disruptive impact on current inter-city transportation systems. Yet, the biggest concern when developing hyperloop projects is the high costs associated with infrastructure. Urban development and human communities must evolve along with the system for the project to be financially viable. This type of transportation solution does not depend solely on the construction and maintenance costs; it must be well-integrated with local economies and broader landscape projects.

# Future Perspectives
This technological solution could alter the way the industrialized world transports cargo. Road freight creates noise pollution, a matter of concern in areas of conservation as well as cities. Replacing a significant share of shipments carried by trucks would create shared value for society. Overall, it offers an attractive shared value proposition, integrating social welfare with economic value in a successful business model.

Concerns regarding safety, costs, and engineering challenges have yet to be fully hashed out, and one of the most challenging issues revolves around regulatory restrictions along with the expensive nature of digging and building underground pipe systems. This advancement for public mobility could also generate friction with companies that rely on old transportation methods; they might be unable or unwilling to adapt to change.

description.shortText: Brain-inspired chips whose building blocks store and process information faster and more efficiently with lower energy consumption than current systems with similar response characteristics to biological neurons.
description.longText:
An artificial analog data processor packed with artificial neurons and synapses that mimic human brain activity. 
Brain‐inspired neuromorphic chips have the potential to revolutionize the current computing paradigm with their massive parallelism and low power consumption potential. The fundamental limitations of existing systems for artificial neural networks lie in the fact that data and processing are physically separated, and continuous analog signals are represented using complementary digital metal–oxide–semiconductor devices (with “0” and “1” states). 

By operating more like natural neurons, the mathematical prowess of artificial neural networks can be mapped directly to the building blocks of neuromorphic devices. The underlying technology, components called memristors, regulate the flow of electricity, reminding a particular charge to act like synapses of the brain. This technology is faster, more efficient, and consumes less energy than current systems. The ability to process and store multiple or even continuous signal states can allow these chips to handle complex data, such as images and video orders of magnitude.

Memristors are being developed using graphene nanostructures, optoelectronics, quantum photonics, DNA, biological cells, or a combination of some of the aforementioned methods. Photons have significantly more bandwidth than electrons, yet, the advantages that optical data processing systems offer have still to manage to outweigh the high costs involved in manufacturing. Single-cell organisms such as slime mold are known for being able to determine the shortest path through a maze, or even model optimal railway systems and could act as a living memristor.

# Future Perspectives

Once this technology becomes scaleable, up to large network sizes, it will affect the future of computing. Laptops, mobile phones, and robots could include ultra-low-power neuromorphic chips that process visual, auditory, and other types of sensory information. Medical sensors and devices could track vital signs and respond to treatments over time, learning to adjust dosages or even catch early symptoms of a disease. Smartphones could learn to anticipate what the user wants next.
 
New developments in creating bio-memristors using DNA and even blood cells as basic computation units are blurring the boundary between silicon and biological systems. Neuroprosthetics could benefit from hybrid organic and digital semiconductors. The smartwatch of the future could be powered by blood-like cells that perform computations and interface directly with vital signs.

*Photo / Illustration: © Ulia Koltyrina / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A computing system that enables local processing of data. It provides safer, latency-free responses to automated devices, such as factory machines, autonomous vehicles, and overall IoT ecosystems.
description.longText:
A method of managing workloads and computation, working by placing the workload closer to the data gathering process. With edge computing, data doesn't need to be sent to the cloud to be processed and sent back to the device. By allowing for data processing locally, this approach can be beneficial for connections that demand low latency responses, such as industry 4.0 appliances. 

Edge computing is mounted with machine learning algorithms, enabling decision-making without relying entirely on cloud computing. It allows autonomous vehicles, for instance, to work in places with poor connectivity and to make decisions faster. In a factory, each machine could have its edge data processor, thus becoming more reliable and independent of externalities while all devices still communicate with a centralized server. 

Other advantages of this approach include the ability to process data with high bandwidth. It increases data protection and privacy as most of the data is never sent back to the cloud. Malicious attacks could, in theory, be more easily stopped by interrupting the internet connection.

# Future Perspectives

By allowing machines to process their data locally, without the need for an internet connection or the cloud, we would undeniably be giving greater independence to machines. In a pure science fiction scenario, we can imagine an artificial superintelligence agent, or even a general-purpose robot, mounted with internal edge computing, making it hard to be controlled by humans.

*Photo/Illustration: spainter_vfx / adobe.stock.com*
