description.shortText: Software designed to record and track the brain's electrical activity in real-time. The data collected is fed into a personalized algorithm, that is, the "mood map," which estimates a person's general mood based on their brain waves.
description.longText:
This software analyses collected data fed into a personalized algorithm, that is, the "mood map," which can estimate a person's general mood based on their brain waves. Such software has to work in tandem with wearables containing a series of small electrodes designed to record and measure the brain's electrical activity in real-time, to then send the data over for further analysis. This system works as a way of gathering data about emotional states in the medium to long term, as the algorithm is connected to a software that creates visualizations of a person's mood, thus detecting and pointing out recurring emotional patterns.

When the system detects patterns that indicate the onset of a depressive episode, for instance, it can be programmed to send a text message instantly to the user or their doctor. The system takes into consideration the networking and adaptability of the brain so that real-time neural interfaces allow the medical field to shift beyond the traditional static view and into the realm of a more precise, focused therapy.

In some cases, the wearables used to enable this software could also be mounted with neuromodulation strategies, meaning that after detecting the pervasive negative mood, it could also send small electric currents aiming to alleviate that feeling. Therefore, the algorithm is in charge of identifying moods and determining solutions to every change at a neural level without the need for physician oversight. In other cases, this emotional imaging could be connected to interactive storytelling or experiences, thus triggering outcomes in movies or games according to the user's emotional state.

# Future Perspectives 

Emotions are the next input in the search for more immersive, targeted digital experiences. It might come to the point in which all mixed reality headsets are integrated with mood map software, and the user's emotions could be fed in real-time to targeting algorithms. This loop could then influence everything that the user experiences in mixed reality layers. The adverts that are shown to someone who is feeling hopeless might be different from the ones shown to people that are feeling joyful, and so forth.

In a more dystopic perspective, knowing and decoding moods of happiness or sadness could be used to force individuals into a specific mood or feeling by using this technology. For example, a worker could be forced into a "happy" state to keep productivity up, or a criminal forced to face "sadness" as a punishment for their transgressions.

description.shortText: Underwater pods designed to cultivate seaweed and other marine species by taking advantage of all the characteristics found in seawater, such as constant temperature and protection from exposure to land-based extreme weather conditions.
description.longText:
Farming aquatic flora and fauna offshore in the open ocean could be a more sustainable approach to feed a growing world population with low environmental impacts. Different from underground hydroponic pods that depend on cooling and heating systems to regulate the temperature, underwater farms offer a more stable environment to yield crops. Underwater pods are usually submerged five to eight meters below the surface, providing a steady temperature to culture, while avoiding exposure to land-based extreme weather conditions.

While lettuce, basil, and strawberries are plants already grown in underwater farms, other approaches include cultivating seafood such as scallops, clams, oysters, and mussels in water columns alongside seaweed and shellfish. As opposed to regular crops, these ocean farming systems remove nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon dioxide from the water, thus helping protect ocean ecosystems and decrease ocean acidification, which is a consequence of carbon pollution. By soaking up carbon and keeping surrounding waters safe for shellfish and other vulnerable creatures, these seaweed-populated underwater farms would serve as a kind of sanctuary for crabs, shrimp, and other marine species.

Restorative ocean farming could play a vital role in helping coastal communities and the planet's climate. However, specific environmental concerns relating to the use of pesticides to prevent diseases are rising accordingly. Solutions such as nanobiopesticides are relatively promising, even though studies never made into testing it yet. 

# Future Perspectives

Although most of the features used in these underwater farms are specifically related to seawater and its geographical features, the same idea could be applied to rivers and lakes as well. This approach is another solution for famine and reduces the amount of land occupied for farming animal protein and food for humans. Nevertheless, freshwater conditions – such as flora and fauna – are different from the sea, so adaptations on structure and practices are expected.

Other questions that emerge include geopolitical issues such as where these pods would be positioned offshore, raising concerns on how to establish appropriate border policies for this technology to be correctly deployed.

description.shortText: Biodegradable coatings are typically made of water, oil, and wax. But, there is a promising new method using agricultural byproducts and waste, such as orange peels, to develop a formula to extend the shelf life of fresh produce.
description.longText:
Agriculture accounts for a considerable amount of waste from plastics and other pollutant materials used for packaging. However, consumers still expect their products to be protected, clean, and safe from any possible threat. This behavior over the last few decades has boosted food packaging production, and consequently, of plastic and many other pollutant materials. As an alternative, packaging made out of biocomposites represent a particularly innovative solution to substitute plastic and reduce the amount of food waste.

Bio-based coatings are made of bio-raw materials, such as biogenic scrap, or bio-mass balance methods using bionaphtha, biogas, or even natural amino acids. Currently, the agro-waste coating is a promising new coating method using agricultural byproducts and waste to extend the shelf life of fresh produce. In the form of a spray, the main component of these new lacquers is a biopolymer resin extracted from byproducts, such as orange peels, that act as a thin film, similar to plastic films. The bio-resin is actually cutin – a wax-like water-repellent biopolymer found in the walls of various plant cells – used to address food protection and preservation.

Renewable bio-based materials can allow slow and selective breathing of the produce, create a tailored atmosphere regarding the ripening process and nutrient composition of particular produce, serve as a vehicle to introduce food additives, and prevent microbial spoilage. They are useful in a range of performance-based markets and applications, including specialty coatings, personal care, cosmetics, food, pharma, nutraceuticals, consumer fuels, and packaging due to their excellent sealability, gas and grease barrier, and thermal resistance. Nevertheless, current concerns about the safety and risks associated with human ingestion and use must be considered before widespread deployment.


# Future Perspectives

By embedding active biosensors in agro-coating compounds, edible packagings could enhance the monitoring of food, avoid spoilage, increase food security, and generate an accountable relationship with consumers. This effort could possibly avoid having an adverse effect on the environment, as the biosensors would be biodegradable along with the coating. Moreover, these active sensing biodegradable coatings could be alternatively used to directly cover other products, such as natural makeup powders, where products undergo unfavorable chemical reactions similar to food products during their expiration that must be monitored and signaled to customers.

In the long term, edible films and coatings could become an ingredient, controlling the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between the product and the ambient atmosphere. Besides, it would provide microbial stability for the product by incorporating antimicrobial agents. The development of antimicrobial coatings can generate a seamless model of preventive medicine in which the food itself turns into the medicine that delivers non-toxic pharmacology needs for populations in many parts of the globe.

description.shortText: Predictive analytics integrated with geographical data that analyzes past and present communication channels of social media posts to predict possible areas that are prone to conflicts. It identifies where it would be better to intervene, and what level of intervention will be necessary.
description.longText:
Predictive analytics integrated with geographical data that analyzes past and present communication from social media channels to predict possible areas that are prone to conflicts. It identifies where it would be better to intervene, and what level of intervention will be necessary. Besides having access to criminal records from groups that were already targeted for illegal activity, quantitative conflict models also focus on analyzing past and present financial transactions and data extracted from crowdsourced platforms. 

Apart from analyzing communication patterns, conflict prediction models incorporate geographical information to automate the identification of possible conflict areas. These models can be scaled to identify risk areas in an entire region or within a city. By using algorithms that forecast risks, similar to predicting policing needs and extreme weather changes, trouble spots could be flagged. 

The patterns in violence and the underlying causes and relations are shifting rapidly, making the process of modeling predictive systems more intricate when it comes to conflict analytics. Due to the structural complexity surrounding processes of peace and conflict, predictive models are still in their infancy. With the help of machine learning, early warning systems could be created to help the global community to take action before violent breakouts. 
Regarding online criminal organizations, governments could more efficiently carry out attacks just by analyzing the formation of online group interactions, thus enabling authorities to act upon them —either preemptively or defensively.


# Future Perspectives

When models are able to predict conflict accurately, they should be able to provide information on where it is best to intervene and ideally give suggestions of how much intervention will be necessary for a peaceful outcome. For a conflict to happen, there are intangible factors that are crucial for predicting when an event is about to occur. The willingness to fight, the weapons used, the funding from sources outside the country, besides the changes in political ideology, are some intangibles that should be seriously taken into account when adding data to predictive analytics. Since the success of predictive models depends directly on the quality and availability of data, global cooperation will be necessary to create databases that can be used to feed algorithms. 

Advances in the field of deep learning that allow real-time sentiment analysis of text, audio, and even video are providing new data-driven indicators that could be integrated with spatial prediction models. Advances in machine reasoning could allow future conflict models to do more than make predictions: they could potentially offer explanations for violence and strategies for preventing it.

description.shortText: This chip-sized device mimics the dynamics of a living organ for safe and efficient tests and improves the physiology of in-vitro models. It enables more efficient research approaches in the fields of biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and chemicals.
description.longText:
More important than a simple issue of economics, the testing of products and pharmaceuticals is ethically problematic considering the animal rights abuses and dangers of using human subjects for testing with unknown consequences. In an attempt to combat these challenges, scientists have developed a chip-sized device that can mimic a living organ and its dynamics on a tiny scale.

This device, popularly known as organ-on-a-chip, contains cells layered in the hollow compartments of the chip according to the actual, emulated organ; fluid flow (blood and lymph) is reproduced via channels. It produces normal levels of organ functionality, allowing an analysis of biochemical, genetic, and metabolic activities. Connecting chips could help systematically map the functions and interactions of the whole body while proving that living organs are more predictable than expected and assist in understanding how diseases develop and progress accordingly.

An organ-on-a-chip can enable new, more efficient biomedical research approaches, more reliably producing results when predicting the effects on humans. It can accelerate research and discoveries in the fields of biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and chemicals. At the same time, academic institutions and hospitals can also benefit from this technology to develop and test personalized medicine. However, the challenge is to make this device as accurate as possible to replicate the simulated results in the real world.

# Future Perspectives

The large-scale adoption of organs-on-a-chip could reduce the time necessary to develop new drugs. It creates more room for experimenting with innovative formulas while abiding by ethical codes throughout the world. Animal and human testing could become something of the past while maintaining industry efficiency.

As the technology matures, these chips could be available as point-of-care testing. That is, at the time and place of patient care, especially in critical care settings such as the intensive care units, the operating room, and the emergency department. 

Eventually, such chips could be made on a personalized scale. Every single person could have their own set of chips, with each of them representing a particular organ. Enter personalized tests: drugs and cosmetics could be first tested on the chip to check for incompatibilities and potential reactions, and only applied directly to the organism following satisfactory results. Unintended consequences, which create health issues and general frustration with personal care products, could be significantly reduced. Finally, the ultimate goal of organ-on-a-chip technology might be integrating numerous organs into a single chip. From this moment onwards, it would be possible to build a more complex multi-organ chip model, finally achieving a “human-on-a-chip” aspiration.

description.shortText: A hybrid model of currency built on both crypto and fiat assets. It is based on a third-generation blockchain using a delegated proof of stake consensus mechanism that provides methods for validating blocks and transactions for governance functions for the common public good.
description.longText:
A hybrid model of currency built on both crypto and fiat assets. It is based on a third-generation blockchain using a delegated proof of stake consensus mechanism that provides ways of validating blocks and transactions for governance functions for the common public good. 

Like all resources, money cannot be limitlessly exploited, even in a digital format. For many, cryptocurrencies are seen as a way to bring more fairness to the global economic system. Yet, due to their decentralized nature, there is no clear central ownership and stabilization management, thus in past years, their price volatility has jeopardized their potential. Large tech companies are on their way to issuing digital currencies backed by some 'real-world' assets as a collective intent to solve this issue, but this movement also raises concerns that private entities may tend to act in their own interests. 

In order to create a more trustworthy and sustainable economic system, governments around the world are trying to partner with private actors to issue hybrid coins with legal tender status. Through this model, crypto-fiat currencies attract a broader network participation the more significant the chain. Besides connecting distant economic systems, the purpose is to promote long-term sustainability and prevent runaway inflation, by algorithmically fixing the annual increase rate on the blockchain. To ensure fairness, each supply grown is automatically sent to all eligible users - not to the banking system as in traditional finance.

Sovereign cryptocurrency rules of issuance are embedded into the protocol, algorithmically enforced apps and DAOs deployed on the blockchain as well. By legitimizing cryptocurrencies, funds are made available to law enforcement. Additionally, in the third-generation blockchain, the consensus is achieved through less energy usage than in proof-of-work and other similar mechanisms. Furthermore, there is no particular class of nodes required in this protocol, like the miners in the blockchain ecosystem. By providing quick finality, low latency, open participation, with a green, mining-less, and sustainable environmental impact, sovereign cryptocurrency could also contribute to the UN Sustainability Goals. 

# Future Perspectives

In the next decade, the development of the Internet of Things (IoT) across the globe may require viable economic assets capable of bridging the gap of the digital and physical world. Hybrid models of currency might be vital for transforming a more significant part of the population into autonomous economic actors, all by all connecting the IoT capabilities with individuals with regular civil duties such as tax payments, insurances, and licensing fees. The digital economy would turn into a synthetic model, facilitating the regulation of marginalized markets, and enhancing peer-to-peer transactions through a collaborative regulatory framework.

description.shortText: Decentralized energy distribution points located nearer to consumers that are able to supply energy to local communities independently of large-scale energy plants.
description.longText:
Different from large-scale conventional utility plants, decentralized energy grids can transfer, store, and harvest electricity or heat in smaller units located nearer to consumers. Instead of centralizing enormous facilities that typically cause considerable sustainability issues, these grids aggregate the decentralized production of energy from distributed energy resources (DERs). From wind, solar, combined heat and power (CHP), biogas, hydropower, fossil steam, power-to-heat, to diesel engines, decentralized energy grids are an optimal solution to empower communities and individuals, so they become the holders of their energy distribution and production. 

Energy storage facilities, such as batteries, thermal, compressed air, and pumped storage, could also be incorporated. With the help of IoT sensors and big data, it could monitor and optimize the grids and the networks benefiting from the energy produced, from homes and small-scale producers to businesses or industrial sites. Considering that this model allows different units to supply power to localized communities and areas, the decentralization of energy could decrease greenhouse gas emissions as the production does not exceed demand. Also, as the decentralization of energy increases efficiency due to the reduction in lost energy during transfer, it could create economic value for the producer in the long-term. However, the implementation costs are still a point of resistance. For instance, as solar panels are expensive assets, the expectancy of wide-range adoption of this energy model is still in its infancy. 

# Future Perspectives
As these systems become more accessible and inclusive, individual households could sell extra energy to the grid, in a peer-to-peer model, becoming a distributed energy grid. Also, these systems are evolving to become autonomous, making optimal decision and energy negotiations without human input, optimizing energy efficiency and cost, taking into consideration not only the source of power but also real-time information such as the weather.

description.shortText: Subatomic particles can exist in more than one state at any given time. Quantum computing takes advantage of this ability, allowing operations to be carried out significantly faster than with regular computers while also being able to store more information.
description.longText:
Regular computing is done using transistor-based operations, where data is stored in the form of bits - binary digits that can only be a zero or a one. This fundamental restriction limits the number of operations a computer can do at one time. A quantum computer, on the other hand, operates on the subatomic level, where the rules of quantum mechanics apply. It can take advantage of quantum mechanical properties like superposition and entanglement. Through the logic of superposition, a quantum bit or qubit occupies more than one state at the same time until a measurement is made to deliver a result. Each qubit can stand for one node, one artificial neuron in a neural network. In regular computing, eight bits of standard computing power has 256 combinations, but only one can be used at a time, whereas eight qubits would be able to store – and process – all 256 combinations at once.

This has significant advantages in performing highly complex operations and solving complicated optimization problems at extreme speeds. Quantum computing could be particularly useful for advanced climate modeling, optimization of transportation, and for quickly solving other complicated problems.  Also, nature itself does not store information in binary, and what better way to solve quantum-mechanical problems than using actual quantum mechanics? As quantum computers can analyze large amounts of data and quickly spot patterns, they could usher in a new era of medical science through the ability to explore new proteins or other molecules extremely quickly and to create effective new drugs much more quickly.

This radically different approach to computing will also have a profound impact on the way artificial intelligence operates, being able to solve complex AI problems and simultaneously generate multiple solutions. It will likely result in artificial agents that can perform human-like problem-solving at high speeds. Future machines could optimize and solve problems previously unsolvable for human brains or the fastest computers of today.

One of the biggest concerns regarding the implementation of quantum computing is the theoretical ability to relatively easily crack nearly every current asymmetric cryptography system in place today. Most encryption systems remain secure solely based on the fact that traditional computers would have to perform a near-impossible number of calculations, taking years or centuries to be able to compute the private key from a public key. Quantum computers could perform this decryption using a fraction of the operations it would take a conventional computer – even a supercomputer. Accordingly, quantum computers could be able to instantly solve even the most robust RSA encryption systems, putting at risk the entire current credit card authentication system and cryptocurrency systems, posing an unprecedented threat to privacy and security. However, quantum technology at the same holds the key to highly secure new forms for data security, e. g. for connections that cannot be tapped without the communicating parties noticing it, or using quantum entanglement for untappable links, or spin measuring technology for connections that are based on using ambiguity for security.

# Future Perspectives 

Instead of physically owning a quantum computer, thanks to emerging and future fibreoptics and wireless standards, it is likely that compute time would be bought from central computing facilities. This would continue the shift towards a post-ownership society.

A whole new field of research called quantum machine learning explores the possibility of merging artificial minds with more nature-like processing technologies. The combination of the extreme computing power of quantum computers and such a versatile technology as neural networks could bring about machines with a level of intelligence similar to that of humans, but with much higher processing speeds. One of the first tasks of quantum machine learning agents might be the design of their own successors.

*Illustration/photo: Marcel Strauß / Unsplash*

description.shortText: Blockchain-based service that anonymously secures and stores an online distributed proof-of-existence for any document. It creates a 'digital fingerprint' that is easily traceable while also adding a layer of security in proving data ownership without revealing the actual data.
description.longText:
A blockchain-based service that anonymously secures and stores an online distributed proof-of-existence for any document, as well as proof-of-ownership and document ownership transfer. While not serving as document storage, documents and files are time-stamped and assigned a digital fingerprint within the blockchain to prevent unauthorized tampering and modification. It allows a public verification of the document’s date, authenticity, origin, integrity, and content without publicly disclosing the content itself. Biometric identification, such as fingerprints, could be used as a digital signature (or private key in cryptography terms) to prove that an individual owns a particular document.  

Traditional centralized entities that secure information and authenticity, such as banks, could replace their current systems with blockchain notaries, giving the digital hash the same status as legal validation. Instead of physically visiting registry offices to validate information, all verifications could be done online. This service could add additional security for digital transactions on the internet, thus allowing extensive cooperation.

The implementation of this protocol creates a "digital footprint" that is easily traceable, adding a layer of security that proves data ownership without revealing the data itself. Considering the advantages, government agencies and public services could employ a distributed network accompanied by a public ledger instead of central notary authorities.

# Future Perspectives

Birth and marriage certificates could also be issued using blockchain notaries, reducing the cost and time and improving safety. This could guarantee the right to identity for children when they are born or even recognize same-sex marriage in places where it is still not legalized.

One possible method of using blockchain notaries is developing smart contracts that invoke a statutory durable power of attorney when the owner/user is not available or disabled. This process would alleviate crucial problems that affect people with mobility limitations. By learning the decision-making methodologies through machine learning, this technology could automate the whole certification system. Questions regarding the level of trust state governments would give to the blockchain remain uncertain, especially considering its by-design resistance to allow any modification made by a central authority on the data.

*Photo/Illustration: Olivier Le Moal / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A blood repellent titanium-based material that can repel virtually any liquid by roughening its surface with nanotubes. With potential medical implant applications, this superhemophobic material could reduce the risk of forming clots.
description.longText:
A titanium-based material that can repel virtually any liquid, but in particular blood, by roughening its surface with nanotubes. By using a substrate made out of superhemophobic titania nanotubes, scientists can use a stable substance that could considerably decrease the surface absorption of protein while simultaneously delaying the clotting process. 

This is a key innovation for medicine in terms of implants and medical devices as it can help solve issues such as blood clotting, as blood is incredibly difficult to repel from other materials and surfaces, creating significant challenges for scientists. Some reasons include the high propensity of blood to activate intrinsic hemostatic mechanisms, as well as the induction of coagulation, and the activation of platelets upon contact with foreign bodies. In other words, when coagulation is imbalanced, patients using implants or medical devices could suffer from thrombogenesis or the formation of blood clots. In turn, this can impede the blood flow either at the site or even further downstream, causing emboli or exposing tissue to ischemia and infarction.

The research regarding the interactions of superhemophobic surfaces and blood showed a considerable amount of protein adsorption and impressive platelet adhesion, which indicates this is a potential method for enhancing the compatibility of blood with other materials. The concept of strengthening hemocompatibility has been paramount in scientific research. This is because currently proposed methods, including modified polymer surfaces, did not show the same results as titania nanotubes arrays. Superhemophobic surfaces are a novel approach designed to enhance hemocompatibility; however, the interactions of blood components with these surfaces have not been studied in-depth, and further research is required for proper deployment.

In addition to medical devices, scientists are also considering the development of superhemophobic textiles, but using another substrate beside titanium nanotubes. Research has shown that a chitosan-aloe vera bionanocomposite could be used to produce not only blood-repellent but also antimicrobial lab garments; an achievement that could improve the life and treatment of hospital patients in the event of contamination.

# Future Perspectives

With the use of blood-repellent materials such as the one based on titania nanotubes, patients can reduce side effects and be protected from contact between foreign devices and blood. However, more long-term research is necessary to fully deploy implantables benefitting from this technology. Another challenge faced by scientists is the development of manufacturing processes suitable for implantables, finding ways to make such devices scalable to attend to all patients with such demands.

description.shortText: A type of identification in the form of a wearable, microchip implant, or AR badge that gathers personal data from locations, social media profiles, and interactions of individuals. It analyzes the data and provides feedback regarding activities, emotions, conversations, and published content.
description.longText:
A type of identification that could take the form of a wearable, microchip implant, or AR badge, it can gather personal data from locations and interactions of individuals. This information can be analyzed to give feedback regarding activities, emotions, conversations, and published content. AR badges can go a step further, in which fiduciary markers can display the desired information through AR glasses or even eye-projectors.

During human interactions, individuals express —and often hide— several emotions, feelings, and thoughts. Social relationships can be overwhelming for some, and sociometric badges are designed to ease this process. This technological solution records geolocation, oral conversations, and data from social media, and then captures and measures what exactly happens between individuals, such as how each individual felt by analyzing the pitch of their voice.  

In order to address solutions to understand sociological behavior, governments and organizations may use these badges to monitor individuals according to their needs or constitutions. It would facilitate the process of law comprehension and acceptance. In educational environments, these badges enable teachers to take their students outside structured environments like classrooms while maintaining the ability to measure their level of engagement and provide personalized feedback objectively. 

Types of use can multiply when considering the many activities that happen inside of schools. Some examples include using the device to analyze the effectiveness of peer learning (e.g., analyzing geo-locations for interaction patterns and creating social networks of who-learns-with-whom) or even to uncover school bullies by analyzing voice pitches to detect 'anger' or 'fear.'

Even if promising, sociometric badges raise considerable concerns regarding privacy. Although the sensitive information gathered in these devices is intended to be shared among other individuals, the act of continuously carrying an identification that displays private data brings up fundamental questions whether this technology is used to help in social relationships or to control human behavior.

# Future Perspectives 

Although an individual could wear these badges, this type of tracking device may be anywhere and everywhere as connectivity grows, and the price of microchips drops. Also, biological information could be used to enrich the gathered data and, therefore, give more precise information about users.

As extended reality flourishes, they could also be used as an additional digital layer to social life, displaying clout, status, and personality traits depending on what the user wants the world to see. A person might choose to display their marital status, a horoscope sign, badges earned in games or sports, the team they support, or the company they work for.

description.shortText: Hollow carbon cylindrical tubes thinner than a strand of human hair that could be significantly stronger than steel. Great conductors of electricity and heat, nanotubes are compact, lightweight materials that have proven to provide a myriad of potential uses.
description.longText:
Hollow cylindrical tubes similar to graphite found in pencils that, while thinner than a strand of human hair, could be significantly stronger than steel. The material has a great ability to conduct electricity and heat over a vast surface area, which can create new methods of improving lithium batteries. A hybrid combination of carbon and graphene nanotubes together would maximize the capacity of the available battery volume.

Carbon nanotubes have also been used as composite fibers in polymers to improve the mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties of bulk products such as bicycle components, maritime vessels, and carbon nanoepoxy resins used for wind turbines, marine paints and sports gear like skis. By extracting the carbon nanotubes and hydrogen from waste plastics, these elements could be converted and incorporated into touchscreen devices (tablets and phones, for instance), high-strength materials like bulletproof vests and hydrogen fuel cells that would power cars and solar panels. They could also be used to manufacture brake discs, advanced aerospace composites, co-axial cables, conductive fuel lines, electromagnetic interference shielding in electronic devices, 3D memory chips, coatings, conductive tires, and inks. 

Carbon nanotubes are also an innovative and powerful tool for water desalination. As they carry a negative charge, they repel negatively charged ions in salt when separating individual water molecules. This process efficiently repels salt and separates water molecules—the basis of desalination processes—and can be used to provide higher quality water for general purposes, and could also be applied in agriculture water irrigation pipes.

# Future Perspectives

The industrial production of nanotubes can lead to a wider application due to the rapid growth in the market for nanoparticles in drugs, cosmetics, fabrics, water filters, and military weapons. With thousands of tons annually produced to fight waste production, carbon nanotubes are expected to be purified and applied in agriculture.

The separation of carbon nanotubes happens when they are filtered from other entities, such as carbon nanoparticles, amorphous carbon, residual catalysts, and other unwanted species. Experts have tested several techniques, from centrifugal separation to chemical separation to remove impurities. As a result, it would be beneficial for the early growth of wheatgrass in a hydroponic garden to test the potential of nanoparticles on the plant. The next step is to look at hydrophobic substrates that mimic the positive effects observed in nanotubes that could be used for high-efficiency channeling of water to seeds. Also, we may see other biomedical applications using these materials to produce hybrid biosensors, drug delivery systems, and high-performance composites for implants.

This process efficiently repels salt and separates water molecules—the basis of desalination processes—and can be used to provide higher quality water for general purposes, and could also be applied in agriculture water irrigation pipes.

Future Perspectives

The industrial production of nanotubes can lead to a wider application due to the rapid growth in the market for nanoparticles in drugs, cosmetics, fabrics, water filters, and military weapons. With thousands of tons annually produced to fight waste production, carbon nanotubes are expected to be purified and applied in agriculture.

The separation of carbon nanotubes happens when they are filtered from other entities, such as carbon nanoparticles, amorphous carbon, residual catalysts, and other unwanted species. Experts have tested several techniques, from centrifugal separation to chemical separation to remove impurities. As a result, it would be beneficial for the early growth of wheatgrass in a hydroponic garden to test the potential of nanoparticles on the plant. The next step is to look at hydrophobic substrates that mimic the positive effects observed in nanotubes that could be used for high-efficiency channeling of water to seeds. Also, we may see other biomedical applications using these materials to produce hybrid biosensors, drug delivery systems, and high-performance composites for implants.

description.shortText: AI developments embedded in agricultural vehicles such as tractors designed to take over horticultural tasks such as pruning, weeding, spraying, harvesting, tilling, and monitoring.
description.longText:
An autonomous self-propelled vehicle, managed by a combination of video cameras, radar, accelerometers, a LIDAR system, and onboard software, which perform agricultural activities and transportation without the need for a driver. By eliminating the need to have someone at the wheel, this technology drastically reduces the time and cost of production and transportation. Agricultural vehicles operate in a significantly safer environment than conventional road systems. They could, therefore, see quicker adoption and serve as a stepping stone to fully autonomous self-driving vehicles across the board. 

Most robots used in agriculture are designed to replace human labor at the harvesting stage, such as fruit-picking robots, driverless tractors, or milkbots. So far, proper execution of tasks has been difficult because of the specificity and peculiarities of trade, including the size and color of the fruit to be picked. However, AI developments may eventually facilitate the creation of self-learning robots that can take over other horticultural tasks such as pruning, weeding, spraying, and monitoring.

These features would open up access to machinery control and the data gateway while contributing to farming autonomy by showing the tractor’s progress in the field and giving farmers the possibility of simultaneously and remotely managing many different crops off-site. For ground transportation, independent trucks would no longer be hindered by the needs and limits of human drivers.

# Future Perspectives

Since there is no need for an operator on board, autonomous vehicles could operate 24 hours a day without stopping. Besides, further developments to reduce their size and radically redesign their shape would result in significant changes. The smaller size and possibly slower speeds due to longer operating hours could introduce higher levels of precision, and higher specialization of vehicles. The same idea would apply not only to farming itself but also as a means to automate the logistics sector without the need for drivers. 

However, as the trend of using autonomous machines to supply our needs is continually growing, the concern over maintaining human labor in agriculture rises as well. For a future in which devices are supporting our activities, we must also take care of the unprivileged sectors of society, which will be at risk of losing their jobs. Accordingly, to avoid facing an employment crisis, it would be interesting to take a look at educational strategies to provide knowledge about autonomous devices. Regulatory frameworks will be needed to tackle potential implications of digital agricultural technologies for farm labor and rural communities in the future since automated equipment could transform the farming workforce as we know it today.

Through careful planning, this digital shift can positively contribute to growth in rural communities by creating new work opportunities. Farmers will redeploy their employees to value-added tasks and new tasks to control and program autonomous machines. This more transparent manner could help ease the continually evolving process of human relationships with robots and AI, thus making the transition less of a challenge.

description.shortText: Drones and other autonomous aircraft coupled with wireless connectivity to complement and distribute terrestrial access to the internet.
description.longText:
Drones, autonomous aircraft, or crewless balloon-based designs able to reach outlying areas to make the internet available to those with little-to-no access across the globe. These uncrewed aerial vehicles are designed to enhance coverage, capacity, reliability, and energy efficiency of wireless networks. 

The uncrewed aircraft can recognize the territory they are flying above, but, current units only follow pre-programmed routes. Once they arrive at controlled airspace, the vehicles keep a certain distance from the ground and circulate the area for a determined period of time. While in mid-air, they complement existing cellular systems by providing additional capacity to hotspot areas as well as to provide network coverage in emergencies or areas without any access to the internet. 

In developing countries, they could dramatically increase access to useful information like the weather forecast, thus optimizing agricultural processes on remote farms. In education, this technology could also provide internet access to remote areas, benefiting unconnected local schools working offline due to infrastructural restrictions. By forming a network, these devices can offer an easy to deploy solution capable of covering rural and remote areas all over the world. 

# Future Perspectives

These autonomous aircraft could be an integral part of smart cities, from both a wireless and operational perspective. They can be used as data collection devices that can gather vast amounts of data from across various geographical areas and deliver them to central cloud units. Besides, they could act as mobile cloud computing systems and could provide fog computing and offloading opportunities for personal devices that are unable to perform computationally heavy tasks.

Even if promising, this technological solution heavily depends on weather conditions. Current examples are unreliable and quickly overwhelmed in certain weather conditions such as a storm or rain. Next developments are expected to include predictive analytics to anticipate whenever the weather may change, thus saving damage costs and improving the solution itself.

*Photo/Illustration: Mikael Damkier / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: By harnessing the incredible density and storage capabilities of DNA, researchers could develop an incredible massive storage system inspired by nature.
description.longText:
Based on the notion that DNA is the densest known storage medium in the universe, per the laws of physics, DNA could be used to store data for millions of years effectively. The method would work like an operational storage system, which would store data at incredible densities (a single gram can hold roughly a zettabyte). First, a software program would convert binary digital data into the DNA string bases, A, T, C, and G. Then, the information would be stored in wet media until retrieved and decoded into binary again.

DNA could be the best long-term repository for information, continuing to exist for thousands of years. Unlike most methods, DNA is and will continue to be highly relevant, meaning that as long as there are humans on Earth, it is quite likely that we will be interested in improving methods of reading and translating our DNA. Instead of becoming obsolete like other forms of data storage, the technology will likely continue to develop for years to come.

The main issue with implementation is cost: the chemical process used to manufacture DNA strands remains complex and expensive. Additionally, the process of automating and writing digital data into DNA is at a critical stage because writing and retrieving data to/from DNA is an incredibly slow process. Due to the complicated process of returning molecules to a digital format, this method could be more suitable as a data archive, which would store long-term data that does not need to be accessed frequently. Later, the concept could be adapted to computer memory, capable of saving videos, photos, or valuable documents in the same molecules as our genes. 

The main issue regarding privacy with this technology centers on having such a massive amount of data gathered in one place. Even though DNA is meant to be unique and impossible to hack, by replicating the same density of the DNA to recreate natural storage systems, it could take many technological developments steps back in the process of decentralizing storage systems. 

# Future Perspectives

Once researchers streamline the process of encoding and decoding data from DNA, this technology could fully substitute digital hardware. Due to its wet media properties, DNA-based digital storage could be especially useful in biotech industries in processing nanoscale activities. For instance, instructions to be followed by ingestible nanorobots once inside the body could be programmed into DNA.

Also, it could be possible to encode all kinds of digital information into a person's DNA. Once we sufficiently manage to use human DNA to store essential content, concerns will begin to arise regarding security and hackability to prevent a malicious individual from gaining the power to access, write, and edit someone else’s private genetic information without consent.

*Photo / Illustration: © yongheng19962008 / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: As concrete is a dense material, it can store massive amounts of potential energy. By stacking heavy blocks of concrete and releasing one block to crash into another with the help of gravity, it generates energy that can be later stored.
description.longText:
Potential energy is the energy stored within an object or substance. As concrete is a dense material, it holds tremendous potential to store massive amounts of potential energy. In order to release this energy, blocks of concrete need to be lifted at considerable heights and then brought back to the pile of concrete blocks. When these blocks get in touch, the gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy. 

The more the concrete blocks are brought further apart, the more potential energy is generated. The crane responsible for lifting the blocks is equipped with electric motors, connected to a ground generator. At the same time, by lowering the concrete mass back down to the ground, the generator shifts to spin and creates electricity ready for consumption. 

A large project, for instance, uses cement blocks weighing 35 metric tons, stacked on a 120-meter tall tower, with six crane arms around it. When there is excess wind or solar power, a computer algorithm directs one or more crane arms to locate a concrete block, with the help of a camera attached to the crane arm’s trolley. This specific system can store the total energy of 20 megawatt-hours (MWh).

# Future Perspectives

Stacking Concrete Energy Storage has drawn a lot of attention from investors due to its mechanical simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and minimum environmental impact compared to lithium batteries. Even if it needs a large area, a concrete gravity power plant can operate for 30 years with little maintenance, while the maximum life of lithium-ion batteries is around 20 years, losing its capacity to store energy over time. Also, there aren’t yet reliable ways to recycle practical lithium-ion batteries.

*Photo: Artsiom Kuchynski /  adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Potentially the world's most robust material, carbyne is a linear acetylenic carbon molecule: an infinitely long carbon chain. It can be viewed as an endless, one-dimensional allotrope of carbon. Its tensile strength is up to three times that of diamond and almost twice that of carbon nanotubes.
description.longText:
With an infinitely long carbon chain structure, carbyne is the most robust material in the world, with Young's modulus about forty times that of diamond and thirty times stronger than that of carbon nanotubes. Young’s modulus is a measure of crosswise deformation of a material in relation to a force that is applied lengthwise. So, the theoretical stiffness of this material is enormous. However, this extreme number is due to the use of a cross-sectional area that does not correspond to the actual space that the material occupies. Practically more relevant is the tensile strength of the material, which is up to three times that of diamond and almost twice that of carbon nanotubes and graphene.

This new material is currently stable only when inside nanotubes and chain length are still limited. It could be highly useful for a new, nanoscale generation of electronics. Furthermore, the molecules can be turned into a semiconductor when twisted. With unusual mechanical and electric properties, it has the potential to make nanomechanics, spintronic devices, and micro-electro-mechanical systems. It also has the potential for energy storage matrices like batteries and supercapacitors, due to its extensive surface area in relation to mass, which is important for energy density.

# Future Perspectives

One of the possible future applications of carbyne is the construction of spaceships and space elevators, which demand super-strong materials to form structures that could measure 65,000 kilometers and more. It could also make spaceplane bodies lighter and thus increase the power-to-weight ratio of these aerospace vehicles. By building a spaceship with carbyne, it could be possible to create a single-stage spaceplane that can reach orbit.

*Photo/illustration: Tobias van Schneider / Unsplash*

description.shortText: The use of a combination of ad-targeting, behavior tracking, natural language processing, and adaptive engagement scripts to target content for specific needs.
description.longText:
A combination of ad-targeting, behavior tracking, natural language processing, and adaptive engagement scripts, advertising used to target content for specific needs.  By using AI and deep learning algorithms, systems could generate thousands of personalized banners per second, even undertaking the design and rendering of this material, based on an individual’s preferences. At the same time, AI could eliminate error-prone focus groups and disjointed data to bring real-time, relevant insights to help organizations understand, plan, and design better policies for the future. Furthermore, such content could be produced and replicated at an almost limitless scale using the estimated millions of social-media bots. 

Via the aggregation of online chatter, regional patterns, and comparative data, it might become possible to predict the demands of ordinary citizens. With these insights, advertising agencies and brands will be able to target specific content such as public services or organizations, or even collect feedback regarding the governmental process.  Also, marketing budgets could benefit from this software while reducing some sources of fraud, like click injection or simulated ad clicks. Since AI is trained to recognize actual humans with needs and desires, "spoof" data can be cleaned and rejected.

However, the misapplication of this kind of technology could lead to a scenario of data mediation control and manipulation of information. It would create specific ideology-based bubbles from the perspective of both individuals and entire populations or regions. These populations would be prone to mass data collection for analysis, a process that would directly affect collective autonomy and media independence.

# Future Perspectives

In a virtual or augmented world, this technology could provide a unique visual experience for each user, thus shaping how individuals perceive that world. With developed emotional AI, brand avatars might adapt their tone of voice to different profiles by optimizing conversion rates. Members with varying tiers of subscription, for instance, might be able to view the same world differently. A play-for-free member might have to endure advertisements to enjoy certain benefits, while monthly subscription members could roam freely to socialize, play games, and shop.

This can also perpetuate discrimination and reinforce or even worsen existing inequalities by making privacy the most magnificent luxury of the new digital era. On the other hand, the development of data analysis methods powered by artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions could be based on an ethical framework. This could create curated content to connect consumers with relevant products and services in line with their interests and lifestyles. As AI becomes more robust with the intersection of psychology and neuroscience, in theory, it could become one of the most advanced and persuasive forms of communication ever invented by humankind.

description.shortText: A credit-tracking system that evaluates and ranks citizen behavior, quantifying it into a social credit code, linked to a permanent and nontransferable record. Records could be accessed by governments and private companies while allowing citizens to evaluate who they want to be associated with.
description.longText:
A set of algorithms that monitor and assess the trustworthiness of individuals.  By collecting data from social media, public databases such as criminal records, and surveillance cameras, it is possible to rate citizens' participation in society. Depending on partnerships with private parties, it might even be possible to collect data from a variety of sources such as e-commerce websites or even bank accounts. This system is generally based on parameters predefined by the authorities in compliance with universal fundamental rights. Records could be accessed by governments and private companies, while also allowing citizens to evaluate who they want to be associated with. 

The different collected data generates a social-credit score that serves as a way to either reward good behavior or penalize citizens with low ratings. If individuals drop below a predefined number of points, they could be denied loans or access to products or services. Penalties could include delaying paperwork, restricting opportunities for work, or reducing internet speeds, among other consequences. By having a good score, one could skip different types bureaucracies and have several advantages among other citizens. A high score could as well be rewarded with acceptance into universities, better job prospects, discounts on utilities, low-interest loans, and even prioritized in public services, such as transport or hospitals. A government partnered with corporations, for instance, could generate “credit scores” by developing a credit reporting system for individuals. 

Regarding environmental issues, this technology could make possible the analyses and rewards of sustainable behaviors through loyalty points and discounts on purchases. The more popular these systems become, the deeper the level of consumer brand engagement. Nevertheless, by turning every person’s experiences into public transactions, it could enhance the polarization of society, increasing competition between citizens who behave according to society's norms and those who do not. 

In the current world, inequality is a burden that most people are struggling with. An evaluation system that takes into account an individual's behavior could become a factor that might increase the already prevailing social divide. A social currency, that evaluates someone's family background and social class but also the choices they take daily, could assume the shape of a prejudice-based system. As a solution, privacy protocols should be taken seriously to ensure this technology is deployed correctly. Otherwise, we might be creating a tool for everyone to silently and secretly monitor each other, thus producing a society without the need for police officers; everyone polices each other. 

# Future Perspectives

By combining distinct ratings with artificial intelligence, social-score programs could have a profound impact on how society behaves both online and offline. Algorithms could autonomously improve themselves by generating their own parameters to define an upstanding citizen accurately. Because these algorithms learn in probabilistic terms, a new type of society could emerge; frowning upon harmful digital behavior. This technological development could either help citizens achieve optimal citizenship scores or lead to ostracism and, ultimately, exile.

Different surveillance systems could immediately flag citizens with low scores, following them more closely than citizens with high scores. Any misbehavior, no matter the severity, would be noted and immediately punished with the help of robot police audits. Finally, instead of exclusively relying on data collected from digital services, live conversations could be scored from microphones scattered across the city.  

These negative aspects could be exacerbated through deep-learning techniques, bringing other complex layers to the subject. In essence, machines embedded with sensors capable of reading people's micro expressions and intentions could rate citizens by their most profound psychological aspects.

Any misbehavior, no matter the severity, would be noted and immediately punished with the help of robot police audits. Finally, instead of exclusively relying on data collected from digital services, live conversations could be scored from microphones scattered across the city.

These negative aspects could be exacerbated through deep-learning techniques, bringing other complex layers to the subject. In essence, machines embedded with sensors capable of reading people's micro expressions and intentions could rate citizens by their most profound psychological aspects.

description.shortText: A driverless vehicle, fully automated in all conditions. It has no steering wheels and pedals and does not require any human control to operate.
description.longText:
A vehicle that does not require any human control to operate. It could take a passenger to any chosen destination by itself. Embedded with different sensors and connected to an integrated digital system, it would monitor and maneuver through all types of road conditions. Unlike the highly automated self-driving vehicle, it would not be restricted to geo-fenced locations, thus eliminating the need for a steering wheel and pedals. Regarding exceptional situations, this vehicle would have a series of emergency features and safety protocols, being able to communicate with the other riders using vehicle-vehicle communication software.

This type of vehicle, considered level five of automation, is currently being used, at a trial phase, in situations such as robotic taxis service. For these vehicles to move into mass production and adoption, it would be necessary to have a legislative structure, which is yet to be addressed. Self-driving vehicles might be a very efficient application of AI technology. However, they still face significant challenges: the unpredictable behavior of humans, for instance, could convert these cars into a threat to people. Although most of the technological capacity is already available to project an artificially intelligent vehicle and many prototypes are being manufactured, due to the regulations regarding safety, these cars might still be years away from being implemented. 

# Future Perspectives

With the existence of fully automated vehicles, driver's licenses would no longer be part of our world. Therefore, it would enable many people who are not capable of driving to have the chance to become more independent as they move around the city.  Also, some types of workers and professionals would have their time spared to undertake work-related activities while commuting, such as having quick meetings or catching up with emails and messages. 

Besides that, the implementation of fully autonomous cars could as well make roads safer and mitigate the traffic. Parking spaces, from houses with garages to whole buildings that today are projected to be parking lots, would no longer be necessary. Driverless cars could as well play a significant role in architectural shifts in the urban environment, such as eliminating the need to have a personal car, thus directly influencing a city's traffic.

description.shortText: Aquatic uncrewed vehicles designed to clean up waste and pollution as well as logging real-time water quality data. They float on the surface of the water, scooping up litter, biomass, microplastics, and other detritus.
description.longText:
Drones equipped with a floating structure used in aquatic settings for monitoring, collecting real-time water quality data, and cleaning up waste and pollution in water bodies. These uncrewed vehicles are equipped with LiDAR to avoid collisions from up to 60 meters away, along with IoT sensors for measuring factors such as temperature, pH, depth, and green algae. Also, together with GPS waypoints and autonomous software, aquatic drones can follow set pathways, which can be selected according to currents and tide pools, floating on the water's surface, scooping up litter, biomass, microplastics, and other detritus. 

Current models resemble a small catamaran with a sieve-like basket underneath and are powered by a lithium-ion battery that can last up to 10 hours. The drones’ capacity for autonomous operation is improving, as the vehicle is still human-supervised. Velocity and steering are preprogrammed and performed autonomously by the drone, but whenever abnormal circumstances occur, operators are required to control the vehicle. Currently, aquatic drones are used in urban settings and more stable waterbodies or slow-moving currents such as canals, ports, rivers, and lakes.

# Future Perspectives
With 5G and more powerful computing capacity, aquatic drones could be grouped to swarm, collect water-quality data, and maritime life information in a holistic approach. They could also be used around off-shore platforms to supervise activities around the premises and warn the operation centers when incidents take place. In the future, they could also be solar-powered or propelled by organic batteries, thus avoiding any toxic waste to spill into the water. 

Moreover, with the evolution of the integrated sensing technology, in the future, aquatic drones will be capable of real-time recognizing micro-concentrations of specific chemicals, such as algae toxins, and identify their source based on the diffusion pattern of these chemicals in the water, potentially allowing the exploration of novel substances for the pharmaceutical and the cosmetics industries.

*Photo: Mihail /  adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A method of injecting a neural implant to stimulate individual neurons to control brain activity and measure the responsive behavior.
description.longText:
A method of injecting a neural implant to stimulate individual neurons to control brain activity. Similar to the implantation of microchips, the fabrication begins with a dissolvable layer deposited on a biocompatible nanoscale polymer mesh substrate, with embedded nanowires, transistors and other microelectronic devices attached. The ultraflexible mesh is then tightly rolled up, allowing it to be sucked up into a syringe via a thin glass needle and subsequently injected into the brain tissue.  To achieve wireless signal transmission, injectable, magnetoelectric nanoelectrodes then wirelessly transmit electrical signals to the brain in response to an external magnetic field. In this way, individual neurons can safely be stimulated to achieve the desired the responsive behavior.

Electronic brain interfaces could lead to sophisticated and conceivable ways to treat conditions ranging from neurodegenerative disorders to paralysis. In addition, this technology would also be crucial for people with Parkinson’s,  a neurological disease that causes a group of neurons in one area of the brain to begin dying off, triggering uncontrollable tremors and shakes. By sending targeted electrical jolts to this area, it could potentially stimulate the living neurons back into activity and halt the symptoms of Parkinson’s disease. Other potential biomedical applications or therapeutic use cases include Alzheimer's Disease, epilepsy, traumatic brain injury, and other neurological/neurologically-related conditions, as well as cognition, memory, and sensorimotor disorders.

With a simple injection, specific brain regions can be targeted in a far less invasive manner than with previous methods of Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS). However, with this method, concerns remain over security, with questions raised as to whether it would be possible to hack a brain by using a mesh of conductive polymer threads with either nanoscale electrodes or transistors attached at their intersections, or hacking Bluetooth connectivity to the implants.

# Future Perspectives 
The delivery of implants via neuromorphic mesh opens up the way for new research fields such as co-injection of electronics and cells, and in future mesh electronics may also function as a tissue growth scaffold to perform regenerative medicine.
Researchers are also exploring the feasibility of implantations of mesh electronics into other tissues and organs such as in the spinal cord, in the muscle, and in the eye for in vivo recording of single retinal ganglion cells.
These methods also have potential applications in reversing or controlling aging, brain–machine interfaces, and even cyborg animals. Further, in the future, it may be possible to avert the need for injections as the field of optogenetics develops, as scientists research how light may be used to control neural circuits deep within living brain tissue, without the need for surgery.

*Photo / Illustration: © andreiuc88 / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Also known as metamaterial modeling, 4D printing is a process similar to 3D printing that precisely fabricates metamaterial objects that are able to change their shape in response to stimuli such as heat, moisture, or light.
description.longText:
4D printing is a fabrication process that, with the help of a 3D printer, constructs objects from materials such as auxetics, shape-memory polymers, and hydrogels, that fall in the category of metamaterials. Metamaterials can alter themselves in response to their post-fabrication environment, e. g., change their shape depending on their exposition to heat or cold.

This method enables the precise fabrication of dynamic structure, e. g. for the production of artificial muscles for robots, whole bodies for soft robots, or for prosthetics. Other goods manufactured in this way include flat-pack furniture, drug capsules, and cardiac stents fine-tuned to respond to body temperature.

#  Future Perspectives
The overall manufacturing sector could drastically change as 4D printing becomes cheaper and more accessible. For logistics, shape-changing packages could improve container capacity and even help deal with fragile or perishable cargo. Water management, construction, and manufacturing could benefit from responsive pieces and raise operational efficiency. In the fashion industry, 4D printing could enable designers to develop products that perfectly fit the user's body.

*Photo/illustration: JJ Ying / Unsplash*

description.shortText: Powered by VR glasses, aromatic diffusers, electrical stimulation, and special utensils, this system aims to change the human perception of portion sizes and taste by tricking the body senses into believing that the subject is immersed in a desirable dining experience.
description.longText:
By tricking the human mind with a multisensory experience, this system aims to change the perception of portion sizes and taste while enjoying food when believing that the subject is immersed, through non-invasive methods, in a desirable dining experience. One of the main applications for such devices is simulating food experiences in virtual reality with different flavor sensations overlaid by taste (via electrical stimulation on the tongue), smell (via micro air pumps), color (via RGB Lights), and thermal (via Peltier elements) sensations. The user could attend a VR dinner with friends and taste the virtual food while not consuming any calories or physical subtracts. 

A taste display in the shape of popsicles or chopsticks could artificially recreate any given flavor by electrically triggering all five taste receptors in the user's tongue. The exact flavor recipe could be downloaded and then meticulously reproduced by mixing electric currents in specific intensities. Simultaneously, a small electrode is connected to the jaw muscle, creating haptic feedback that simulates resistance, thus giving the sensation of chewing, even if the user is not eating physical and real food. In order to recreate the scent of the food, a lightweight device delivers synthetic smells, while an aromatic diffuser simulates the environment's aroma. 

A current challenge of such technology is that a recipe would need to be carefully broken into its chemical components to be replicated by the wearable device. Properties like the exact amount of umami and sweet flavors, or the precise texture of each recipe, for example, would need to be transferred to the device. 

# Future Perspectives

The implementation of such a system is expected to play a pivotal role in helping people with weight management, diabetes, and allergies. It would support them in eating whatever they want while not being affected by their dietary restrictions. It could also be helpful as a treatment in cases of food compulsion disorders, in which the patient could fulfill the urge for food with no consequences.

Furthermore, this method of food hacking could be applied to issues ranging from dietary restrictions to reducing the environmental footprint of food production by helping consumers switch to more sustainable options.

*Photo / Illustration: © Mediteraneo / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A protocol that uses the power of crowd data to forecast and predict events by allowing the buying and selling of shares in a specific outcome.
description.longText:
A speculative market where participants trade information. Investors, in this environment, bet on the outcomes of future events. Smart investors will do their research, experts will weigh in, and insiders on the subject will bet on the most likely outcome. Thus, prediction markets serve as aggregators of information. 

The model works on the principle that the wisdom of the crowds will always be superior to the data known to only a few experts. As opinions are tokenized or used as stakes, they require more foundation, thus creating a more rational logic than mere beliefs or feelings. By financially incentivizing individuals to share their knowledge on the market, more deliberate insights into social, industrial, and political trends can be generated. 

Today, most prediction market platforms are centralized and have limitations, including local regulations, owners’ reluctance to list specific contracts, trust in the operator of the platform, and the payment of additional fees for the ability to make use of their services. By replacing this process with a decentralized or distributed blockchain-based solution, many benefits are delivered, such as censorship-resistance, a reduced number of intermediaries, and increased accessibility. 

A decentralized prediction market is harder to shut down, either by governments or malicious actors. On blockchain, every node on the network runs the code, and smart contracts are built to a certain standard. No user would be able to edit or delete the programs that underpin the market. Also, blockchain doesn’t require administrators or intermediaries and is outsourced to automated codes, meaning that they don’t pay fees to a third party. 

In order to determine which outcome has occurred at the time of expiry, a truth mechanism is put in place. Since the blockchain and smart contracts cannot access off-chain data, such as if the outcome happened or not, the concept of blockchain oracle was introduced. They are third-party services that serve as bridges between blockchains and the outside world. A blockchain oracle could be linked to a third-party website or feed, however misinformation or media manipulation could undermine the essence of the blockchain. Another option is to financially incentivize users to truthfully report on events, by implementing staking mechanisms, which require users to put forward tokens to become reporters in that dynamic. If they report correctly, they are rewarded, if not, they will lose their stake.
The decentralization of this concept enhances its potential as a prediction tool. Also, as more capable oracles are advanced, blockchain technology could host provably fair code that cannot be tampered with. 

# Future Perspectives

Before the launch of the blockchain, economist Robin Hanson suggested a democratic model based on prediction markets known as Futarchy. He claimed this could be a democratic tool in which elected officials could define measures of national wellbeing to determine which policies would have the most positive effect. If implemented in the blockchain, this could bring a new narrative to democracy, with more participation from the people. However, some issues we face today might still occur in this model, such as media manipulation, lobbying, and majoritarian democracy. Still, Blockchain Prediction Markets could have a significant influence on trends forecast across different markets, as it excels at amassing and representing information in a decentralized and trustless manner.

description.shortText: AI software that supports legal prosecutions by automatically detecting and enforcing sentences. The Internet of Things would feed nearly unhackable data into the system to ensure informed decision-making while addressing law-breaking.
description.longText:
AI software that supports legal prosecution by automatically detecting and enforcing sentences, using historical data and harm assessment algorithms to analyze criminal databases. This software is fed with data derived from CCTV cameras and surveillance biometric recognition systems. The data is then turned into evidence, thus helping provide educational insights, enforce penalties for convicted criminals, or issue automatic fines and tickets. The algorithms could also be trained to give offenders a score to categorize the severity of their unlawful act. 

Different studies have proven that the information gathered by those devices could be used for criminal assessment, and function as a significant deterrent for bad behavior. The resulting predictions from these algorithms could help in pretrial, parole, and sentencing decisions. As automation takes over the judiciary and police systems, resources could be used more efficiently while saving capital. 

Private institutions could also use this technological solution by accessing and editing a cloud-based database. Establishments could share real-time CCTV camera content with the cloud for the system to analyze and send instant alerts whenever an intruder enters the establishment. The user can also alert the community at large when a crime occurs, adding images of the suspect(s) to watchlists and criminal databases.

However, this type of AI usage is subject to criticism because it could be used to reinforce societal biases. Solutions created to avoid algorithmic prejudices range from eliminating offensive and prejudicial content — usually designed under white-male perspectives — from algorithmic structures, to hiring a diverse team of developers consisting of minority groups. 


# Future Perspectives 

As judiciary systems around the world begin to see the potential of connected devices and artificial intelligence, surveillance and the usage of algorithms may become mandatory to keep the peace and keep criminals off the streets. Although the debate on issues of privacy, reinforcing bias and stereotypes continues, these subjects may be harder to justify, given the myriad of evidence and peace of mind that this technology could achieve. In the case of a private shared database, any user could be able to add a subject to the "criminal" list, thus creating a scenario of peer-based vigilance, in which every citizen is a node in a surveillance state.

*Photo/Illustration: Leszek / adobe.stock.com*
