description.shortText: An interface that transmits messages without generating audible sounds by picking up on nerve signals sent to the vocal cords, analyzing and translating them into messages that can be delivered to other recipients.
description.longText:
When words are silently “said” inside the head (a process called subvocalization), the brain triggers microscopic reactions in the muscled used to produce speech. Since the myoelectric signals emitted by these muscles are highly individual to each person, it is very difficult to detect and interpret them for the recognition of the words spoken internally. 

Powered with a machine learning system base on an artificial neural network that needs to be re-trained for each user, electrodes contained in wearables would detect neuromuscular signals and recognize what the user has “said”. The muscular activity in the jaw and face would transmit internal verbalizations, undetectable to the human eye, and this device would interpret the subvocal signals to identify which words the user had in mind.  

Once trained, this technological solution has a variety of applications. Looking up information on a smartphone during conversations requires shifting one's attention from the conversation to the handheld device, for instance. By using a voiceless speech interface, these interactions could be drastically simplified, allowing the user to interact with their personal assistant by silently voicing commands without having to leave the context of the original conversation.

Furthermore, it could allow voice communication in high-noise environments, such as the flight deck of an aircraft carrier, in power plants, near printing presses, or at other loud manufacturing facilities. Conversely, in silent settings or places with possible eavesdroppers such as during a military operation, voiceless communication could replace forms of silent communication such as hand gestures. In healthcare, speech could be restored to people unable to vocalize. In extended reality, these sensors could give a voice to virtual avatars of people with speaking disabilities.

# Future Perspectives

The added convenience of this technology also comes with a substantial risk of intrusiveness. Is it vital to have electrodes reading human thoughts while grocery shopping? Invasion of privacy could become a concern and require a whole new set of policies designed to protect mental secrecy. 

The implementation of such a system could be an important step towards achieving a transhuman body with seamless interaction with the Internet. It would be a step towards a more general brain-computer interface.

By using a voiceless speech interface, these interactions could be drastically simplified, allowing the user to interact with their personal assistant by silently voicing commands without having to leave the context of the original conversation.

Furthermore, it could allow voice communication in high-noise environments, such as the flight deck of an aircraft carrier, in power plants, near printing presses, or at other loud manufacturing facilities. Conversely, in silent settings or places with possible eavesdroppers such as during a military operation, voiceless communication could replace forms of silent communication such as hand gestures. In healthcare, speech could be restored to people unable to vocalize. In extended reality, these sensors could give a voice to virtual avatars of people with speaking disabilities.

Future Perspectives

The added convenience of this technology also comes with a substantial risk of intrusiveness. Is it vital to have electrodes reading human thoughts while grocery shopping? Invasion of privacy could become a concern and require a whole new set of policies designed to protect mental secrecy.

The implementation of such a system could be an important step towards achieving a transhuman body with seamless interaction with the Internet. It would be a step towards a more general brain-computer interface.

description.shortText: A nano-scale tagging system used both to track cells in the human organism and to monitor commercial items along production and distribution chains. It is also being used in nature to supervise wildlife on land, in the air or water.
description.longText:
For many global industries and government regulators, counterfeiting and contamination remain top concerns, with public health implications and a substantial economic impact at stake. As a solution, nano-scale tagging systems could be used to monitor and tag various items, improving supply chain efficiency while making it easier to track assets and general-purpose compliance applications.

These nanotags can take shape as nanogel marking or synthetic DNA coated with silica. Luminescent proteins could also be used to respond to microbes, allowing easy and obvious detection of contamination. This tagging system would react to chemicals, pathogens, and toxins present in goods, thus helping enhance the item's monitoring process throughout the production and distribution chains. Once applied, nanotags cannot be replaced or removed from the product, and, they do not alter the color, flavor, or texture. 

The data collected through nanotags could enhance consumer awareness, such as in cosmetics, when buyers can access the current condition of a given product, for example, a defacto updated expiration date. Also, this technology can help companies better manage their goods and systems, increasing productivity and efficiency, as well as bringing economic benefits to both farmers and retailers while improving product quality and prices for consumers. In the healthcare industry, for instance, applying multimodal nanoimaging agents in the human body would enable noninvasive, quantitative, and longitudinal stem cell tracking. In this process, labeled stem cells are injected into an injured muscle and then tracked by an imaging system. 

Today, this technology is being used to observe and track wildlife, such as birds, bats, giant insects, and fish. This data can give insights on migration patterns to help find more suitable locations for wind turbines and other buildings. There is also a potential use to monitor pets and livestock for the early detection of zoonotic diseases.

# Future Perspectives

In the future, nanotagging is expected to help researchers identify patterns of hundreds of molecules that form molecular signatures for different applications. It offers innovative solutions that one day may include connective features like with the Internet of Things applications. Furthermore, it could help raise the awareness level of ethical marketplaces and encourage their managers and owners to crack down on intellectual property abuse.

As countries increasingly grow adverse to agrochemicals, nanotags will make it easier for inspectors to identify if molecules have been altered or were subject to prohibited substances. Such tags could become a mandatory practice to facilitate the work of some regulatory bodies inspecting goods.

*Photo/Illustration: Dmytro Sukharevskyi / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: An alternative consensus algorithm to the Proof-of-Work model. It relies on market incentives instead of computing power to verify transactions, thus reducing energy consumption and improving safety in a more accessible and decentralized blockchain.
description.longText:
An alternative consensus algorithm to the Proof-of-Work (PoW) model which relies on market incentives instead of computing power to verify transactions, thus reducing energy consumption and improving safety in a more accessible and decentralized blockchain. To build trust, participants put down a deposit or stake an amount of cryptocurrency, in exchange for the right to add blocks to the blockchain. In the Proof-of-Stake model, there are no miners, but validators who mint or forge new blocks, a different method from the Proof-of-Work system.

While these types of networks have yet to be tested at scale, the PoS model is attractive and promising. It is substantially less computationally expensive to set up a node than its PoW counterpart and addresses the economic and ecological costs of mining. Besides, it provides increased protection from a malicious attack on the network. Executing an attack would be much more expensive, and there are reduced incentives for an attack: the attacker would need to own a near majority of all Bitcoin (or any system). Therefore, the attacker would suffer severely from their attack.


# Future Perspectives

Early advantages of deploying blockchains reliant on PoS would include enhanced network security combined with improved energy efficiency. Improvements in the speed of blockchain consensus algorithms could have broad implications for the types of applications that could run on the network. Particularly promising is the Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) system, which operates somewhat like a representative democracy and uses real-time voting combined with a social system of reputation to achieve consensus.

*Photo/Illustration:  Vadym / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Using genome editing technologies such as CRISPR/Cas9, it is possible to provide a cheap and easy way to modify the genes of any organism, including plants that contain allergens, as is the case for peanuts and wheat.
description.longText:
Using genome editing technologies such as CRISPR/Cas9, it is possible to provide a cheap and easy way to modify the genes of any organism, including plants that contain allergens, as is the case for peanuts and wheat. Scientists have been tweaking the genes for the proteins linked to the causes of peanut allergies in order to create an allergy-free version of the snack.

At the same time, other researchers are working on projects to edit wheat and other related cereals in order to make them gluten-free, helping people that face issues with the autoimmune condition celiac disease. When removing 90% of the gliadins in wheat, scientists are able to trigger a process called RNA interference, responsible for stopping specific proteins from being made.

Food allergies are a major health concern in industrialized countries. Reduction of allergens in foods, either by food processing or genetic engineering are strategies to minimize the risk of adverse reactions for food allergic patients. 


# Future Perspectives

In the future, it is expected that other plants could be edited in order to help people with other particular allergies and intolerances such as the Oral Allergy Syndrome, also known as pollen-food syndrome, which triggers an allergic reaction to certain proteins in a variety of fruits, vegetables and nuts. The same principle could be applied to livestock, especially considering people allergic to seafood.

description.shortText: A headband that applies a small electric current to the brain in order to stimulate the users' neural activity.
description.longText:
Through a neuropriming headset, small electric currents would be applied directly to the brain, improving the users' learning ability by creating and reinforcing neural pathways while the wearer is performing physical training or learning educational inputs. Although aiding the user to learn new skills is the most widespread use of such a device, it could also be targeted to reduce depression, alleviate the symptoms of anxiety or help the user to sleep better.

After studies showed that weak currents positioned on the motor cortex could increase motor learning in humans, such a device has become especially popular among athletes and people seeking to improve their physical abilities. When tested by Olympic athletes, this technology helped enhance their performance, accelerating the motor skills' learning process and allowing them to achieve their desired results while doing less than the necessary training. The military, for instance, could use this headband to increase accuracy and reaction times during the training of special-forces snipers and fighter pilots. Also, some studies have shown that using the headband may improve other learning skills such as acquiring a new language, playing musical instruments, and solving physics problems. 

The sensation of using such a device varies according to the users. From a disturbing ticklish sensibility to feeling nothing at all, it depends on the intensity of the electrical current and the part of the brain that receives stimulation. Some experts argue that this technology still needs some clinical trials to check the long-term effects, which are unknown since the technology is still emerging. However, if tests keep registering the same efficient outcomes, this technology will likely be widely distributed throughout the market, not only for athletes or scientists wanting to improve their skills but also for the overall population.  

# Future Perspectives

Beyond unlocking novel and unseen human cognitive abilities, this technology could increase the possibility of "hyper learning" to become a reality for those who could not afford to do so. However, it could also awake reproachable opinions comparable to those of the anabolic supplements because these devices would be used to take advantage of those who do not have access to this technology. Therefore, regulatory boards would find it hard to establish a rule direction that crosscuts all layers underlying competition and learning between humans. Besides, the long-term use of such devices, especially on children, could have undesired outcomes, like increasing their sensitivity to negative emotions.

*Photo / Illustration: © andreaobzerova / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Mobile micro-gardens designed to produce vegetables, fruits, roots, and herbs in reduced spaces, indoors or outdoors.
description.longText:
A climate-controlled agricultural unit, the size of a shipping container, able to grow all sorts of food for small-scale cafeterias, restaurants, or bars. The self-contained farms allow small scale producers to grow a variety of items on-site and offer some of the freshest options possible. 

Microculture gardens could be a useful resource for producing a broad range of plant species, including leafy vegetables, fruits, root vegetables, herbs, and more. By shortening the distances between producers and consumers, prices would decrease, as shipping would get significantly cheaper. This farming solution could occupy viable spaces throughout urban communities with small-scale, self-sustaining food forests.

This solution is designed to use less than one meter of space and could be constructed using re-purposed or up-cycled materials. The materials and designs would provide modularity, mobility, and easy replicability. Microculture gardens could also be used to feed isolated groups of people, like maritime crew members or even astronauts, while in missions. 

# Future Perspectives

Low-income neighborhoods that often lack access to healthy food could benefit by having their communities surrounded by microculture gardens that provide fresh produce throughout the year. By letting communities manage their micro-gardens autonomously, they could not only offer self-sufficiency but also an income source as cultivated food could be sold.

*Photo/Illustration: smspsy / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Attention could be tokenized in the blockchain distributed ledger to reward users for watch-time or time spent online. The system works by transferring micropayments for each advert seen by a user.
description.longText:
In the attention economy, the time people spend consuming digital content is perceived and valued as a commodity. Companies, brands, and publishers are thus continuously battling over engagement. Current technologies can measure how much time is spent on a particular website, video, audio, game or application. With blockchain-based platforms, users could be rewarded directly by the advertisers with micropayments in cryptocurrencies, or tokens, for each advert seen, in a consensual manner. 

At the moment, this can be done by browsing through unique blockchain-based browsers, which uses the same technology to measure watch-time or time spent. This process cuts the need for a middleman, makes more efficient adverts, guarantees transparency and data safety through a cryptographic ledger, and avoids bot fraud. Tokens acquired might be used to reward online creators for their content, creating a possible new monetization model for this and other kinds of virtual work.

Still, as efficient as it may sound, the process of capitalizing attention is heatedly debated, especially now that this technological solution is gaining popularity. When attention is used as a currency, it is hard to leverage if the digital content seen by the user is something they are in fact, interested in. The act of using adverts that employ psychological strategies to catch the user's attention ensuring they spend more time online than they usually would, remains to be discussed. This should be set at the forefront of the debate, mainly because the field of user experience is profoundly based on this premise. Solutions range from offering the users a wage while engaging online to benefits in digital services.

# Future Perspectives

With eye-trackers, it would be possible to measure exactly where users are looking at any given time for a more accurate attention measure. Paired with biometric and brain sensors, emotional responses could also be rewarded. Also, as extended (virtual, mixed or augmented) worlds become more present in our lives, our attention could be measured closely with sensors in our phones, glasses, and other wearables. With these blockchain-based attention tokens, attention key performance indicators such as time-spent and watch time could be rewarded directly to users, disrupting the currently popular advertising-based model of the giant technology platforms.

description.shortText: By bestowing trash with value, communities could build incentives to significantly reduce the quantity of waste carted away to landfills. Collectors could convert plastic waste into cash or other assets, such as food, fuel, schooling, public transportation, or mobile phone charging vouchers.
description.longText:
Plastic waste is now so ubiquitous in our environment that it has even been suggested it could serve as a geological indicator of the Anthropocene era. Rather than viewing it as garbage, organizations are starting to empower local communities by paying them to collect waste and bring it to collection centers, a business model commonly known as 'waste as a currency.' In this model, plastic waste is processed into pellets and sold to companies above market value as a recycled raw material.

Collectors could convert plastic waste into cash or other goods, such as food, fuel, or vouchers for schooling, public transportation, or mobile phone charging. Some initiatives use a blockchain-based banking system to convert the weight of plastic into an online token accepted in several local businesses and services. Also, urban recycling platforms are starting to use digital currencies to reward good behavior, paying users for properly separating recyclables. Rewards can include discounts and other bonuses at local businesses in the neighborhood.

This system stimulates growth by encouraging collectors and citizens to become small-scale entrepreneurs and is highly desirable in sustainability terms. It acts as a closed-loop system that directly recycles the waste it creates. Further, by offering unskilled workers the chance to improve their household incomes, inequalities may decrease while reducing the demand for the production of new plastic.

# Future Perspectives
Consumers are becoming increasingly aware of how their habits impact the environment, to the point some brands started to accept waste as a form of payment. By taking waste as a currency for goods to enhance positive perceptions, it allows previously wasteful brands to align themselves with eco-conscious customers. Additionally, by bestowing trash with value, companies are building incentives that should significantly reduce the quantity of waste sent to landfills.

Geopolitical problems could emerge from this type of currency if it becomes too widespread and accepted as a commodity. Corrupt governments, for example, could start to produce waste as a means of accumulating the reward that comes from it or incentivizing entire communities to make as much trash as possible. Although, with the constant evolution of remanufacturing techniques, the overproduction of waste could become a means to support these initiatives and further counteract the possible threats coming from corruption.

description.shortText: Railway sleepers, made of recycled plastic, able to generate kinetic energy. This railroad material has a longer lifespan, reduced maintenance costs, vibrations, and noise.
description.longText:
With the same mechanical characteristics as traditional reinforced concrete sleepers, railway energy harvesting can generate and transmit the kinetic energy from the motion produced by trains. Made from recycled plastic, this energy harvesting and storage solution can decrease power consumption, maintenance costs, and increase train services security. Current models have sensors embedded into the platform, used to measure and monitor the performance of the railway system. 

Energy can be harvested more efficiently from two different primary sources, such as vibration or solar. Both options are incredibly efficient and clean. One is based on harvesting, recovering, and recycling track vibration. The second one only requires photovoltaic panels to enable renewable energy harvesting. As it made of a recycled by-product, this solution is low-cost and easy to be implemented in current railway infrastructure. 

# Future Perspectives 

Transport represents a high share of greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution. With the global shift towards a low-carbon, circular economy already underway, improving energy efficiency in the sector has become paramount. In the coming years, AI usage in the industry holds massive potential to better understand and improve railway logistics. From traction to infrastructure, all railway elements necessary for trains to operate will work on a zero-emission basis.

*Photo/Illustration: den-belitsky /  adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Clustered Regularly-Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) is a genome-editing technique generated through precise editing of an organism's native genome, even in DIY settings.
description.longText:
Clustered Regularly-Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) is a technique to achieve precise, literal cut-and-paste addition/subtraction of genomes. It relies on two major components: the Cas9 protein that can cut DNA, and the use of a guide RNA, capable of recognizing the sequence of the DNA string that can be edited.  

This technology makes it possible to edit genomes by either modifying, deleting, or inserting new sequences to rewrite DNA. The pivotal point involves altering original base pair arrangements within the genome of an organism, without the need to introduce foreign genetic material from another organism.

CRISPR is more agile and accurate than previous or competing models of genetic editing. It opens up a vast range of opportunities that include editing allergens in peanuts, creating mushrooms that do not brown or even breeding genetically-engineered mosquitoes that cannot transmit diseases such as malaria. 

By using CRISPR to finely control the activity of specific genes, we can better understand how organic bodies naturally carry out the same process. In terms of human system trials, researchers in China have been looking into editing human cells to create cancer-fighting white blood cells that could be injected into patients or babies vulnerable to HIV. However, despite the infinite possibilities for CRISPR, there are still crucial ethical and moral implications that arise as significant challenges and issues to be discussed, especially regarding the alteration of the human genome. We might have to decide which genes are subject to editing, and which traits are prohibited from being edited in an embryo.

On the other hand, CRISPR CAS9 technology has become a promising alternative for crop improvement. As the world's population is expected to grow substantially in the following decades, maximizing the yield productivity without increasing the environmental impact is one of the many excitement possibilities of CRISPR. Besides, society at large seems more open to CRISPR compared to other techniques like in the case of genetically transformed organisms, also referred to as GMOs, which have experienced intense public backlash.

In addition, it is possible to manipulate a new generation of fish species as a means of creating directional breeding. For example, catfish had its genome sequence 99.7% assessed, making it possible to change their performance traits by manipulating their microRNAs. Some additional features include phenotypic variations to make catfish more resistant to diseases, heat stress, hypoxia, and even reduce their head size.

# Future Perspectives

Although CRISPR is currently used in very targeted manners, for example, by developing new model systems or by stimulating the effect of treatments using genetic editing, there is still a lot to be discovered in terms of side-effects and reversibility. Scientists have been looking into the consequences of this gene-editing technique, especially given the fact that it may be impossible to reverse or turn off these edits. 

Apart from safety risks, human genome editing poses some massive moral questions. It could offer a chance to edit harmful mutations, but for those living in poverty, genome editing could be used as one more tool for the privileged to vault ahead. Bioethics is currently debating how and where it is mandatory to trace a line within disease treatment and human enhancement to combat the creation of genetic disparities.

Taking this technology one step further, scientists are even considering bringing back extinct species such as the woolly mammoth with the use of the same technology. By following the same concept, companies are testing age-reversal technologies in human clinical trials, the combination of which could extend lifespans by a decade or more. One day it may be possible to eliminate the negative features of aging, erase wrinkles, and potentially wipe out age-related diseases.

description.longTextHtml:
Clustered Regularly-Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) is a technique to achieve precise, literal cut-and-paste addition/subtraction of genomes. It relies on two major components: the Cas9 protein that can cut DNA, and the use of a guide RNA, capable of recognizing the sequence of the DNA string that can be edited.

This technology makes it possible to edit genomes by either modifying, deleting, or inserting new sequences to rewrite DNA. The pivotal point involves altering original base pair arrangements within the genome of an organism, without the need to introduce foreign genetic material from another organism.

CRISPR is more agile and accurate than previous or competing models of genetic editing. It opens up a vast range of opportunities that include editing allergens in peanuts, creating mushrooms that do not brown or even breeding genetically-engineered mosquitoes that cannot transmit diseases such as malaria.

By using CRISPR to finely control the activity of specific genes, we can better understand how organic bodies naturally carry out the same process. In terms of human system trials, researchers in China have been looking into editing human cells to create cancer-fighting white blood cells that could be injected into patients or babies vulnerable to HIV. However, despite the infinite possibilities for CRISPR, there are still crucial ethical and moral implications that arise as significant challenges and issues to be discussed, especially regarding the alteration of the human genome. We might have to decide which genes are subject to editing, and which traits are prohibited from being edited in an embryo.

On the other hand, CRISPR CAS9 technology has become a promising alternative for crop improvement. As the world's population is expected to grow substantially in the following decades, maximizing the yield productivity without increasing the environmental impact is one of the many excitement possibilities of CRISPR. Besides, society at large seems more open to CRISPR compared to other techniques like in the case of genetically transformed organisms, also referred to as GMOs, which have experienced intense public backlash.

In addition, it is possible to manipulate a new generation of fish species as a means of creating directional breeding. For example, catfish had its genome sequence 99.7% assessed, making it possible to change their performance traits by manipulating their microRNAs. Some additional features include phenotypic variations to make catfish more resistant to diseases, heat stress, hypoxia, and even reduce their head size.

Future Perspectives

Although CRISPR is currently used in very targeted manners, for example, by developing new model systems or by stimulating the effect of treatments using genetic editing, there is still a lot to be discovered in terms of side-effects and reversibility. Scientists have been looking into the consequences of this gene-editing technique, especially given the fact that it may be impossible to reverse or turn off these edits.

description.shortText: Additive manufacturing used to prepare recipes with different configurations, sizes, flavors, textures, and colors.
description.longText:
By filling 3D printing machines with macronutrients such as starch, protein, and fat, recipes can be prepared with ready-to-eat, fresh food with appealing shapes and textures. The addition of flavors and smells could be programmed into recipes, as well as the precise calorie intake, opening up a variety of different possibilities for food production.

Through the combination of nozzles, powdered materials, lasers, and robotic arms, 3D food printers can make sugar sculptures, patterned chocolate, latticed pastries, or even pizza, using fresh ingredients sold in commercial kitchens, bakeries or restaurants. Nowadays, some devices already let home users manufacture healthier versions of "processed" foods that are similar to those made by mass producers, but with ingredients using less salt, oil, and fewer artificial additives. In another example, a 3D printer could contain vegetable cells that could be printed directly into a living vegetable tissue, creating a fresh artificial salad.

Within the context of healthcare, printed food allows for better control of nutritional content. Users could formulate dishes that better suit their dietary needs, and would only print what they are going to eat, thus helping avoid food waste. This appliance has the potential to decrease food production costs and help combat food shortages. 3D food printing could also be seen as a potential solution for bringing fresh, made-on-site food on space exploration missions.

# Future Perspectives

Experts believe that hydrocolloids, or substances that form gels with water, could then be used to replace the base ingredients of familiar dishes with plentiful renewables like algae, duckweed, and grass. For that, scientists are researching a printing method that could use microalgae, a natural source of protein, carbohydrates, pigments, and antioxidants. In times of food scarcity, the shape, smell, and texture will count more than the actual ingredients that have been used to provide the right amount of nutrients, and calories for basic intake.

description.shortText: A soft, amorphous robot that can identify microscopic or macroscopic harm and self-heal autonomously.
description.longText:
A soft robot made of synthetic polymers, powered with sensors able to identify damages and autonomously decide how to recover performance. The robot senses macroscopic and microscopic injuries and acts to fix them, restoring initial functions, and returning to action. These sensing and self-healing elements increase a robot's lifespan. This feature also decreases human labor and costs, reducing the need for preventive checks, corrective maintenance, and repair costs.

Mounted on AI-based software, the soft robot can measure and report its activity, thus providing insights about spotted vulnerabilities. Also, as the software creates patterns of previous incidents, the robot can warn about activities prone to risks and avoid accidents to both robots and humans working on a factory floor.

# Future Perspectives

Thanks to its autonomous self-repairing nature, this robot can be deployed to perform long-term activities in places where humans cannot access, like rescue areas or locations with extreme weather conditions. They could also be used in outer space as builders of an interstellar community.

*Photo: Vladislav Ociacia / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Geofencing applied for educational and training purposes, segmenting specific content, and informative communication based on students' current location.
description.longText:
A location-based education service in which an app or other software uses GPS, RFID, Wi-Fi or cellular data provides on-the-spot information for users when a mobile device or RFID tag enters or leaves a certain geographical location defined by virtual boundaries, also known as a geofence. Geofencing is a business model widely used for marketing campaigns. It targets individuals based on their current location, and when applied for education, this model helps students and trainees to explore their learning environment while simultaneously targeting a specific audience, for example during recruitment fairs, community college transfer days, at local businesses, on-campus events, and more. It can also notify users about detailed historical information from sites around the city or warn students of spreading health issues on and off-campus.

With the spread of mobile devices, location-based learning offers other educational purposes outside of campus or company contexts. With data aggregated distinguished zones, geofencing apps could send notifications to users with content regarding the area they enter, serving as a virtual tour guide. It also serves as a cultural heritage platform, educating tourists as well as the local community about a particular region. In a regional education program for farmers, educational content about various crops is segmented in different dialects, offering the possibility to switch languages depending on the area. 

# Future Perspectives
With the emergence of satellite internet reaching remote locations and smartphone accessibility growing, this could be an essential tool for contextual and spatial education across the world. With augmented reality glasses, geofencing could help with content segmentation for ultra-specific locations, overlaying educational information for any person who enters the premise.

*Photo/Illustration: Andrey Popov /  adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A cyber-defense strategy where fake persona decoys are used to entrap and deceive attackers who use social engineering as a strategy.
description.longText:
Social engineering involves gaining access to buildings, systems, or data by exploiting human psychology, as opposed to gaining access through software or network vulnerabilities. In its current form, social engineering is time-consuming for the attacker. However, it is the hardest form of attack to defend against since it cannot be prevented with hardware or software alone. Even with rock-solid security systems, companies are still vulnerable to attacks that exploit the human element. 

Merely securing the company’s network is not enough; as such, employers have focused prevention efforts primarily on increasing user awareness through training and implementation of broad security policies. However, the simple adoption of security standards does not guarantee security, and new employees who may not undergo the necessary training could be specifically targeted.

A honeypot is an intriguing computer security mechanism that imitates existing infrastructure to trap attackers and learn their behavior. For social engineering defense, a so-called “social honeypot” involves creating fake users on social-media websites or fake employees in the company database. By acting as a decoy user, they try to entrap attackers. Since all communication with the honeypot is entirely unsolicited, there is a high chance of the initial contact being spam or an attack. 

When the honeypot receives a message, the profile and social details of the sender are harvested, and machine learning with statistical analysis is used to classify whether the sender is malicious or benign. The result of this classification is automatically propagated to the devices of all real employees, which will then automatically block further communication attempts from the offending party. Since potential attackers directly target honeypots, they do not need to intercept external communication channels and, therefore, do not interfere with the privacy of employee communications.
 
# Future Perspectives
Social honeypots could be connected with automated data theft detection systems, which would continuously monitor covert channels such as the deep web. If the honeypot’s fake personal details are detected, this could alert the organization to the existence of a potentially undetected large-scale data leak.

In the future, hackers could even be able to automate social engineering. The only way to defend users would be to create sophisticated automated security mechanisms, taking the security arms race out of the domain of system admins versus hackers and into the field of artificial intelligence versus artificial intelligence. Machine learning would allow attackers to automatically create convincing fake personas, able to interact with their victims through conversation. 

At the same time, creating fake social honeypots and their corresponding social media presence could also become automated, and like chatbots, they would interact with their attackers. The result would be to have two artificially intelligent personas trying to convince each other of being a real person. An exciting variation of the Turing test, but without humans.

description.shortText: The combination of the Internet of things, sensors, the blockchain, and real-time monitoring could help track products, and provide a full-service solution for farmers as well as consumers to help avoid waste and food loss throughout the supply chain.
description.longText:
Pinpointing the primary sources of food waste at restaurants, hospitals, schools, houses, and other buildings may be the first step to recapturing or saving millions of uneaten and wasted food products around the world. Implementing a software platform that tracks food inventory, records purchasing and expiration dates as well as the reason for discarding food could help detect weak points in the established product journeys. Touchscreens and other easy-to-use interfaces could further facilitate the adoption of this type of technology by allowing employees, cooks, and other personnel to make instant notes about food being discarded.

Besides the intentional discarding of leftovers, there is also spoilage and loss of food during transportation from the farm to the processing factory; additionally, vegetables and fruits are typically selected (or not) solely based on visual qualities. This technology could also help avoid cases where producers have a larger supply than demand, and food ends up rotting somewhere along the supply chain. It is estimated that post-harvest waste happens partly when temperature-sensitive products are not managed correctly. To prevent this, sensors and the Internet of things could help track produce and precisely map where precisely along the chain losses take place. Additionally, they could provide information about food quality and whether discarding products, at any given stage, is essential or not.

# Future Perspectives
Together with other tools such as blockchain, it would be possible to track the origin of the food by monitoring and registering all the information that could help avoid losses along the entirety of the supply chain. Besides, software on mobile phones and smart household appliances could provide real-time information about quality, ripening stage, etc. for end consumers in their own houses or in stores.

The quantity of food wasted by citizens in both developed and developing countries is alarming, especially considering how, after a somewhat stable decline, hunger has increased again in the last decade. The recovery of food surpluses, therefore, is gaining much-needed attention, creating a market for innovative solutions based on information and communication technologies. Several mobile applications attempt to reduce domestic food waste by introducing a “food sharing” model. Current practices to recover surplus foodstuffs in consumable conditions are still unable to reach the vast majority of food waste. Effective solutions will need to integrate at different stages of the supply chain, and take into account uses besides exclusively human consumption.

description.shortText: A type of smart matter composed of submillimeter-sized nanobots that can freely change their physical properties according to software input or autonomous sensing of the surrounding environment.
description.longText:
Also known as claytronics, this class of matter comprises billions of nanorobots, each having its own sensors and acting autonomously, while communicating with others of its own kind to create larger structures. Each nanorobot is called a catom, and in theory, each catom could be as small as a single atom or even a quantum dot. A bucket of claytronic matter would have the ability to freely change its physical properties, including shape, density, conductivity, optical properties, and more. Self-assembly could be triggered by software input or by autonomous sensing of the local environment. 

Research is embedding plastic material with magnetic particles to enable it to shape-shift. Another current study uses an electrostatic actuator in each catom to control its physical shape. These are initial experiments in the promising field of claytronics. For the time being, we still need to overcome several challenges to achieve the full potential of claytronics. Technologies such as networking, cell communication, distributed control, optimization, algorithmic programming, and the broad nanotechnology field must be perfected.

# Future Perspectives 

Claytronics could be particularly useful in small environments such as spaceships or places that lack raw materials, such as newly colonized planets. The idea of manually constructing any given object could be abandoned; the items could be programmed into shape instead.

Once fully developed, this technology could have a significant impact on the economic system and resource management. For instance, every person could own a limited amount of multi-purpose matter that adapts itself according to their specific needs. By providing every catom with access to an intelligent neural network, it could be possible to create smart matters that predict and autonomously reshape itself according to its user instructions, discarding the necessity of being pre-programmed by a human.

*Photo/Illustration: VAlex / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A communication protocol for wireless communications technologies that support cellular data networks, expected to be around 1,000 times faster than 5G.
description.longText:
The sixth-generation wireless (6G) is a communication protocol for wireless technologies that could provide higher capacity and lower latency compared to 5G, possibly reaching one microsecond-latency communication, which is 1,000 times faster than one-millisecond throughput (estimated 5G cellular technology latency). It is expected to be the successor to 5G mobile networks.

6G is still in the research stages. Although scientific advances are experimenting with devices capable of operating at higher frequencies, the required high transmission speeds, the energy consumption rates, and the acceptable proportions of the related heat development in the electronic circuits are just some examples of the challenges 6G networks will face in the future. Studies estimate that 6G networks would likely operate in frequencies from 100 GHz to 3 THz due to their wide swaths of the unexplored spectrum (unused frequency waves in the electromagnetic spectrum). 

# Future Perspectives

The scientific community commonly references 6G as the "wireless cognition," an allusion to wireless networks that could allow human thoughts to move freely over the air. In the future, through the electromagnetic frequencies of 6G, remote robots and AI applications could exchange data with excellent coverage at incredible speeds. Also, the 6G frequencies would be in the sub-Terahertz bands. Hence, researchers calculate that, based on these ample bands, it could transmit super-fast computations over a wide variety of frequencies, enabling future mobile devices to have vastly more extraordinary capacities, such as human-to-machine interactions. 

*Photo/Illustration: Atik sulianami @ unsplash.com*

description.shortText: Malware and hackers targeting banks and digital services could be thwarted through a combination of online and offline security methods. Through virtualization or quantum key distribution, the protection of servers could be significantly improved.
description.longText:
Malware and hackers that target banks and digital services could be thwarted through a combination of online and offline security methods. One of the techniques with the most significant potential for security involves the isolation of a server through virtualization or quantum key distribution. As cybersecurity improves, it will become increasingly harder for fraudsters to avoid both the physical and digital barriers.

Satellite quantum key distribution is a secure process for data transfer between two computers, in which the next-generation encryption method uses laser links from satellites to transmit encryption keys, as even fiber optics are not reliable enough over such large distances. The keys are used for encryption methods such as one-time pads which have the required properties for quantum cryptography. One variant of this process uses regular transmission of photons whose quantum properties can be used to keep information hidden from any interceptor and, at the same time, can alert the communicating parties of any tampering. Another variant uses satellites to distribute pairs of entangled photons over large distances. These act as if magically connected and mimic each-others state. In this case, information can practically be teleported between the particles and this offers the highest level of security, but is difficult and costly to achieve.

For governments and defense agencies, data sovereignty is one of the most critical issues, especially as cyberwars and attacks increase annually against organizations that increasingly centralize more sensitive data. As quantum computing becomes more commonplace, conventional digital cryptography will be easier to crack, making it necessary to implement fraud-proof authentication on servers to guarantee data security against these new technological threats. Even though satellite quantum key distribution seems to be ground-breaking security innovative, the sovereignty of data creates controversy because satellites are owned and maintained by individual countries or private companies; other countries or parties would need to sign agreements to use the satellites, or could be prevented from using these secure new communication highways and become increasingly vulnerable.

# Future Perspectives

A future quantum internet would rely on a global long-distance network; innovation is leading the way for the creation of safe quantum cryptography. Satellites that transfer data with photons could travel far longer distances than fiber optics. The particles themselves cannot travel faster than light, but the information transferred between them can if they are entangled. This could open up whole new possibilities for a highly secure and almost latency-free Internet.

*Photo/Illustration: Kevin Quezada / unsplash.com*

A future quantum internet would rely on a global long-distance network; innovation is leading the way for the creation of safe quantum cryptography. Satellites that transfer data with photons could travel far longer distances than fiber optics. The particles themselves cannot travel faster than light, but the information transferred between them can if they are entangled. This could open up whole new possibilities for a highly secure and almost latency-free Internet.

description.shortText: A robust encrypted database that safely stores e-citizen data and withstands any cyberattack with the ability to reboot an entire country in an instant. Like a traditional embassy, it has sovereign rights and is located outside the state of ownership.
description.longText:
A data backup embassy is a robust encrypted database that withstands any cyberattack. It works as a storage facility that guarantees digital continuity to vast amounts of sensitive data such as medical history, social security, and corporate information. Similarly to a typical embassy that functions based on sovereign rights, it would be located outside the physical borders of the country.

In emergency cases, it could reboot an entire country in an instant, thus helping a country to overcome botnet attacks quickly with denial-of-service programming, an algorithm that prevents digital services from running. By working as a cloud-based extension of public digital services, only the physical hardware storing the database would be transnational. However, the government would continue to have complete sovereignty over the information stored inside.

Though it helps protect data against cyberattacks, the creation of a transnational database would also keep citizen data safe and accessible even in the event of an attack by a foreign military. The same protection applies to power outages, natural disasters, or any other type of calamity. With this strategy, a country could have its public services up and running again in no time. 

Currently, there are many challenges regarding how international laws could adhere to this technology. An international agreement concerning modern storage methods of government data should establish a global methodology for this technology to be deployed. It should include, especially regarding the principles of protecting public safety, individual privacy and transparency frameworks to deal with, and store sensitive data.

# Future Perspectives

To keep such an immense amount of information physically stored in the same place undoubtedly increases both the focus and intensity of cyber-attacks and data theft. The storage system could use a virtual model for data in a privately owned public cloud that could provide different functionalities, such as auto-scaling and geographically spread application instances, which could help mitigate attacks. 

If coupled with the blockchain technology, instead of securing system vulnerabilities with one or a few transnational data embassies, thousands of computers could serve together as one extensive backup database. By doing this, it would ensure the safety of not only e-citizenship data but also public services and individual user data as well.

An effective way to store such information would be through DNA-based storage systems with the capability of storing an incredible amount of data while occupying very little physical space. Although this method of storage could still be physically stolen, it would eliminate the chances of cyber-attacks; for the time being, system hacking is non-existent against DNA-storage media.

*Photo/Illustration: Sashkin / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: An energy storage solution that harvests, stores, and converts atmospheric air into potential energy. As it does not rely on natural resources besides atmospheric air to work, this solution promises both applicability and scalability. The energy container is easy to transport and cheap to replicate.
description.longText:
An energy harvester container, designed to extract, store, and convert atmospheric air into potential energy. By exposing the air to extremely low temperatures, liquid air energy storage (LAES) can transform and conserve the air in a liquified state. 

First, the air is cooled inside the equivalent of giant thermos flasks at low temperatures of around -195 degrees C. As the liquid air is stored at almost ambient pressure, the energy density becomes very high, only requiring small storage space. In order to extract energy from the storage compartments, the liquid air is exposed to the environment temperature that heats it up, returning it to a gaseous state. As liquid air is released back into a gaseous form, its expansion can power the turbines that put the energy back into the grid. 

# Future Perspectives

Long-duration energy storage solutions today usually face geographical restrictions on the amount of sunlight or wind flows that enable solar and wind power plants to function. As LAES does not rely on natural resources besides atmospheric air to work, this solution is promising both in applicability and scalability. The energy container is easy to transport and cheap to replicate. 

Current prototypes work on differing air conditions, even in more polluted or industrial areas. Accordingly, this solution shows excellent potential in generating clean energy in a reasonably effortless process and can help mitigate the effects produced by gas emissions on the atmosphere.

*Photo/Illustration: Franco Nadalin / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Deep neural networks that produce full-body renderings for varying body poses and camera positions. It could be used as a dynamic augmented reality avatar to be worn daily in virtual social interactions.
description.longText:
Deep neural networks that produce full-body renderings for varying body poses and camera positions. It could be used as a dynamic augmented reality avatar to be worn daily in virtual social interactions. It uses neural networks to synthesize video data of texturized bodies in motion. 

By training an appropriate type of neural network, e. g. a convolutional one, with videos and pictures of moving bodies in different poses, it is possible to create photorealistic animated or still figures and place them in any scenario. There is no need for the dataset to contain the exact person that will be rendered into the avatar, meaning that the same dataset can be used to create several avatars. 

In principle, the technology can use the image-to-image translation by simply processing image and video data. More recent approaches use a neural network to map 2D textures, i. e. images, to the surface of conventional, deformable 3D models. Such networks learn from image and video data, what bodies look like from certain angles and in certain lighting conditions and thus produce more realistic results than regular texturing of 3D models. Also, they produce better spatial representations than image-to-image translation, which is missing concrete 3D data. These new approaches can also change aspects of the avatar realistically, such as body weight, height, etc.

# Future Perspectives

This approach could be used to substitute actual celebrities in advertisements or movies, the artist would need to provide only some photos and the authorization to use the images. Computers could render everything else. Conversely, it could be used in malicious ways, to create full-body deep fake videos. As computer renders become indistinguishable from actual videos, the power of images and video as factual evidence might be called into question.

*Photo / Illustration: © Glebstock / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A type of crypto token that is not interchangeable or replicable. It is used to represent scarcity items in virtual environments, in which the currency is the desired item itself.
description.longText:
Commonly known as NFTs, non-fungible tokens are unique digital items that can be sold, traded, and stored within the blockchain. The name "fungible" is derived from the fungibility of exchanging physical objects without modifying their value. The creation of NFTs is a way to ensure the uniqueness of a digital asset because it cannot be replicable and copied, which creates a limited availability of a commodity. When an item is non-fungible, its value is intrinsically connected to the item itself. 

The use of non-fungible tokens within the gaming ecosystem is becoming ever more popular. It solves a fundamental problem regarding ownership of in-game goods. When a player buys an item inside a specific game, even if such an item costs money, it cannot be owned by the buyer because if the game developers decide to discontinue the platform, all in-game items will be lost. If the item is stored in the blockchain in the form of an NFT, it becomes genuinely possessed by the player, and it will continue to exist outside the game. In some cases, it is even possible to create trans-game assets. 

As NFTs represent a big market for collectible digital goods, artists are also taking advantage of NFTs to tokenize artworks to ensure ownership and distinctiveness to the pieces. Another possible use-case for such tokens is for the tokenization of physical assets, as it creates a digital counterpart of the physical good. Thanks to the immutability of blockchains, the tokenization of physical goods could be used to replace contracts automatically. 

# Future Perspectives

As we move to the digitalization of physical goods, more and more users will become familiar with new forms of buying and selling such items. Prestige items, such as luxury fragrances, will be encoded into NFT through novel artworks created from perfumes and fused to their physical counterparts. These NFTs will be part of large-scale campaigns to accompany a limited rollout of an exclusive prestige category item. Each limited edition NFT artwork works as a unique blockchain asset and the form of non-interchangeable cryptocurrency comes with a physically redeemable collector's edition version of the prestige item. Yet, for many, it can be complicated to manage several digital wallets and decentralized goods across platforms. One way to solve this challenge would be creating third parties platforms in the form of crypto banks that would help users deal, trade, and possess NFTs by making transactions frictionless.

description.shortText: By combining computational fluid dynamics with machine learning and meteorological data-sources, this system steadily improves the ability and accuracy to forecast both weather and natural incidents with far-reaching results for individuals and businesses.
description.longText:
By combining computational fluid dynamics with machine learning and meteorological data-sources, a predictive weather system provides a more accurate alternative to current weather prediction models. This dynamic and fluid forecast software aggregates a multitude of climate and weather-related data. This data is later rated, ranked, and weighted by machine learning to process immediate comparisons between historical data and weather forecasts. Used in this way, weather models could more efficiently take into account inaccuracies, such as overestimated rain predictions or even to perform more accurate predictions.

Apart from developing rankings, machine-learning models that use deep learning show promising results in predicting cyclones, atmospheric rivers, weather fronts, and forest fires, and can even assess deforestation. With better predictions of climate, it may be possible to modify decisions to decrease undesirable impacts and take better advantage of expected favorable conditions. 

Farmers, for instance, could be better prepared to make decisions regarding crop management with the inclusion of the ideal window for sowing, fertilizing, weeding, and harvesting. In the case of urban planners, simulation models can be useful to adapt both existing projects and upcoming developments in order to make them more responsive to the consequences of climate change (for instance, reducing heat islands and adaptation of areas prone to flood), as well as more accountable to the measurements and policies that regulate emissions.

# Future Perspectives

Gathering and processing high-quality data of potential environmental risks will continuously be a need for both future and present-day society. Improving accuracy in weather prediction can have far-reaching implications, not just for disaster mitigation, but also for businesses that rely on commodity futures trading or other weather-based factors. Due to the amount of data that needs to be analyzed, advancements in the quantum computing area should directly impact the accuracy of these forecasting systems.

Also, by combining this software with new infrared remote atmospheric sounding systems with cloud-penetrating microwave radiometers, space-borne radar, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), as well as remote sensing observations from the ground, it could create a sensor web around the globe for future views of the Earth. These new and improved weather and climate products are also leading to new industries, like “weather derivatives.” Weather derivatives are financial solutions that help weather-sensitive companies spread out and insure themselves against their inherent risks.

*Photo/Illustration: pictureguy32 / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A computational method that optimizes crop growth. It collects data from real crops in the field and creates a mathematical model to simulate how yields perform under any given circumstance.
description.longText:
In silico studies are computer simulations with 3D models reflecting the real world as closely as possible. Unlike digital twins, in silico designs can react to specific inputs and provide conclusions for further analysis. In silico farming is a farming ecosystem transformed into code, where planting patterns, tillage systems, sunlight and shading, water availability, microbial interactions, and many other variables are digitally tested. By modeling the coupled plant-soil atmosphere management ecosystem, the simulated spatial resolution and precision output could potentially be comparable to having a large number of physical sensors distributed in the field. 

Recently, in silico trials are being applied in crop science to monitor highly accurate digital plants to help speed up selective breeding. Accordingly, researchers can build statistical models that identify mathematical relationships using agricultural data and then create simulations based on those equations, allowing the measured traits to play out on the screen. Once they visualize the crops, scientists can manipulate the data to see which factors result in the fastest-growing, most drought-resistant, or least pest-susceptible plants possible. 

Currently, this method cannot help individual farmers to manage their operations. It is mainly used by international organizations, national governments, and multinational corporations that run what-if scenarios about climate change and agriculture policy.


# Future Perspectives
In silico farming is a bottom-up approach, meaning the process begins by simulating the properties of individual plants and then extrapolating the data and behavior to determine the yield for whole crops. Machine learning methods, on the other hand, offer a top-down approach to crop prediction. It processes data captured by drones and satellites with publicly available remote sensing data, subsequently tracking and predicting the impact of environmental factors on crops, including weather changes, soil parameters, and possible plant diseases.

The integration of top-down predictive models with bottom-up simulations at the individual plant level would make it possible to reap the best of both worlds: high spatial resolution and sound predictive forecasts for entire crops. In the future, instead of merely responding to food shortages, it could be possible to preemptively set appropriate food reserve levels, identify low-yield regions, and predict where to send food aid. If computer simulations scale up, they could boost the democratization of precision, taking mono, polyculture, and agroforestry farming to new levels.

*Photo/Illustration: zapp2photo / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A 3D-printed substance compatible with living systems. The material is printed using living cells, drastically reducing the possibility of rejection. This material could potentially become a milestone for on-demand organ printing.
description.longText:
A 3D-printed substance or structure compatible with living systems. The material is printed using living cells, drastically reducing the possibility of rejection. 

After taking samples of a patient's cells using a sophisticated 3D bioprinter that extrudes different kinds of cells at once, the printer can print new cartilage and bones or other associated tissue of a whole new organ to replace the human equivalent. Alternatively, the bioprinter extrudes a grid made of vascular human stem cells. The tissue is infused with nutrients, fluids, and cell growth factors to control stem cell differentiation and ensure the proper cell functions after the printing procedure. This process introduces vascular networks that embed blood vessels into the tissue, thus creating living complex 3D-printed systems.

With the help of 3D printing, biomaterials could be synthesized and engineered for use in living systems for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes or augmenting various natural functions. Moreover, the 3D-printed organic tissue could reduce the risk of rejection. Patients would receive a new organ from their own cells with significantly decreased inflammatory rates compared to medical procedures using non-biological materials.  This material could potentially become a milestone for on-demand organ printing.

# Future Perspectives

3D bioprinting has the potential to solve a myriad of complex problems regarding medical treatments, from creating full-grown functioning organs and limbs to augmented organs in a microchip. Moreover, bioprinting may bring novel applications in the skincare and cosmetics industry by merging functional skin layers with biological tissue particles that can be easily integrated into the skin. By adding antimicrobial and regenerative ingredients to the bioprinted material, it could bring wound-healing effects, recovering ruptured and wounded skin, or healing damage due to acne, eczema, and skin diseases.

In a more distant future, once the making of living organic parts is mastered, we may be able to design human bodies beyond only reproducing current shapes. Want a third arm or a sixth finger? Just print it.

description.shortText: Virtual reality solution designed to help surgeons visualize and interact with the anatomy of each patient prior to the surgery.
description.longText:
System that allows medical professionals to interact with patient-specific organs and tissue in an open 3D space emanating from a display. The software provides an exact replica of the patient's organ and through the use of a digital pen, the surgeon can move, dissect and manipulate it, giving the doctor a volumetric understanding of the real anatomy prior to the actual surgery and allowing an operation to be practised, and the outcome viewed, before the patient undergoes surgery.

# Future Perspectives

The solution has the potential to improve surgical planning as well as clinical efficacy. With advances in 3D printing and the incorporation of patient-specific anatomy, Virtual Simulation Surgery modernizes biomedical training, strengthening surgeons' skill sets, which could decrease hospital costs, improve patient outcomes, and may replace the need for and use of live animals in medical school curricula and skills-training programs.

description.shortText: A driverless vehicle designed to be shared by a small number of commuters, for a pleasant and less hectic ride in urban areas compared to busses or trams.
description.longText:
Shared self-driving pods that allow people to request them through a mobile app and hail them just like taxis or similar services. Like other automated driverless vehicles, they possess basic features such as vehicle-to-vehicle communication, sensors, and image processing to navigate in real-time and smoothly. They can operate on elevated or underground shuttle networks or traditional roadways.

The models being developed offer a sustainable mobility service, which uses clean energy alternatives and is battery-powered. In terms of maneuverability, they have a 360-degree steering system that enables navigation in extremely tight urban streets and parking in small places. Besides, the interior could be adjusted to fit the needs of whichever business wishes to use it, from ride sharing to food deliveries or even a mobile office space or meeting room. In general, they are higher than regular self-driving vehicles and are similar to busses, but much shorter.

# Future Perspectives

Transport-as-a-Service (TaaS) is becoming a crucial topic when it comes to planning the future of urban mobility. As people are more likely to move into urban zones in the coming decades, a consideration must be the growing need for new classes of urban transport vehicles that are both efficient and environmentally friendly. To enable a wide availability of autonomous means of transportation, concerns around the safety of their implementation must be addressed. Even though these technologies are expected to reduce accident rates significantly, this can only be a guaranteed if urban regulations and infrastructure conditions are adapted accordingly.

*Photo/Illustration: christian / adobe.stock.com*
description.longTextHtml:
Shared self-driving pods that allow people to request them through a mobile app and hail them just like taxis or similar services. Like other automated driverless vehicles, they possess basic features such as vehicle-to-vehicle communication, sensors, and image processing to navigate in real-time and smoothly. They can operate on elevated or underground shuttle networks or traditional roadways.

The models being developed offer a sustainable mobility service, which uses clean energy alternatives and is battery-powered. In terms of maneuverability, they have a 360-degree steering system that enables navigation in extremely tight urban streets and parking in small places. Besides, the interior could be adjusted to fit the needs of whichever business wishes to use it, from ride sharing to food deliveries or even a mobile office space or meeting room. In general, they are higher than regular self-driving vehicles and are similar to busses, but much shorter.

Future Perspectives

Transport-as-a-Service (TaaS) is becoming a crucial topic when it comes to planning the future of urban mobility. As people are more likely to move into urban zones in the coming decades, a consideration must be the growing need for new classes of urban transport vehicles that are both efficient and environmentally friendly. To enable a wide availability of autonomous means of transportation, concerns around the safety of their implementation must be addressed. Even though these technologies are expected to reduce accident rates significantly, this can only be a guaranteed if urban regulations and infrastructure conditions are adapted accordingly.

Photo/Illustration: christian / adobe.stock.com

description.shortText: A category of buildings with a near-zero or zero net energy consumption, as well as zero on-site carbon emissions.
description.longText:
A construction system, able to reduce operational carbon emissions through buildings that consume the same amount of energy they produce. To generate energy on-site, this model takes into account the local ecosystem for the best microgeneration technologies, including photovoltaics, wind turbines, small-scale hydropower, or even other renewable sources, such as waste heat from large-scale power generation.

One of the biggest challenges in the energy sector today is balancing power supply and demand during peak times, which zero-energy buildings could alleviate. However, regulatory frameworks are still inconsistent and/or incompatible with each other when it comes to energy pricing and a sufficient incentive effect on sustainable and manageable energy production is still lacking. Emergent regulatory practices need to address these issues, including factors such as resource cycle, impact on land use, the environment, water, and human health.

# Future Perspectives

With the growing demand for decarbonization, one promising solution for cost reduction and market acceleration is to plan zero energy districts. Expanding the context to a district scale may require intense and sophisticated planning from scratch, resulting in high initial costs. Yet, in the long term, it can yield many benefits that are not possible with individual zero energy buildings, such as scale effects to drive down costs per unit, shared power infrastructure, and general cost-effective energy.

entities.name: Deep Fake Detection Tool
synonyms: real-time video footage could be fake

description.shortText: AI-assisted tools designed to detect when digital data, such as videos and photos, has been corrupted. It helps both citizens and institutions to look for original and truthful sources and combat image appropriation.
description.longText:
In a context where biometrical certifications are used in security procedures, such as facial-recognition systems, concerns to detect fake digital content raise increased attention. With the democratization of cameras in mobile devices and open-source access to stock images, it is becoming easier to create deep fakes. Supported by artificial intelligence, deep-fake detection software could be trained to identify anomalies that the human eye is unable to notice organically. 

The software would continuously run in the background, automatically scanning any video clip played by the user. When a deep fake is detected, the software notifies the user, similarly to an antivirus alert from malicious activity. Trained to analyze natural human body movements, facial alterations, and the synthesizing of fake audio, this AI spots unauthentic information that is nearly indistinguishable from the original content.

As deep fakes are gaining more visibility throughout the web, the widespread availability of deep-fake detection tools becomes as crucial as their constant improvement. These systems need to generate additional data for continuous practice and analysis, so then the differentiation between authentic and unauthentic content is refined to a higher degree.

# Future Perspectives

Truly robust detection methods will need to look beyond superficial quirks as artificial intelligence gets better at learning to mimic human eccentricities. By fact-checking pulses, breathing rates, human-like movements, and metadata, future software would need to employ multiple formulas, strategies, and sources for fraud detection. 

Within AR/VR worlds, deep fake detection becomes even more troublesome since users are free to create avatars that escape the aesthetics conceived in the physical reality, and hackers could invade a user's account and commit virtual identity theft. In this scenario, the technology might evolve from analyzing only audiovisual cues to encompassing biometric data from the user operating synthetic persona.

In addition, these techniques could be used to transform the current method of lie detection in courts and law proceedings. These systems would provide additional tools for improving the struggle for justice, by cross-examining the entire chain of politics that ordinary civilians are generally unable to grasp. However, it would require a systematic approach with other technologies capabilities such as bias-detection algorithms to guarantee fairness in trials and create a sustainable juridical system.

*Photo / Illustration: © panuwat / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: An augmentation method able to create micro-pores in the skin in a minimally invasive manner to deliver effective ingredients with enhanced absorption rates.
description.longText:
A physical enhancement method that creates micro-pores in the skin in a minimally invasive manner to deliver effective ingredients with enhanced absorption rates. The patch composition naturally dissolves on the skin following use. These patches can be used efficiently in cosmetics given their patient usability, safety, and effectiveness. 

Self-dissolving and biodegradable microneedle technologies for transdermal sustained delivery of drugs and vaccines are commonly used in medical treatments. The success of these delivery systems in medical care treatments is inspiring the cosmetic industry to do the same. Ongoing research is successfully loading skincare components into biodegradable dissolving micro-needles in order to produce novel cosmetic patches.

Although some components are extremely common in cosmetics, such as collagen or hyaluronic acid (that has strong moisturizing effects due to its high capacity to hold water), they also have difficulty penetrating the skin because of the large size of the individual molecules.

# Future Perspectives

The future advancement of microneedle development will contribute to the engineering of smart microneedles that can control the release of various active ingredients under various conditions, in line with the dynamic physicochemical changes of the skin. Moreover, novel microneedle patch delivery systems with needles that can effectively release specific active ingredients to the deeper layers of the skin could potentially be part of complex skin therapies. They would administer specific probiotic and living prebiotic mixtures that can be released at given conditions to support the targeted rebalancing of specific bacteria of the microbiome inhabiting the various skin layers.

*Photo / Illustration: © Andrey Popov / adobe.stock.com*
