description.shortText: Nanomachines combined with reactive molecules via mechanosynthesis to build parts with higher precision. These parts are assembled by positioning mechanisms to make macroscopic products that remain atomically precise.
description.longText:
Nanomachines combined with reactive molecules via mechanosynthesis, a chemical process that determines reaction outcomes of chemical compositions using mechanical constraints to control reactive molecules to specific molecular sites. Nanofactories use simple hydrocarbon feedstock molecules, such as natural gas, propane, or acetylene to create atomically precise diamondoid products.

By employing controlled molecular assembly that makes it possible to create novel products having the intricate complexity currently found only in biological systems. This molecular structure of a diamondoid product resembles a complex composite material instead of a brittle solid crystal.

# Future Perspectives

With the development of nanofactories, novel complex diamondoid-based products could be available to be included in nanocomputers, medical nanorobots, aerospace and defense mechanisms, devices for cheap energy production, and environmental remediation. Medical applications are of highest priority, including anti-aging therapies and resuscitation from cryonic preservation, although earlier-generation research nanofactories will produce substantially less complex products but still provide an evolutionary pathway.

*Photo / Illustration: © bondvit / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A robot powered by AI software capable of carrying out a variety of in-home tasks, such as cleaning and cooking. Equipped with wireless network and voice-identification patterns, the robot is able to perform tasks with no human oversight, while interacting with smart-home devices.
description.longText:
Specialized robots are already making their way into homes all over the world, helping with tasks such as mopping, vacuuming, and lawn-mowing. Now, more general robots are able to help with a variety of tasks, using abilities similar to those of a human being.

By using cutting-edge artificial intelligence technology, these robots are able to clean the whole house by themselves. This includes not only the cleaning itself but also recognizing and remembering where people are and the location of objects in the home. Advanced robotics allows the robot to be able to handle objects, properly managing them for each needed task, such as making coffee and cooking.

Equipped with wireless network standards and the ability to be controlled by voice commands, the robot is able to perform tasks with no human oversight, while interacting with smart-home devices. It even has a safety module, which enables the robot to recognize and react to emergency situations, such as a person falling or undergoing a seizure.

# Future Perspectives

Robotic companions, especially those that help with in-home tasks, will eventually be a reality in many households. They could greatly reduce the amount of time spent with those chores, freeing up time for leisure or work-related activities. In addition, as their ability to communicate improves, they could be seen as great companions for those who are usually alone at home or for people who require care.

In more traditional cultures, household robots also have the potential to shift home relationship dynamics, taking away from women the burden of being responsible for home care, which could mean a major cultural and economic shift regarding social inequality.

*Photo/illustration: Possessed Photography / Unsplash*

description.shortText: Implants and wearables that deliver artificially synaesthetic experiences by translating sensory input in a different modality from the original stimuli, allowing users to see, hear or feel things that would not otherwise be detected by normal human senses.
description.longText:
These implants and wearables are designed to enhance or substitute perceptual ability, allowing the user to see, hear or feel things that would not otherwise be detected by normal human senses. A set of algorithms translate inputs from sensors such as microphones or cameras into other sensations, e.g. sound into touch or color into sound. 

This technological solution uses infrared goggles, parabolic microphones, and thermal sensors. Although these devices enhance human perception, the brain is usually still aware that it is being fed information through a piece of hardware and doesn't interpret this data in the same way it would have when the information comes from a natural sensory organ. The brain is the organ responsible for perceptual information processing, independent of the source and, through neural plasticity, it can rewire itself to substitute sensory information from one sense with that of another. With new devices and improvements in brain-machine interfaces, technological developments are reaching a point at which it is becoming possible to fool the brain into perceiving artificial sensory information as if it were part of its own natural sensory repertoire.

Besides augmenting human senses, such wearables work as devices for sensory substitution or addition. Therefore, people with disabilities could perceive the world differently by using their other senses. Colorblind individuals, as well as blind people, could hear colors as sound frequencies sent to their ears or electrical signals directly to their brains. For disabled individuals, using sensory substitution could make it easier to participate in educational experiences created for individuals without disabilities. For example, a vest with vibration engines in different parts of the body could translate spoken words into patterns, allowing users to understand what is being said as their brains are subconsciously translating the complicated vibration patterns into language.

# Future Perspectives

Once brain-machine interfaces become more sophisticated, sensory substitution without having to take a detour through existing human senses could become a reality by routing information directly to the brain. Encoding sensory information in a way that the brain can understand will likely require techniques based on machine learning, incorporating feedback from the brain to co-adaptively learn how to present the information to the brain.

Patients who have suffered the loss of eyesight or who were naturally born blind could receive neural implants resulting in the ability to see, maybe even in the infrared and ultra-violet ranges and beyond. With the ability to project images directly into the visual cortex, a whole new level of immersive experiences could be reached. Also, combined with smart drugs or supplements, this type of effect could be achieved without intrusive methods such as implants or wearables. As pharmaceutical technology develops, chemicals could be combined with implants to give the user a desired and controlled sensory substitution without suffering adverse side effects.

By exchanging or amplifying human senses, a new way of perceiving the world through synesthesia could lead to a novel interpretation of reality and what it means to be human. Implantable devices could give humans abilities of other animals, or ones that do not exist in nature at all, allowing humans to “feel” electromagnetic fields, stock-market data, or even the weather when in space. In the end, the metaphorical sixth sense could become a reality.

*Photo / Illustration: © Unique Vision / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Artificially constructed device produced in a laboratory or with a 3D printer, designed for organ replacement.
description.longText:
Using 3D printing techniques or growing the device in a laboratory setting, artificial organs could restore a specific function or group of functions in the body. The production of organs could solve the major issue of endless transplant lists and improve the quality of life for individuals with one or more failed organs. Furthermore, it can also facilitate testing new medications.

Usually made from the patient's own stem cells, to try to avoid further compatibility complications, these artificial organs are grown in laboratories and can either replace organs with life-sustaining functions or even serve as replacements for joints found in the knee and hip, for example. With a growing number of people facing organ failures due to age-related disorders, companies are focusing on the development of artificial implant products such as wearable artificial kidneys, bio-lungs, and artificial pancreas for diseases that cannot be cured with alternative treatment methods. 

# Future Perspectives

Despite the bright future envisioned with such developments, it remains a challenge in the medical field to find professionals who are qualified and prepared to perform such surgical procedures. On the other hand, the same technology could also be a handy resource for training students in medical schools, since the devices are very realistic - to the point of even bleeding, like their natural counterparts.

*Photo / Illustration: ₢ Robina Weermeijer / unsplash.com*

description.shortText: Devices that harvest, convert and store energy generated from motion, be that human motion, such as walking or riding a bike, or motion coming from another source, such as wind power, or waves. Kinetic energy harvesting is one of the cleanest and most sustainable ways of obtaining energy.
description.longText:
Kinetic energy is all energy generated through motion, thus, it can be harvested from anything that moves, such as wind, waves, vehicles and even human beings. There are five possible types of kinetic energy: radiant, thermal, sound, electrical, and mechanical.

Producing and storing electric energy from kinetic sources requires an electromechanical transducer to convert movement into electricity. The amount of energy produced is proportional to the stress created. One of the latest developments in this area is, for instance, using MEMS (microelectromechanical systems) autonomous plasma switch to control TENGs (Triboelectric Nanogenerators), tiny energy harvesting devices that can be used to convert mechanical motions into electrical outputs using triboelectrification inductions, which could be used to develop e-textiles that harvest energy more efficiently.

Kinetic energy harvesting devices could be implemented in urban areas, to generate green energy from citizens walking about the city. It could be implemented on the ground, imitating bricks and used to cleanly and efficiently power the streetlights along the sidewalk every time someone passes by, for example.

A wearable device, such as a shoe, could harvest around 7 watts per step, enough to charge a smartphone. The technique uses a conductive liquid to create friction on a nanofilm-covered surface. Combined with a perforated layer that acquires bubbles of pressurized gas, this device generates electricity, which can be stored in a battery and then later used to power devices via a built-in USB port.

Another example entails an electric bicycle that could have the ability to harvest the power generated by braking and pedaling and then convert this kinetic energy into its electricity, eliminating the need for the bike to be plugged into a power socket to charge. It could allow users to travel longer distances, speeding up their daily commute, and improving urban mobility.

# Future Perspectives

As humanity moves towards a more symbiotic relationship with its devices, one could easily imagine a moment where all wearables are charged using the owner's kinetic energy. With this uninterrupted power supply, these devices wouldn't need to be taken off the body or plugged into a power supply. These devices could also incentivize non-motorized modes of transport, such as walking and cycling, by implementing a gamification aspect. Furthermore, there are projects starting to harness vehicles and citizen movements around the city to power its own IoT structure.

description.shortText: Interactive storytelling software that uses machine learning to recognize behavior patterns, and revises narratives using emotion-based experiences. By computationally predicting the emotional response to a narrative segment, this system could expand human interaction with digital content.
description.longText:
Data analytics and machine learning, applied as story creation tools, combining content creation, emotional curves, sentiment analysis, and video synthesis. Capable of making assumptions based on past and real-time collected data, this technology can predict future emotional responses and generate storytelling based on human emotion.

Spectators and listeners are exposed to a webcam powered by AI and skin-conductivity sensors that process, analyze, learn, and make assumptions at a scale and depth of detail impossible for individual human analysts. The data gathered routes back into the software, and the narrative of a game or a story changes based on the emotional inputs provided by the user.

The software provides storylines, such as characters, plots, relationships, and scenarios, that adapt to how audiences respond to those inputs. By computationally predicting the emotional response to a narrative segment, this system can influence both the storyline and keep the user on a dynamic curve of interactions.

# Future Perspectives

AI-generated narratives, plus AI capabilities of reading and reacting to emotions, could increase the effectiveness of learning processes, augmenting engagement upon recognition of positive emotional reactions. These changes could herald a new empathetic and responsive future for storytelling, where viewers or players are encouraged to bring about changes to the narrative while learning about different topics and their behaviors.

Additionally, this solution could be equally valuable for therapeutic purposes, such as helping mental health professionals identify sources of trauma by increasingly exposing subjects to patients and adjusting to their psychological responses and needs.

description.shortText: Biological engineering of the environment of a celestial body such as a planet, moon or asteroid to resemble Earth to make it habitable. If successful, such methods could also provide a solution for bioremediation on Earth.
description.longText:
A method of engineering the environment—such as atmosphere, temperature, topography or ecology—of a planet, moon, or asteroid to resemble Earth to make it habitable. Recent studies have shown that the use of biology in space could lead to a substantially lightened payload. In this sense, it is expected that it will soon be possible to find a function for a synthetic biological architecture that could detoxify the soil of other planets which contain substances such as perchlorate—like Mars for instance. 

By using other methodologies like bacterial nitrate fixing, it should be possible to enrich the soil with ammonia, substances that are important for the growth and development of plants. Scientists are therefore working on a way to deliver a comparative assessment with alternative chemical approaches that will make it feasible to utilize biotechnology to support manned interstellar missions in order to terraform other planets for agricultural practices—both for plants and microbes.

Some possible approaches include washing away perchlorate to cleanse the soil or using hydroponics in order to grow plants with an initially low mass of microbial cells, on-demand cell growth with in-situ resources, and the elimination of toxic wastewater. Some organisms targeted for these types of projects are Pseudomonas, relevant extremophiles that offer properties to help reduce perchlorate in the soil while also being capable of mutating to adapt to a variety of environmental conditions. 

# Future Perspectives
Besides offering solutions for space exploration and colonization, the same principle could be applied on Earth for bioremediation approaches targeted to cleanup land near oil wells and toxic spills. In addition, non-arable land enrichment would improve food production to address famines, drought, and large populations in general.

description.shortText: Meal replacements based on algae that contain a controlled quantity of calories and nutrients designed to substitute traditional food meals.
description.longText:
Meal replacements formed from algae that contain a controlled quantity of calories and nutrients designed to substitute traditional solid food meals. Algae are the fastest growing plant organisms in nature and are a great alternative source of vitamins, proteins, and minerals. Algae have a lot of potential as a scalable food source, as they grow anywhere – often in vertical fermentation tanks – without using large amounts of land or water. In current experiments, lab-grown algal-based food shows no negative impact on the environment, nor residual waste discharged into the ecosystem. 

Producing food today puts an incredible amount of stress on the environment. Besides, difficulty accessing nutritious food contributes to the growing rate of obesity or inadequate nutrition. Given that traditional approaches were not capable of satisfactorily mitigating the problem of global food insecurity, researchers and many actors, along with the food supply chain, believe that artificial, lab-grown food could efficiently ensure appropriate nutrition for everyone on the planet. 

This type of food would be especially helpful in areas where people do not consume the suggested daily serving of nutrients. This growing industry claims that these products can be used to partially or even wholly replace traditional diets. They are also more sustainable and healthier and do not require conventional agriculture techniques for production. Currently, they do not offer the traceability that is critical in widespread consumer use and acceptance. Still, as technology evolves and provides tastier solutions, these products could be in supermarkets in the form of drinks, healthy shakes, or even snacks.

# Future Perspectives

One could easily imagine a world where meals look like astronaut food. Due to the environmental limitations placed on producing accessible food for everyone and the shortcomings of value chains being unable to distribute quality food equally throughout the world, alternatives need to be developed to preserve life on the planet. 

In the mid-term, algae can be used as a nutrient boosting ingredient, while in the future, there could be meals entirely based on algae. Solutions like algae-based meals are only the tip of the iceberg, other meal replacements could follow suit, assuming that the public becomes more accepting of GMOs as they prove worthy of our tastebuds and long-term health.

*Photo/Illustration: chokniti / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A chemically synthesized DNA strain with all the genes, spacers, sequences and folding necessary for it to be functionally capable of replacing a real chromosome.
description.longText:
A chemically synthesized DNA strain with all the genes, spacers, sequences and folding necessary for it to be functionally capable of replacing a real chromosome. 
Reading the genome is already an established technology, but writing it is not. There is still a limit to the length of DNA that can be synthesized with minimal error.  Long synthetic strains usually encounter a number of mutations and begin to lose functionality. However, every year longer strands of DNA are artificially obtained. A full yeast chromosome has already been developed from scratch and worked in living cells as if it were a natural one. The synthesized chromosome can exist alongside natural chromosomes, and serves as a platform to safely and easily add new functions to the micro-organism. 

# Future Perspectives 
In combination with genome editing techniques, synthetic chromosomes may provide a tool to design complex genetic systems or assemble new genetic pathways. In the future, synthetic chromosomes may, for example, enable the creation of new complex organisms. In the case of synthetic human chromosomes, it gets us closer to the creation of a full synthetic human genome, and therefore full synthetic human cells. It could be used to replace chromosomes with disease marker genes in embryos or even give rise to new types of gene therapy in adults.

*Photo / Illustration: © ktsdesign/ adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Carbon credits implemented as a currency or as tokens stored on the blockchain that create economic benefit, capital, and demand for emissions reductions. It brings transparency, trust, and scalability to carbon markets.
description.longText:
Carbon credits are certificates that allow the holder to emit a certain amount of carbon dioxide or other greenhouse gases. However, since the birth of carbon offset markets, fraud has been a severe problem, such as double spending of unretired carbon credits. When combining the blockchain with carbon credits, it can track, measure, and store the output of carbon emissions and then autonomously trade or block quota transactions with the third party while also enhancing transaction efficiency and transparency.  

This emission reduction protocol provides a positive economic and social reward for reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. It creates an economic benefit, capital, and demand for emissions reduction opportunities and, ultimately, incentivizes change in both individual and group behavior. By taking advantage of the integrity and accountability that blockchain provides, the carbon trading market would make their carbon data emissions traceable and reliable. Low-carbon projects that reduce greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, for instance, would receive carbon credits to be used as revenue for reducing carbon emissions or for sequestering carbon. Conversely, companies that produce greenhouse gases would buy carbon credits to offset their emissions.

Carbon credits can be implemented as a currency or as tokens stored on the blockchain that contain unique information about each credit’s origin, authenticity, and additional data, including being a benefit or bonus from reforestation or renewable energy. Blockchain technology could also lower entry barriers while allowing carbon credits to be broken down into per-product or per-transaction quantities. As a result, consumers could be given the opportunity to offset their carbon impact for individual purchases in real-time.

# Future Perspectives

By creating a financial pathway for incentivizing emissions reductions, proactive investment into climate projects, technologies, and policies would be stimulated. New peer-to-peer and business-to-consumer marketplaces would emerge, making it easier for everyone to participate in these new carbon markets.

The blockchain protocol could open up existing carbon markets and create a broader range of players, including smaller businesses and individuals. The public and transparent nature of the information could encourage international collaboration and strengthen trust in the system.

*Photo/Illustration: markrhiggins / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: Artificial apiary that creates a constant spring-like environment for bees in urban settings that can help save honeybees from extinction.
description.longText:
A synthetic apiary which creates a controlled space in which seasonal honeybees can thrive year-round. Light, humidity, and temperature are engineered to simulate a perpetual spring environment. Also, undisturbed by external stimuli that may be found in urban environments, bees are provided with synthetic pollen and sugar water, while being regularly evaluated for health and well-being. After succeeding in the adaptation phase, in which the queen is able to lay her eggs in the apiary, the other bees will be able to function normally in the artificial environment.

Soon, this technology will allow hives to be integrated into urban planning, attaching them to buildings despite extreme weather conditions. Long-term goals include developing new ways of allowing bees and humans to cohabitate and create further understanding of the factors that influence hive building and structure. This outcome reveals that natural cultivation in artificial spaces could be possible across scales, from organisms to building-scale.

Bees, as agents of cross-pollination, are an essential part of our agricultural production. However, their health and population have declined over the past decade due, in large part, to environmental conditions and exposure to pesticides. By creating a controlled environment in urban settings that can help establish and support bee colonies, we might be able to preserve the natural environmental balance they create as one of the most important species on the planet.


# Future perspectives

Synthetic Apiary Environments could be a complementary technology to other areas such as Vertical Farming or urban agriculture in general – bees could simultaneously pollinate horticultural crops while providing an urban source of honey for local communities or restaurants. If this kind of experiment succeeds, it could be readapted to take care of other endangered species vital to sustaining life on Earth, such as fungi, earthworms, and ants.

*Photo/Illustration: Karel / stock.adobe.com*

description.shortText: While bias is inherently present in data used by algorithms already deeply embedded in our lives, bias detection algorithms, equipped with metrics related to fairness, can help mitigate this issue. Overall, this algorithm detects unfair coded bias.
description.longText:
As machine learning infiltrates society, we have realized that algorithms are not always perfect: algorithmic bias has already been detected in several examples. Although machine learning is a continuous form of statistical discrimination by its very nature, the kind of bias primarily addressed is unwanted variety, placing privileged groups at a systematic advantage and unprivileged groups at a systematic disadvantage. Examples include predictive policing systems that have been caught in runaway feedback loops of discrimination and hiring tests that end up excluding applicants from low-income neighborhoods or prefer male applicants to female ones.

Systems can be designed to scan algorithmic models and detect bias at different points in the machine learning pipeline: either in the training data or the learned model, which correlates to varying categories of bias mitigation techniques. The adversarial de-biasing procedure is currently one of the most popular methods to combat discrimination. It relies on adversarial training to remove bias from latent representations learned by the model. Besides that, metrics for datasets can measure outcomes that provide an advantage to a specific recipient or group that historically held a systematic position of power and partition a population into groups that should have equality in terms of benefits received.

This solution could reduce unfair outcomes and recommend specific changes to how the mathematical models interpret the data — inducing a reparation program through machine learning, instead of perpetuating a centuries-old system that generates disadvantages for certain societal groups. By examining several public models, the amount of influence that sensitive variables — race, gender, class, and religion — have on data can be measured along with an estimated correlation between said variables. Researchers could also visualize how a given model’s outcomes are skewed and take preventative measures to make the model immune to these biases.

There is an even more straightforward yet effective way of avoiding bias in machine learning models. Hiring a more diverse team of software engineers and data scientists by including people from different backgrounds such as gender, race, age, and diversified body and mental capabilities could inevitably help broaden the point of view of the algorithms they program.

# Future Perspectives

Given the ubiquitous nature of algorithms and their deep-reaching impact on society, scientists are trying to help prevent injustice by creating tools that detect underlying unfairness in these programs. Even though the best technologies still serve as a means to an end, these solutions are essential in paving the way towards establishing trust. By encoding variational “fair” encoders, dynamic upsampling of training data based on learned representations, or preventing disparity through distributional optimization, these tools could possibly help create ethical and transparent principles for developing new AI technologies.

Since many bias-detection techniques can overlap with ethical challenges in different areas such as structures for good governance, appropriate data sharing, and explainability of models,  an all-encompassing solution to algorithmic bias must be established in both legal and technical terms to bridge the gap and minimize potential conflicts based on bias and prejudice. Otherwise, an unchecked market with access to increasingly powerful predictive tools can gradually and imperceptibly worsen social inequality, perhaps even leading to a new era of information warfare. In light of this dystopian outcome, governments worldwide, including Singapore, South Korea, and the United Arab Emirates, have announced AI ethics as a new board/committee/ministry to be integrated into their political system.

description.shortText: An energy-efficient recycling method, in which unsorted general household waste is transformed into a recyclable thermoplastic substitute. Overall, this solution is expected to reduce the costs related to logistics and household waste treatment.
description.longText:
A biobased modular and adaptive conversion process, able to transform unsorted household garbage, such as bones, food scraps, diapers, and even plastic, into a fully recyclable thermoplastic substitute. In short, this method transforms waste into more basic natural particles that will be later reconstituted, bonded, and shaped in several grades. 

First, the waste is collected and directed to a processing plant. There, it gets transformed, despite the varying compositions, thus reducing residual waste stream into a more basic natural component by breaking up waste into a nearly molecular level. Then, it treats the garbage within a closed-loop system that combines the most basic organic elements such as cellulose, sugar, and fibers with bioplastic. This process produces no emissions, does not use water, and leaves no residual waste. 

The processing plant usually is equipped with machine vision as a means to identify the waste it is decomposing. This feature makes the process progressively simple, as it recognizes the waste while recycling, besides learning from new materials entering the facility. Machine vision helps eliminate the necessity of performing separate collection manually, reducing the volume of waste drastically. 

The end product is a bio-based composite material that is energy-efficient and environmentally sound. This dynamic solution works bilaterally, reducing the costs related to logistics and household waste treatment while introducing a more circular and alternative climate-positive thermoplastic material designed not to harm the environment. Besides, it helps prevent the trash from reaching landfills and transforms various waste inputs into homogeneous and carbon-neutral raw materials. 

# Future Perspectives

In the future, it might be used on a large scale to treat city waste through integration with public systems. The implementation of such treatment plants associated with urban and industrial centers would facilitate the reinsertion of byproducts into the plastic production chain, thus helping solve the problem multilaterally. Finally, adapting the solution for direct domestic use alongside predictive software would create potential future applications for some industrial segments. 

In addition, in chain restaurants, like in the fast-food industry, for instance, legislations that require companies to have unsorted waste treatment systems of their own, could contribute to generate more ecological ethics in such brands.

*Photo/Illustration: vchalup / adobe.stock.com*

description.shortText: A system that extracts images collected with machine vision and processes imagery with AI software. It creates dynamic information over a high-definition 3D city map, containing data about geospatial services, such as public transportation and the best routes for autonomous vehicles.
description.longText:
A high-definition map generated by crowdsourced information from portable sensors, 3D visualizations, and digital twins of a city's architecture and infrastructure. This information is mounted directly onto the city through augmented and virtual reality, or it could be accessed online. 

By combining thousands of pictures and spatial information, an extended city map enables navigation in ultra-realistic maps, which process data for various uses. A computer vision scan of all the imagery, for example, could build 3D visualizations of the environment and all its objects. This system would allow identifying and grouping these objects into semantic segmentations. 

The data gathered by the sensors could provide valuable insights for geospatial services and autonomous vehicles, with each map tailored according to the user necessities, routes, and preferences. By creating a unique and personalized experience, a wheelchair user, for instance, could customize the map to show obstacle-free pathways. Drones and flying vehicles could use embedded high definition maps to know drone restriction area limits, thus helping avoid possible fines.

Information such as weather, seasons, time, viewpoint, real-time camera angles, and others could enable agencies to research and remotely evaluate the environment and conditions. This opens up the possibility for global collaboration in developing local solutions.

Yet, privacy issues are paramount; algorithms must keep individual identities anonymous. This can be automated with deep-learning algorithms to enforce privacy compliance by hiding or blurring faces, license plates, windows, or anything that may compromise citizens' identities.

# Future Perspectives 

The advantage of crowdsensing data lies in constructing elements from different angles and viewpoints. In this sense, governments, organizations, and businesses will be able to access and create their utopian or dystopian world maps by using real-world data. Augmented reality art and modifications could also participate in this vast shared experience.

In a future scenario, high-definition maps are expected to be so detailed that eventually, they could be indistinguishable from pictures, with the difference that maps would be enhanced with real-time dynamic data. With the utilization of XR glasses, citizens could add chosen dynamic information onto the city view, thus adding and substracting overlays according to their preferences. 

Powered by VR technology, this system could develop a whole new model for tourism, in which a person could visit a new city or country without leaving their home. This practice could enable people to get to know touristic sites without contributing to the carbon emissions that come with long flights.

description.shortText: Digital reconstruction of the brain to simulate a variety of behaviors on a circuitry level.
description.longText:
Digital reconstruction of a slice of the brain including all the different neurons found in that area, the factors that make them fire, and the connections they make. After completing the reconstruction, supercomputers can put the neurons through a simulation of different behaviors. By adjusting the level of calcium ions, which pass information between neurons, a wide range of activity patterns can be simulated. For example, it can increase certain brainwaves, such as those we observe in deep sleep. These findings cannot be concluded by looking at the features of individual neurons. Many other findings may be drawn from the digital reconstruction of the brain once the full net is mapped. These simulations prove that the brain can switch between different states and raises questions regarding the interrelatedness of those states to diseases or different levels of consciousness.

# Future Perspectives
A computer-simulated organ would allow scientists to noninvasively test new treatments for disorders and diseases, providing a viable alternative to research that involves both human trials and animal testing. 
However, the still little understood intricacies and variability of brain activity mean that difficulties arise when attempting to determine which is the 'correct' neural activity pattern to be modeled. While modeling the human brain has been accomplished successfully, when it comes to a full simulation, significant challenges are yet to be overcome.  For instance, consciousness has still not been defined satisfactorily. Furthermore, in computing, perfect code exists for algorithms, and bugs can be quickly fixed. But it is unclear how a system of algorithms would ever be able to capture the variability of the brain, from DNA mutations to random synapse activity. 
Instead, it might be that  computational neuroscience abandons the pursuit of reconstructing the biological brain in favor of creating advanced algorithms akin to black boxes to execute tasks, while remaining internally inscrutable.
Lastly, the ethics of digitally reconstructing the brain remain in question, as biases can all too easily be introduced to simulations, thereby creating a mirror of their creators' biases in simulated neural activity.

description.shortText: Unbound by offline territorial borders, this "virtual passport" is digitally assembled, enabling anyone, anywhere in the world to apply.
description.longText:
This type of virtual document does not grant citizenship in the traditional meaning of the word, nor does it substitute travel papers. E-residents may have online access to specific services. As a transnational identity, this virtual residency is government-issued, which enables e-residents to use business tools offered by the government. E-residents can also enjoy a legal framework that provides insurance, compliance, and stability, especially since policy changes are accessible online.

Services include banking, taxation, enterprise formation, signatures for official documents, in addition to mandatory bureaucratic obligations such as electronic applications, documentation, annual tax filings, or government reports. The only "offline" requirement for this type of business is to have a local contact person in the country of e-residency. But this requirement is being met through agencies that provide legal addresses and a local contact person for e-resident entrepreneurs.

As the number of digital location-independent enterprises rises, entrepreneurs look for ways to meet their needs without the bureaucracy of their countries of residence. This digital identity allows business owners to set up and fully manage enterprises online from anywhere in the world where there is an internet connection. It has begun to spark a generation of "digital nomads," location-independent entrepreneurs or employees that opt against living in one specific place, choosing instead, to travel anywhere with a stable internet connection to run their businesses.

# Future Perspectives
At the moment, the only country providing e-residency it is Estonia. Though following its extended success, other countries may offer their own type of digital services. However, from a regulatory standpoint, there are many difficulties when trying to open a company with business partners of differing nationalities. From this difficulty, opportunities may arise, such as new transnational businesses resulting from this new wave of young professionals looking for digital common ground.

description.shortText: By reprogramming cells from the immune system, biomedical engineers could treat and cure diseases and conditions such as cancer, HIV, and multiple sclerosis. Such techniques also help develop vaccines and healing treatments for inflammation, wounds, and tissue regeneration without stem cells.
description.longText:
An area of research focused on bioengineering techniques to target cellular and molecular processes to develop new treatments and tools to understand, control, and exploit the immune system as a means to treat conditions and diseases.

New vaccines and healing technologies for wounds, inflammation, or even cancer and tissue regeneration are some possibilities explored by researchers. One of the latest breakthroughs in the field was the discovery of killer T cells that are programmed to wipe out cancer. This achievement of immune system engineering was so revolutionary because it could treat not only cancer but also multiple sclerosis and HIV.

With the discovery of gene editing techniques such as TALENs and CRISPR, startups have also used the same premise to engineer T-cell-based therapeutics to autonomously target conditions and diseases on a cellular level. This discovery is so essential because an immune cell is meant to communicate with other cells, deliver substances, and change what happens in a microenvironment. At the same time, they retain memory about the organism and can multiply among themselves. Synthetic immunology is suggesting a new method of treatment that tackles specific search-and-kill behaviors when these engineered immune cells deliver specific drugs in an organism.

Furthermore, mRNA 'programmable' vaccines have been developed over recent decades. Immunization is achieved by injecting a genetically engineered messenger RNA sequence coding for viral antigens which triggers, or engineers, an immune response to the injected RNA, teaching the immune system to respond to infection. In less than a year since the first outbreak of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, mRNA vaccines for COVID-19 were demonstrated to be effective and safely tolerated, preparing the way for widespread, global immunization programs. 

# Future Perspectives

While immune engineering is currently focused on treating conditions such as cancer, the field does not need to limit itself to this specific disease. HIV is being targeted by this solution, both in terms of treatment and the possibility of being cured. However, research is continuing on more improved approaches because of the very specifics of HIV: since the virus hides in the body even after treatment, patients must take antiretroviral drugs for the rest of their lives. Immune engineering could change this scenario by programming cells that could result in a one-time treatment capable of eliminating the virus once and for all.

description.shortText: The deployment of fungal, bacterial, and microbial organisms naturally found in living plants as a means to protect and improve crop performance. This is a more eco-friendly approach than synthetic pesticides and fertilizers.
description.longText:
All living plants are populated with various endophytic microorganisms that form a complex microbiota that lives within a plant for at least part of its life cycle, including members of the Actinobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Firmicutes bacteria groups, along with fungi and various eukaryotic microbes. These endophytes and their host plant have developed a mutualistic symbiotic relationship, where the host plant provides the nutrients and habitat for the survival of the endophytes. At the same time, the compounds produced by them can boost the plant's immunity and its resistance against biotic and abiotic stresses. An endophytic strain can potentially inhabit multiple host genera yet exhibit genotype specificity within a species.

The interface between plant roots and soil and their microbiota enhances plant mineral uptake, regulates chemical compounds, such as phytohormones that modulate plant growth and development, and protects plants from soil-derived pests and pathogens. They can produce a wide range of bioactive compounds with anticancer, cytotoxic, and insecticidal properties, making them attractive to the pharmaceutical and the skincare industry. 

Currently, scientists are looking for ways to manipulate the microbes populating this below-ground habitat to increase crop production sustainably. Two significant paths are being explored; one that uses plant breeding to select for varieties that have enhanced symbiosis with the microbiota and the development of plant probiotics through the assembly of beneficial microbes into synthetic communities (SynComs). This second approach mixes SynComs with seeds at sowing, and once the seedlings germinate, it acts as a kind of plant vaccine.

# Future Perspectives
Many questions remain unanswered about the plant microbiome. For this technology to be deployed appropriately, extensive research is needed to investigate the immense variety of endophytic microorganisms, their possible combinations, interactions, and their different effects in the various plants. 

In order to develop novel microbiome cocktail mixtures, the combination of specific bacteria, fungi, and microbes could enhance the green production of plants for active ingredients for pharmaceutical or cosmetic usage. Also, these endophytes hold immense potential to become a safe and cost-effective alternative to chemical pesticides and fertilizers. The increased acceptance of fungal endophytes could be an integral part of pest management programs for optimized crop production and ensure the long-term sustainability of agriculture.

description.shortText: A swarm of solar panels that covers the Sun's surface and absorb all the energy produced by it. This enormous structure can collect the necessary power to generate electricity on Earth.
description.longText:
A net of solar panels orbiting around the sun to absorb energy and provide a power source. Energy would be transferred wirelessly between the individual components and Earth. Alternatively, millions of mirrors could be used to focus light onto a fewer number of collectors.

Unlike a shell-like Dyson sphere, named after the physicist Freeman Dyson who created the concept, the megastructure would cover the surface of the sun and be able to absorb all the energy produced by it. Similar to a black hole in that regard, a Dyson Sphere would only use solar cells, with the intent to fulfil the energy requirements of planet Earth.

By collecting sunlight yield through solar panels, such a gargantuan undertaking might be logistically possible. The idea is to construct one-kilometre (0.6 mi) solar panels to orbit around the Sun in hundreds of stable criss-cross patterns. However, another hypothesis is to build this technology using the planet Mercury as a resource to harvest the necessary materials to build the swarm.  


# Future Perspectives
By not having an impact on the environment, while helping push humankind to survive the challenges of energy consumption, this could be an interesting and clean solution to provide and deliver power to our homes and industries. It is, however, necessary to design a better solution to construct and install the solar panels while orbiting the Sun. It is of utmost importance for proper implementation, to not only have a look at the materials that could be harvested from the planet Mercury but also explore other alternatives.  

Despite the challenges, this energy production source provides a new horizon that would not affect our environment or unnecessarily occupy lands currently destined to become enormous power-plants. Such amounts of energy could be used to maintain desalination methods on Earth, increasing access to clean and abundant water in different contexts, such as agriculture or even to maintain more fragile communities.

description.shortText: A complex digital environment that can be accessed by people using avatars that react in real-time to the user's motion and expressions. A persistent representation of a virtual universe that incorporates elements of the real world.
description.longText:
A collective virtual shared space accessed by individuals through their avatars. It is thought to be the next generation of the internet. The objective of the metaverse is the use and interaction of sophisticated avatars that react in real-time to users' emotions, intentions, movements, and expressions. By migrating simple tasks that we already do online, such as video conferences and remote teamwork, we could decrease online fatigue by offering a spatial experience to the brain. From this perspective, it is possible to imagine entire factories existing entirely in virtual environments.

For companies and industries, the metaverse could play a crucial role by allowing them to launch products in the metaverse. In this scenario, interactions and public acceptance can be measured, and changes in the product design could be made instantly. This could decrease the resources and tests needed before the product is created physically. 

# Future Perspectives

The metaverse experience is expected to be highly immersive with complex and realistic simulated inputs almost impossible to distinguish from the physical world. It could house human minds, purely digital beings, and visiting humans alike. At some point, it could be possible for a user to be permanently connected and inhabit this digital universe at all times, leaving the living-breathing body attached to a life-support system or detaching forever from the physical body and uploading their mind. Uploading one's mind permanently into a metaverse could be a way to avoid death, or at least, to perpetuate life while the physical body is deceased. First adopters for this feature could include the severely disabled.

The possibility of permanently inhabiting such an environment comes with several risks. A metaverse would still largely depend on private companies and servers to function, which means that all experiences and lives appended to this system would need to follow the terms and conditions set by these companies. Besides being susceptible to any privacy breach, digital beings could become homeless or even die, for instance, if the company hosting their world in a metaverse decides to discontinue its services.

description.shortText: Lab-grown meat produced by placing animal cells, painlessly harvested from animal muscle tissue, in a culture dish to reproduce and develop into edible meat.
description.longText:
Artificial or lab-grown meat, grown from animal cells in a lab, which could replace meat for human consumption. The cells would be painlessly harvested from animal muscle tissue and placed in a culture dish, with nutrient inputs such as amino acids, carbohydrates, minerals, fats and vitamins, to reproduce and grow, yielding enough cultured meat for consumption. Scaffolding bones could give shape to the in-vitro meat, leaving it with an appearance similar to that of conventional meat from different animals. This process does not necessarily require genetic manipulation, but if used together, these technologies could create new product varieties that cover different nutritional requirements.

The production of meat from livestock occupies vast portions of land and uses a significant amount of the Earth's food resources. Traditional methods of meat production take a notable toll on the environment, whether by exacerbating the effects of greenhouse gases (methane, for example) or by inducing pain and distress in animals. Finding culturally acceptable alternatives to animal meat — especially as global demand for beef is estimated to double by 2050, and a large portion of the population traditionally and habitually consumes meat products — is a necessity for a growing society.


# Future Perspectives

While already in production, current in-vitro methods are still not quite energy efficient. But there is a possibility that as production methods mature and scale, by leveraging renewable energy sourcing and localizing production in specific regions (much like craft beer today), the environmental benefits of lab-grown meat could improve significantly.

Efficiency and the bio-conversion rate are crucial for the development of sustainable meat products. The low bio-conversion price in pigs and cows offers a wide margin for improvement. Deployment at scale has the potential for massive, worldwide impact, beginning with the reduction of CO2 emissions and soil degradation caused by the majority of methods of livestock production. It would also help stop the spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, pathogens, and diseases while reducing transportation needs for livestock or meat. However, in-vitro meat is not being developed as a possible way to eradicate hunger, instead, the aim is to provide an alternative source for eating and nutritional habits with an ethical perspective.

description.shortText: A device that uses electroencephalography (EEG) and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) that allows multi-person brain-to-brain communication. It could restore language abilities in patients with learning difficulties or those with disabilities brought on by having a stroke.
description.longText:
A communication device that transfers thoughts via noninvasive brain-signal detection through electrodes and electroencephalography (EEG). Based on the idea that connected brains working together are more effective than a single mind, this technology captures signals or thoughts from one brain and transfers them to others via communication protocols such as the internet. 

With an interconnected transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), the device uses a magnetic field to activate brain cells and deliver information between two or more parts. Despite being akin to a brain-machine device, this technology uses a computer as an intermediary to connect and communicate between two or more brains; without requiring any invasive procedures, with electrodes placed on the scalp of the subjects to link the brain. 

# Future Perspectives

In the health and medical sectors, this technology could restore language abilities in patients with learning difficulties or those with disabilities brought on by having a stroke. It would work by synchronizing the patient's brain with the brain's language regions of a healthy person. 

As Brain-to-Brain Communication devices gain traction in both popularity and advancements in research, the information gathered from brain communication could be transferred to a cloud-based BBi (brain-to-brain interface). A BBi could allow the direct transmission of information, thus eliminating the need for physical gestures or movement.

Ultimately, all human, animal, and machine knowledge could be summed up and instantly accessible in a Noosphere state. Identities, thus, would become diluted. All beings and machines would be joined at this frontier of all knowledge, working on expanding its limits.
